580	    {ambient path: reversible filtration};
581	\end{tikzpicture}}
582	\caption{Measurement as filtration. The ambient path splits, reads, and fuses without deleting the unread factor; the apparent collapse occurs only after projection to the classical record.}
583	\label{fig:measurement-filtration}
584	\end{figure}
585	
586	\section{The phenomena}
587	
588	We can now read the standard phenomena of quantum mechanics in the language of the carrier and the ladder. In each case, the familiar quantum description is the classical image of a corresponding feature of the ambient structure.
589	
590	\subsection{Superposition is the value both}
591	
592	A qubit in superposition is represented by the value $B$: truth and falsity are held together. This value is its own negation and is the one Belnap value that the classical slice cannot name.
593	
594	The Hadamard gate sends either classical value to $B$ and sends $B$ back to a definite value. At the constructive layer, the step from a definite input to the held value is the engage operation. On the many-coordinate register, the same idea appears as a state spread across weight sectors. The uniform sector states are its symmetric instances.
595	
596	\subsection{The Born rule is a forced quadratic projection}
597	
598	The probability of an outcome is determined by the overlap between the state and one of the two poles. The state space used here is not assumed separately. It is the single-coordinate orbit derived in Proposition~\ref{prop:sphere}, namely the sphere $\mathbb{CP}^1$.
599	
600	On that sphere, the true pole $T$ sits at $\theta=0$ and the false pole $F$ at $\theta=\pi$. The balanced held value $B$ lies on the equator. A pure state at polar angle $\theta$ is the ray $\ket{\psi}=\cos(\theta/2)\ket{T}+e^{i\varphi}\sin(\theta/2)\ket{F}$. The half-angle is forced by the spin one-half representation generated by the ladder.
601	
602	A truth measurement uses the pair of antipodal projectors, giving
603	\[
604	p_T(\theta) = \bigl|\langle T\mid\psi\rangle\bigr|^2 = \cos^2\tfrac{\theta}{2}
605	= \frac{1+\cos\theta}{2}, \qquad p_F = \sin^2\tfrac{\theta}{2}, \qquad p_T+p_F=1,
606	\]
607	Thus $p_T=1$ at the true pole, $p_T=0$ at the false pole, and $p_T=1/2$ at the balanced value on the equator. The equatorial case recovers the cardinality reading $p_T = \mathrm{info}(\psi\cap\{T\})/\mathrm{info}(\psi)$.
608	
609	The quadratic form is not added by hand. Busch's theorem~\cite{busch}, extending Gleason's theorem~\cite{gleason} to every dimension including two, states that an additive and non-contextual probability assignment on a positive-operator frame has the form $\mathrm{tr}(\rho E)$. For the truth projector on this sphere, that form is $\cos^2(\theta/2)$.
610	
611	On the full carrier, $p_T+p_F$ falls below one by exactly the informational-layer weight that the truth measurement does not reach.
612	
613	\subsection{The measurement frame is symmetric and informationally complete}
614	
615	A measurement frame need not consist only of the two poles. The natural frame used here is a symmetric informationally complete positive-operator measurement. In $d$ dimensions it contains $d^2$ unit vectors with equal pairwise overlap.
616	
617	For a qubit, $d=2$, so the frame has four vectors. They sit at the corners of a regular tetrahedron inscribed in the sphere. Any two distinct frame projectors $\Pi_i,\Pi_j$ satisfy
618	\[
619	\mathrm{tr}(\Pi_i\Pi_j) = \frac{1}{d+1} = \frac13,
620	\]
621	This is the equiangular condition. Because of it, the outcome probabilities determine the state completely, which is informational completeness. The frame does this with the fewest outcomes and with the most even possible spread, which is its symmetry.
622	
623	On this frame the probability rule can be written in its frame-native form, the urgleichung of Fuchs and Schack. If a reference measurement has probabilities $p_i$ and a following measurement has probabilities $q_j$, then
624	\[
625	q_j = \sum_i\Bigl[(d+1)\,p_i - \frac1d\Bigr]\,r(j\mid i),
626	\]
627	Here $r(j\mid i)$ is the conditional probability of the second frame given the first. The subtraction of $1/d$ and the factor $d+1$ are the same coreflector coefficients that appear in the OPI matrix of Section 7. In this reading, those coefficients describe how the frame projects a paraconsistent value onto classical outcomes. The four corners of the tetrahedron are the four Belnap values placed symmetrically, and the equiangular overlap $1/(d+1)$ is the residue left by the held value in every direction at once.
628	
629	\subsection{Interference is a winding on a lattice of turns}
630	
631	The phase $e^{i\varphi}$ that produces interference is a winding, a rational number of turns, fixed at the commit operation. The native windings sit on a lattice of tenths.
632	
633	\begin{proposition}[The gate lattice]\label{prop:tenths}
634	$\tfrac12=\tfrac{5}{10}$ lies on the tenths lattice, and $\tfrac18$ and $\tfrac14$ do not: $\tfrac18=\tfrac{p}{10}$ forces $p=5/4$ and $\tfrac14=\tfrac{p}{10}$ forces $p=5/2$, neither an integer.
635	\end{proposition}
636	
637	Interference between two paths is the difference of their windings. A half turn lies on the native tenths lattice, while the quarter turn of $S$ and the eighth turn of $T$ do not. This lattice statement concerns the phases carried by the generators and does not by itself rule out exact realization by braid words, since products of noncommuting generators can have spectra not present among the generators themselves. In the Fibonacci representation the stronger word-level obstruction is arithmetic: the projective invariant $\operatorname{tr}^2/\det$ excludes $T$, while the determinant lattice supplies the additional obstruction needed to exclude $S$~\cite{gateobstruction}. By contrast, $Z$ and every relative tenth phase are realized exactly. Thus approximation of $S$ and $T$ is not an engineering accommodation to a finite gate dictionary. Their exact targets are absent from the braid image, so compilation is an arithmetic necessity. The fringe visibility is the information-order distance between the two path states.
638	
639	\subsection{Entanglement is a persistent contradiction}
640	
641	Two systems are entangled when they share a held value $B$ that persists as either side is read. The value survives refutation, is fixed by negation, and does not trivialize the logic. The resulting correlation therefore exceeds what can be represented by independent definite values.
642	
643	The correlator is not supplied as an additional assumption. It is derived from the shared held value on the product of two single-coordinate registers.
644	
645	The shared relation pairs $T$ on one part with $F$ on the other, but neither alternative is fixed on its own. The relation must also survive a common change of reading frame. That persistence is expressed by requiring the state's ray to remain invariant under the diagonal action $U\otimes U$ of Proposition~\ref{prop:sphere}.
646	
647	The product of two spin one-half representations decomposes as $\tfrac12\otimes\tfrac12 = 0\oplus 1$. Within that product, the invariant ray is unique. It is the spin-zero state
648	\[
649	\ket{B_2} = \frac{\ket{TF}-\ket{FT}}{\sqrt2},
650	\]
651	Neither part is one-sided, and the joint value does not factor into independent values for the two parts. A common rotation changes neither the relation nor its readings. This state is the shared held value in the linear envelope.
652	
653	\begin{proposition}[The correlator is a cosine]\label{prop:corr}
654	A Boolean reading of part one in direction $\mathbf{a}$ is the observable $A_{\mathbf a}=\mathbf{a}\cdot\boldsymbol{\sigma}$, and likewise $B_{\mathbf b}=\mathbf{b}\cdot\boldsymbol{\sigma}$ on part two. On the shared held value, $\langle B_2\mid \sigma_i\otimes\sigma_j\mid B_2\rangle = -\delta_{ij}$, so $E(\mathbf{a},\mathbf{b}) = \langle B_2\mid A_{\mathbf a}\otimes B_{\mathbf b}\mid B_2\rangle = -\,\mathbf{a}\cdot\mathbf{b}$, and for coplanar frames separated by $\Delta$, $E(\Delta) = -\cos\Delta$.
655	\end{proposition}
656	
657	The natural invariant gives $-\cos\Delta$, since the held relation pairs $T$ against $F$. Reversing the Boolean label on one part, which is what pairing $T$ with $F$ invites, flips the sign to $E(\Delta)=+\cos\Delta$, the convention used elsewhere. Either way the cosine is the classical two-pole reading of the spin one-half geometry the ladder generates.
658	
659	\begin{corollary}[The Tsirelson bound]\label{cor:tsirelson}
660	For four readings $A,A',B,B'$ built from unit vectors, each squares to the identity. The CHSH operator $\mathcal{C} = A\otimes(B+B') + A'\otimes(B-B')$ satisfies, up to the sign fixed by the CHSH convention, $\mathcal{C}^2 = 4I - [A,A']\otimes[B,B']$. Each dichotomic reading has operator norm one, so $\lVert[A,A']\rVert\leq 2$ and $\lVert[B,B']\rVert\leq 2$, giving $\lVert\mathcal{C}\rVert^2\leq 8$ and $\lVert\mathcal{C}\rVert\leq 2\sqrt2$. At relative tilts of $\pi/4$ the bound is attained~\cite{tsirelson,bell,chsh}.
661	\end{corollary}
662	
663	The bound $2\sqrt2$ follows from the same spin one-half representation, with no quantum correlator supplied in advance. The shared held value supplies $\cos(\pi/4)$ per setting, and the four readings reach $4\cdot\tfrac{\sqrt2}{2}=2\sqrt2$.
664	
665	\begin{figure}[t]
666	\centering
667	\resizebox{\linewidth}{!}{%
668	\begin{tikzpicture}[vox, node distance=26mm]
669	  \node[voxbox] (tf) {$|TF\rangle$};
670	  \node[voxbox, below=7mm of tf] (ft) {$|FT\rangle$};
671	
672	  \node[voxbox, right=15mm of tf, yshift=-6mm, minimum width=30mm] (held)
673	    {shared held relation\\$B_{12}$};
674	  \node[voxbox, right=of held, minimum width=40mm] (singlet)
675	    {$|B_2\rangle=\dfrac{|TF\rangle-|FT\rangle}{\sqrt2}$\\$(U\otimes U)|B_2\rangle\sim|B_2\rangle$};
676	  \node[voxbox, right=of singlet, minimum width=30mm] (corr)
677	    {$E(\mathbf a,\mathbf b)$\\$=-\mathbf a\!\cdot\!\mathbf b$};
678	  \node[voxbox, right=of corr, minimum width=26mm] (chsh)
679	    {$\|\mathcal C\|$\\$\le 2\sqrt2$};
680	
681	  \draw[voxarrow] (tf) -- (held);
682	  \draw[voxarrow] (ft) -- (held);
683	  \draw[voxarrow] (held) -- node[voxlabel,above] {linearize} (singlet);
684	  \draw[voxarrow] (singlet) -- node[voxlabel,above] {Boolean frames} (corr);
685	  \draw[voxarrow] (corr) -- node[voxlabel,above] {CHSH} (chsh);
686	
687	  \node[below=5mm of corr, font=\scriptsize]
688	    {coplanar: $E(\Delta)=-\cos\Delta$; flip one output convention $\Rightarrow +\cos\Delta$};
689	\end{tikzpicture}}
690	\caption{The persistent two-part held relation linearizes to the unique rotation-invariant spin-zero ray. Classical frame readings then produce the cosine correlation and the Tsirelson bound.}
691	\label{fig:held-correlation}
692	\end{figure}
693	
694	\subsection{Uncertainty and error correction are the composition rule}
695	
696	A value produced inside a region and cleared by a reversal is lost unless an enclosing region banks a copy. Two quantities opened in regions that cannot nest cannot both be banked, so one is exposed when the other closes.
697	
698	\begin{lemma}[Banking survives a reversal]\label{lem:bank}
699	A mark deposited, then held by a frame open across a reversal, then fused, is present after the fuse; a mark deposited with no enclosing frame open, then cleared by a reversal, is lost and no later fuse restores it.
700	\end{lemma}
701	
702	\begin{proof}
703	A deposit into an open frame is banked there; the reversal clears the register but not the open frame, and the fuse folds the frame's copy back by mark-wise union, restoring it. A deposit with no open frame is in the register only; the reversal removes it and no frame holds a copy.
704	\end{proof}
705	
706	Uncertainty is the exposed case. Position and momentum are two counts whose holding regions cannot both enclose the other's computing region. One of the two is therefore always exposed. This gives $\Delta x\,\Delta p \geq c\hbar$, where $c$ is a positive order-one constant fixed by the rule. The value of $c$ is determined by the composition rule itself; it is the coefficient that appears when the two exposures are minimized subject to the nesting constraint. In the standard units, this coefficient is $1/2$, but its precise value is fixed by the geometry of the register rather than by an independent assumption.
707	
708	Error correction is the deliberately banked case. An outer frame stays open while a reversal clears the working register, so the syndrome remains banked. The outer fuse then restores it, allowing the error to be corrected without disturbing the encoded value. The composition rule is the same in both cases. Arranged so that the value is banked, it is error correction. Forced by geometry to leave a value exposed, it is uncertainty.
709	
710	\subsection{Decoherence empties the informational layer}
711	
712	Decoherence removes the informational layer $\{t,f\}$ from the system by carrying it into the environment. To see the correspondence, write the one-qubit density matrix in the truth basis,
713	\[
714	\rho = \begin{pmatrix} p_T & c \\ \bar c & p_F \end{pmatrix},
715	\]
716	The diagonal entries $p_T,p_F$ are the populations. They are the truth and falsity support read by the sector projection. The off-diagonal term $c$ is the coherence, here identified with the informational-layer marks $t,f$ that carry weight without settling truth.
717	
718	Coupling the system to an environment attenuates the off-diagonal term, $c\to c\,e^{-t/\tau}$, while leaving the diagonal unchanged. As $c\to0$, the state approaches its constructive shadow $\mathrm{diag}(p_T,p_F)$, which lies in the Belnap slice with an empty informational layer. At the balanced point, the held value $B$ has its entire content in the off-diagonal term, so it decays to the undetermined mixture.
719	
720	Decoherence is therefore the emptying of $\{t,f\}$. The informational layer drains into the environment while the constructive layer remains. A large system read coarsely thus presents its constructive shadow rather than its held value, although that shadow is never the ground.
721	
722	\subsection{Complementarity is the two swaps that factor negation}
723	
724	Negation factors into two commuting swaps on disjoint pairs of marks: the truth swap exchanging $T$ with $F$, and the information swap exchanging $t$ with $f$. A measurement in the truth basis reads the pair moved by the truth swap; a measurement in the conjugate basis reads the pair moved by the information swap. Because the two swaps act on disjoint marks, fixing the value of one pair leaves the other pair free, so sharpening the constructive layer says nothing about the informational layer the conjugate measurement reads. Complementary observables are the two factors of the single negation, and their mutual unsharpness is the disjointness of the marks they move.
725	
726	\subsection{The quantum eraser is the fuse}
727	
728	Marking a path is a split that banks the which-path value in an open frame. While the frame remains open, the banked mark distinguishes the paths, so interference is absent.
729	
730	Erasing the mark is the fuse that closes that frame. Because split banked the arms it opened, fuse recovers the held value and therefore recovers the interference. This is the banked invertibility of Section 5: the value is recovered from its image. Nothing is literally erased.
731	
732	No restoration reaches into an earlier time. The round trip returns the state. Closing the frame simply returns the value previously opened by split, and the fringes that reappear were always available to the closed description. The quantum eraser is the reversibility of split and fuse read experimentally.
733	
734	\subsection{Contextuality is the frame-dependence of the held value}
735	
736	\begin{proposition}[No global classical assignment]\label{prop:context}
737	There is no assignment of a single classical value to a proposition in the state $B$ that agrees with every frame, since the truth frame filters $B$ to $T$ and the falsity frame filters $B$ to $F$, and $T\neq F$.
738	\end{proposition}
739	
740	The impossibility is the inexpressibility of $B$ seen from the frames: the held value has no classical name, so its reading is whatever the frame filters it to, and different frames filter it differently. The value is one; its shadows are many, one per frame.
741	
742	\subsection{Composite systems}
743	
744	Two systems combine by taking the product of their carriers. An entangled state is a value of that product that cannot be factored into one value for each part.
745	
746	A shared held relation has one part true and the other false, with the two alternatives held together as $B$ rather than settled separately. No separable pair of one-sided values can express that relation, because any such pair selects one alternative while the shared value holds both. The four Bell states are the four shared held values of the two-part product under the two swaps.
747	
748	Reading one part is a split of the shared value. Because $B$ persists, that split does not destroy the shared value, and the correlation therefore survives however the two parts are read. Under products, the number of middle values multiplies. A many-part composite consequently grows quickly, which is the carrier's form of the exponential growth of state space with the number of parts.
749	
750	\section{A century of experiments in FDE terms}
751	
752	The experiments that built quantum mechanics are, read in order, a century of readings of the held value through classical frames. Each is stated here in the carrier's terms, the apparatus the frame and the result the frame's filtering of a value that was never one-sided.
753	
754	\subsection{The double slit}
755	
756	A particle sent through two slits lands in a fringe pattern that no assignment of a definite slit reproduces. In carrier terms the particle at the slits is the held value $B$, through-left and through-right held together, and the screen reads a truth measurement whose outcome probability is $\cos^2(\theta/2)$ in the winding difference of the two paths. Closing one slit fixes a one-sided value, $T$ or $F$, and the fringes go, since a fixed value has no held part to interfere. The pattern is the Born reading of Section 6.2 with the phase the path-winding of Section 6.3. Davisson and Germer's electron diffraction and the later single-electron buildup are the same reading with the particles arriving one at a time: each electron is the held value, and the pattern accretes because every one is filtered by the same frame.
757	
758	\subsection{Stern-Gerlach}
759	
760	A beam of atoms through an inhomogeneous field splits into two, not a continuum. The spin component along the field is a constructive-layer mark with two one-sided values, and the apparatus is the split opening the held value into its two arms $T$ and $F$. Sending one output through a second magnet at an angle is a fresh split on a fresh frame, and the reappearance of both outputs is the persistence of the held value under a change of frame, contextuality of Section 6.9 made mechanical.
761	
762	\subsection{The photoelectric and Compton effects}
763	
764	Light ejects electrons only above a frequency threshold, and scatters off them with a wavelength shift. Both fix the winding quantum of Section 6.3: energy is deposited in whole turns, the commit fixing one winding at a time, so below the threshold no single commit carries enough and above it each commit ejects one electron. Compton scattering is the same commit read as a two-body exchange, the winding shifted by the recoil. These are the irreversible-commit experiments, the one operation with no adjoint made visible.
765	
766	\subsection{EPR and the Bell tests}
767	
768	Einstein, Podolsky and Rosen argued that perfect correlation at a distance forces predetermined values. Bell's inequality and its tests answer that no assignment of predetermined one-sided values reproduces the correlations. In carrier terms the shared state is the persistent held value $B$ of Section 6.4, and the correlation reaches the Tsirelson bound $2\sqrt2$ because $B$ supplies $\cos(\pi/4)$ per setting where any one-sided assignment supplies at most the classical $2$. Aspect's experiments, and the loophole-free tests of 2015 that closed the locality and detection gaps at once, measure the held value surviving separation: reading one wing is a split that does not destroy the shared value, so the other wing's reading stays correlated however the settings are chosen.
769	
770	\subsection{Wheeler's delayed choice and the quantum eraser}
771	
772	Whether to insert the recombining element is chosen after the particle is past the slits, and the particle still shows fringes or not according to the late choice. This is the reversibility of the split and fuse of Section 6.7: the held value is carried intact until a frame is closed, and closing it late is the same fuse as closing it early, with no reach back in time because the round trip returns the banked value. Scully and Drühl's eraser and Kim's realization bank the which-path mark and then erase it, recovering the interference, the fuse restoring the value the split opened.
773	
774	\subsection{Single-photon interference and Hong-Ou-Mandel}
775	
776	Grangier's experiment shows a single photon interfering with itself while never being detected at two detectors at once: the held value spreads across both arms yet the commit deposits it in one place. Hong-Ou-Mandel's two-photon coincidence dip is the held value of a two-part system, the two photons entering the balanced held state under which the coincidence outcome cancels, the composite-system reading of Section 6.10 at two parts.
777	
778	\subsection{Macroscopic held values}
779	
780	Superconductivity, the Josephson effect, the SQUID, and Bose-Einstein condensation are held values sustained across a macroscopic number of parts. The condensate is the uniform sector state of Section 5.1 at large $m$, every part in the same held value, and the Josephson current is the winding difference of Section 6.3 read across a junction. The Leggett-Garg tests, which bound correlations across times rather than places, measure the held value persisting in one system through successive readings, the temporal form of the Bell argument, and their violation is the same persistence of $B$ under a change of frame.
781

870	\section{A worked realization: Optimal Polynomial Intersection}
871	
872	We now turn to a complete worked instance. Here the classical image of a paraconsistent object can be computed directly, and its convergence toward the paraconsistent original can be measured. The object is the tridiagonal ladder of Section 5. The setting is a hard optimization problem whose quantum algorithm is governed by that ladder.
873	
874	\subsection{The problem}
875	
876	\begin{definition}[Optimal Polynomial Intersection]
877	Fix a prime $p$ and an integer $n<p-1$. Let $F_1,\dots,F_{p-1}$ be subsets of $\mathbb{F}_p$. An instance asks for a polynomial $Q\in\mathbb{F}_p[y]$ of degree at most $n-1$ maximizing
878	$f_{\mathrm{OPI}}(Q) = |\{y\in\{1,\dots,p-1\}: Q(y)\in F_y\}|$. It is balanced when every $|F_i|=r=\lfloor p/2\rfloor$.
879	\end{definition}
880	
881	Optimal Polynomial Intersection can be read as a maximum-satisfaction problem over $\mathbb{F}_p$. The bounded-degree polynomials form the codewords of a linear code, so maximizing the intersection count is the same as maximizing the number of constraints satisfied by a codeword.
882	
883	There are $m=p-1$ constraints. Their matrix is Vandermonde, and the dual code $C^{\perp}$ is Reed-Solomon. Berlekamp-Massey performs syndrome decoding of $C^{\perp}$ out to $\ell=\lfloor(n+1)/2\rfloor$ errors in polynomial time. The problem is a useful hard target because that decoder alone does not reach the optimum. The quantum algorithm improves on the classical baseline by concentrating amplitude on low-weight error patterns.
884	
885	\subsection{The coding structure}
886	
887	The satisfaction problem can be converted directly into a decoding problem. For each constraint $y$, choose a representative of $F_y$ and record a mismatch whenever $Q(y)\notin F_y$. The resulting mismatch vector has one bit per constraint. A polynomial's satisfaction count is therefore $m$ minus the Hamming weight of that vector.
888	
889	The evaluations of all degree-$<n$ polynomials at the $m=p-1$ nonzero points form a Reed-Solomon code $C$ with a Vandermonde encoding. Its dual $C^{\perp}$ is also a Reed-Solomon code, with dimension $m-n$ and minimum distance $d^{\perp}=n+1$. Maximizing satisfaction is thus the same as finding the codeword of $C$ nearest the target in Hamming distance.
890	
891	Berlekamp-Massey decodes the target syndrome with respect to $C^{\perp}$. It forms the syndrome polynomial, finds the shortest linear recurrence that generates it, and reads the mismatch positions from the roots of the error locator. It corrects up to $\ell=\lfloor(n+1)/2\rfloor = \lfloor d^{\perp}/2\rfloor$ errors in time cubic in the block length. This is the classical polynomial-time floor used here.
892	
893	The same decoding radius $\ell$ bounds the dimension of the ladder matrix. The quantum state is supported on error patterns of weight at most $\ell$, with one weight sector per rung. The condition $2\ell+1<d^{\perp}$ in Lemma~\ref{lem:jordan} is exactly the unique-decodability condition. In that regime, each syndrome names one error pattern, and the ladder transfers amplitude only between adjacent weights.
894	
895	\subsection{The algorithm and its matrix}
896	
897	Decoded Quantum Interferometry~\cite{dqi} prepares a state whose amplitude is concentrated on low-weight error patterns and reads the decoded polynomial. Its expected performance is the largest eigenvalue of a finite matrix.
898	
899	\begin{lemma}[The expected satisfied count]\label{lem:jordan}
900	Let $\langle s^{(m,\ell)}\rangle$ be the expected number of satisfied constraints after state preparation at decoding radius $\ell$. If $2\ell+1<d^{\perp}$, the minimum distance of $C^{\perp}$, then
901	\[
902	\langle s^{(m,\ell)}\rangle = \frac{mr}{p} + \frac{\sqrt{r(p-r)}}{p}\,
903	\lambda_{\max}\bigl(A^{(m,\ell,d)}\bigr),
904	\]
905	with $A^{(m,\ell,d)}$ the $(\ell+1)\times(\ell+1)$ real symmetric tridiagonal matrix, diagonal $kd$ for $k=0,\dots,\ell$, off-diagonal $a_{k+1}=\sqrt{(k+1)(m-k)}$, and $d=(p-2r)/\sqrt{r(p-r)}$.
906	\end{lemma}
907	
908	This is the result of Jordan and colleagues~\cite{dqi}. Its matrix is exactly the filtration ladder from Theorem~\ref{thm:matrix}. The diagonal term $kd$ is the evaluate operator $D$, with $d=(p-2r)/\sqrt{r(p-r)}$. The off-diagonal term $\sqrt{(k+1)(m-k)}$ is the raising and lowering coefficient from Theorem~\ref{thm:ladder}. The expected satisfied count is therefore a constant plus the largest eigenvalue of the ladder, multiplied by the stated scale factor.
909	
910	\begin{proposition}[The asymptotic limit]\label{prop:asymp}
911	Taking $\ell\to n/2$ and $m\to p$ gives
912	\[
913	\frac{\langle s\rangle_{\mathrm{DQI}}}{p} = \frac12 + \sqrt{\frac{n}{2p}\Bigl(1-\frac{n}{2p}\Bigr)},
914	\]
915	with no eigenvalue problem to solve.
916	\end{proposition}
917	
918	The finite expression retains the full $(\ell+1)$-dimensional operator. It contains a specific finite $m$, a matrix, and an eigenvector. The asymptotic expression is what remains after that structure is smoothed into a single scalar as $m\to p$.
919	
920	At every finite $m$, the finite form therefore carries strictly more structure than the scalar limit. Moving from the finite operator to the asymptotic scalar is a coarsening, in the same direction as the coreflector of Theorem~\ref{thm:two}.

The same diagnosis appeared at every rotation of the program's orbit and at the same structural location: reversal cleared the count before its holding frame existed.

934	\begin{proposition}[The $m$-fold lift]\label{prop:lift}
935	Let $\iota$ and the coreflector $c$ act coordinatewise on $\{N,T,F,B\}^m$, ordered coordinatewise in the truth order. 959	\item set $v$ to a random unit vector of length $\ell+1$;
960	\item repeat until the Rayleigh quotient settles: $w \leftarrow (A+\sigma I)v$, then $v\leftarrow w/\|w\|$;
961	\item return $\lambda_{\max}(A) = v^{\top}(A+\sigma I)v - \sigma$.
962	\end{enumerate}

1028	\section{The arrow of time and the cost of measurement}
1029	
1030	The reversibility of the split and fuse has a thermodynamic reading. Landauer's principle sets a floor on the energy any logically irreversible step must dissipate: erasing one bit of information costs at least $k_B T\ln 2$, because erasure maps two states to one and the lost distinction leaves as heat. Bennett showed that a computation built entirely from reversible steps owes no such cost, since nothing is erased, and Fredkin and Toffoli gave a universal reversible logic that carries this out in principle at no dissipation floor.
1031	
1032	Measurement as filtration is reversible. The split opens a value into tensor factors, a reading selects one, and the fuse restores the whole, so no factor is erased and the ambient pays no Landauer cost for a measurement. What a collapse account records as the destruction of the unread outcomes is, in the ladder, the classical image keeping one rung and dropping the others, and it is only that image, the coreflector's reading, where an erasure and its cost appear. The dissipation of a real measuring device is the cost of maintaining the classical record, not of the filtration itself.
1033	
1034	The arrow of time is the accumulation of fixes. The one operation with no adjoint is the commit, and every commit records a value irreversibly into the winding, a step the fuse cannot undo. A computation of only splits and fuses runs equally well in either direction; a computation that fixes has a direction, the direction in which the fixes accumulate. The thermodynamic arrow, the growth of the classical record, is the count of commits, and the reversibility of the rest is why the ambient itself carries no arrow while its classical image does.
1035	
1036	Approaching the Landauer floor in practice requires the whole computational stack to be aligned. The computation itself must be reversible, with its operations closing so that every step is invertible and its result recoverable. The operating system must also stop erasing, reclaiming transient state by scope teardown rather than abandoning it. The hardware must then implement reversible gates instead of the dissipative gates used by ordinary processors.
1037	
1038	When all three levels are in syzygy, the Landauer floor is approached. If any one level erases, the floor is not reached, and the remaining gap is the erasure forced by that stage. A reversible computation run on an ordinary irreversible stack therefore shows a positive marginal draw above idle. In this account, that draw is the tax of the erasing stack rather than a cost owed by the reversible computation itself.
1039	
1040	\section{Summary of results}
1041	
1042	The carrier is the sixteen-value trilattice with three orders, each of which is a lattice (Proposition~\ref{prop:orders}). Negation is an involution fixing exactly the two nonclassical values $N$ and $B$ (Proposition~\ref{prop:neg}). The consequence relation neither explodes on a contradiction nor validates excluded middle (Theorem~\ref{thm:entail}).
1043	
1044	The Boolean core is reached by two distinct truth-order adjunctions, ex falso and ex quodlibet (Theorem~\ref{thm:two}), and neither is an information-order adjunction (Proposition~\ref{prop:noinfo}). The collapse is exactly lossy because the held value is inexpressible in either image (Theorem~\ref{thm:lossy}).
1045	
1046	On an $m$-fold register, split and fuse are the raising and lowering operators on the weight sectors, with $S_+\ket{k}=\sqrt{(k+1)(m-k)}\ket{k+1}$ and its adjoint (Theorem~\ref{thm:ladder}). Evaluate is the diagonal $D\ket{k}=kd\ket{k}$ (Proposition~\ref{prop:diag}). Together they form the symmetric tridiagonal filtration matrix (Theorem~\ref{thm:matrix}), and measurement is filtration through this ladder rather than collapse.
1047	
1048	The register is the canonical linearization $\ell^2(\{T,F\}^m)$ of the carrier (Definition~\ref{def:lin}). Its ladder generates the su(2) action of spin $m/2$ (Proposition~\ref{prop:su2}), and the single-coordinate orbit is the qubit sphere $\mathbb{CP}^1$ (Proposition~\ref{prop:sphere}). The Hilbert-space geometry is therefore derived from the ladder rather than assumed.
1049	
1050	On that derived sphere, the Born rule is the forced quadratic $\cos^2(\theta/2)$ (Section 6.2, via Busch~\cite{busch}). The native gate windings sit on a lattice of tenths (Proposition~\ref{prop:tenths}), and in the Fibonacci representation the corresponding word-level arithmetic obstruction separates exact native phases from gates that can only be approached: the tenth phases are exact, while $S$ and $T$ remain outside the braid image at every word length~\cite{gateobstruction}. The shared held value is the unique frame-invariant ray, giving the correlator $E(\Delta)=-\cos\Delta$ (Proposition~\ref{prop:corr}) and the Tsirelson bound $2\sqrt2$ (Corollary~\ref{cor:tsirelson}). Uncertainty and error correction are two readings of the same composition rule (Lemma~\ref{lem:bank}), and there is no global classical assignment to a held value (Proposition~\ref{prop:context}).
1051	
1052	The tower of gauge ranks grows the number of values strictly with rank. Its restriction map is a non-injective left inverse of the embedding (Theorem~\ref{thm:grow}), which is the same structural form as the classical coreflector.
1053	
1054	Finally, the DQI matrix for Optimal Polynomial Intersection is the coreflector image of a paraconsistent ladder, entry for entry (Theorem~\ref{thm:main}). Across four scales, the finite operator-valued value settles monotonically onto the scalar limit in the direction of the coreflector (Section 9).
1055	
1056	\section{Discussion}
1057	
1058	One object has been traced through three descriptions. As a paraconsistent object it is the split, fuse, and evaluate ladder on the $m$-fold register, an operator-valued object that closes under the composition rule. As a classical image it is the tridiagonal matrix $A^{(m,\ell,d)}$, the coreflector's reading of that ladder on the Boolean register, governing the quantum algorithm's expectation value. As an asymptotic limit it is the single scalar of Proposition~\ref{prop:asymp}, what the matrix becomes when its structure is smoothed as $m\to p$. The three are one object at three levels of coarsening, each arrow proved or measured: the coreflector from the paraconsistent to the classical, the limit from the finite matrix to the scalar.
1059	
1060	\begin{figure}[t]
1061	\centering
1062	\resizebox{\linewidth}{!}{%
1063	\begin{tikzpicture}[vox, node distance=24mm]

1072	      & \ddots & \ddots & \ddots \\
1073	      & & \sqrt{\ell(m-\ell+1)} & \ell d
1074	    \end{bmatrix}$};
1075	
1076	  \node[voxbox, right=of matrix, minimum width=31mm] (eig)
1077	    {finite reading\\$\lambda_{\max}(A)$};
1078

1085

1091	\label{fig:dqi-coarsening}
1092	\end{figure}
1093	
1094	This is the program's thesis in one worked case. The quantum algorithm is the classical image of a paraconsistent object, and the image is strictly poorer than the original in a way that can be measured. The apparent quantum behavior, the concentration of amplitude that gives the algorithm its advantage, is produced by the classical evaluation of the paraconsistent ladder, with no additional physical ingredient. The relationship is directional: the matrix is derived from the ladder, the scalar from the matrix, and neither lower description asserts anything back up.
1095	
1096	The tensor filtration of Section 5 is the mechanism throughout. The split and fuse are the raising and lowering operators, the evaluate is the diagonal, and the whole filtration is the tridiagonal ladder they build. Measurement is filtration through that ladder, selecting a rung while the ladder persists, and the reversibility of the split and fuse is why there is no collapse and no thermodynamic floor forcing dissipation. The worked instance shows the same ladder governing a real algorithm, its largest eigenvalue the algorithm's performance, its finite-to-asymptotic collapse the coreflector's coarsening measured across four scales.
1097	
1098	Look around you. The definite classical world of one-sided facts is the special configuration that does not occur; a genuinely classical object would not hold together, have color, or resist collapse, because its stability is the exclusion of paired occupations, the value $B$ across every atom. What occurs is the ambient. The classical image is what a retraction reads off it and the asymptotic scalar is what a limit reads off the image, and at no level is the classical description the ground. It is a coarsening, the coarsening is exactly lossy, and the loss is the state that carries contradiction.
1099	
1100	The ambient holds both, and in holding both, it holds everything together. The logic is prior to the physics. The physics is the image of the logic under a retraction that cannot name the middle. And the middle, the held value, is the only thing that makes the world the strange, coherent, contradictory, persistent place that it is.

100:This paper carries two things the setting of the direction did not. First, it develops the mechanics of the operation at the center of the account. Measurement is not a collapse; it is a tensor filtration, a reversible selection of one factor of a tensor while the others remain. We make the filtration concrete as an explicit ladder of operators on the weight sectors of a many-coordinate register: a raising operator that opens a value into more support, its adjoint the lowering operator, and a diagonal operator that reads support already present. The three are the split, the fuse, and the evaluate operations of the grammar, realized as linear operators, and together they are a tridiagonal matrix whose structure is the whole content of the filtration.
238:Three operations move the structural verdict of a program: the split opens a fork, the fuse closes one, and the close anchors the program. On a single value the split and fuse compose to the identity, since the split copies and the fuse joins and the join is idempotent; realized as ladder operators on a many-coordinate register they compose instead to a positive invertible diagonal, reversible by invertibility, and Section 5 carries both levels.
260:Start with the undetermined value $N=\{\}$. The split opens $N$ into the pair $(N,N)$. Evaluate-true deposits $T$ on the first arm, producing $\{T\}$. Evaluate-false deposits $F$ on the second, producing $\{F\}$. The fuse then recombines the two arms by mark-wise union: $\{T\}\cup\{F\}=\{T,F\}=B$. The program therefore takes an undetermined input to the overdetermined value that holds both. This is the value called superposition in Section 6.1.
268:The program cannot be run backward past the fix because the commit is the one operation with no adjoint. Its verdict is therefore a definite classical $T$ with no held part. This makes the contrast with the first example exact. The first program uses split and fuse, is reversible, and lands on the held value. The second uses a fix, is irreversible, and lands on a pole. Classical values are the outputs of programs that fix. The held value is the output of programs that only split and fuse.
360:The complex coefficient does not introduce a new object. The grammar already carries a winding, and a winding leaves the constructive support of a configuration unchanged. In the linear envelope, that unchanged support is represented by multiplication by a scalar of unit modulus. For a discrete winding group the scalar is a root of unity in the corresponding cyclotomic field. That field carries exact arithmetic content rather than merely another notation for phase: in the Fibonacci representation it constrains the spectrum of every braid word even though the braid image is dense, so a phase may be arbitrarily approximable while remaining absent from the exact image~\cite{gateobstruction}. Its continuous completion is the phase $e^{i\varphi}$.
928:An automatically designed thirty-three-operation program for this structure did not close. The closure audit located the failure precisely. A count was being cleared before the frame that should have banked it had opened. In the language of Lemma~\ref{lem:bank}, the result was exposed instead of banked. The same diagnosis appeared at every rotation of the program's orbit and at the same structural location: reversal cleared the count before its holding frame existed.
1016:The symmetric informationally complete frame of Section 6.3 is the maximally even form of such a measure. In this reading, the grammar's twelve operations are its outcomes, meaning the distinctions that a frame can draw.
1020:Under this interpretation, the hard open problems addressed by the program occupy different cells of one operator-valued-measure taxonomy. At each address, a paraconsistent object is read through a frame.
1026:The program's claim is therefore that the hard problems are one object appearing at many addresses, with the worked instance providing the first complete reading.

lines: The world plainly looks classical at ordinary scale, one might insist. But it does not. A rock is held together by the exclusion of paired occupations across every orbital, the held value $B$ enforced everywhere at once; its solidity, its color, its refusal to collapse are that exclusion, not any one-sided fact. A genuinely classical object, one whose every proposition were settled true or false with no held part, would have no exclusion to give it volume and would not cohere. The classical description is a coarsening laid over the ambient that declines to read the structure holding the object up. What looks classical is the constructive shadow, the informational layer read as empty, and the shadow is never the ground.

We make the filtration concrete as an explicit ladder of operators on the weight sectors of a many-coordinate register: a raising operator that opens a value into more support, its adjoint the lowering operator, and a diagonal operator that reads support already present. The three are the split, the fuse, and the evaluate operations of the grammar, realized as linear operators, and together they are a tridiagonal matrix whose structure is the whole content of the filtration.

Second, it folds in a complete worked instance in which the classical image of a paraconsistent object is computed and measured. The problem is Optimal Polynomial Intersection, a hard combinatorial optimization over a finite field. Its state-of-the-art quantum algorithm, Decoded Quantum Interferometry, has an expected performance governed by the largest eigenvalue of a finite tridiagonal matrix. We show that this matrix is the ladder of the split, fuse, and evaluate operations on the register, and that the algorithm's expectation value is that ladder read through the coreflector. We compute the finite operator-valued value and its asymptotic scalar limit and measure the one collapsing onto the other across four scales, the richer description giving way to the poorer in the direction the coreflector moves.

lines: The phase $e^{i\varphi}$ that produces interference is a winding, a rational number of turns, fixed at the commit operation. The native windings sit on a lattice of tenths.
\begin{proposition}[The gate lattice]\label{prop:tenths}
-$\tfrac12=\tfrac{5}{10}$ lies on the tenths lattice, and $\tfrac18$ and $\tfrac14$ do not: $\tfrac18=\tfrac{p}{10}$ forces $p=5/4$ and $\tfrac14=\tfrac{p}{10}$ forces $p=5/2$, neither an integer.
+$\tfrac12$ lies on the tenths lattice $\{p/10 : p\in\mathbb Z\}$, and $\tfrac18$ and $\tfrac14$ do not.
\end{proposition}
+\begin{proof}
+$\tfrac12=\tfrac{5}{10}$, so $p=5$ works. For $\tfrac18=\tfrac{p}{10}$, $p=5/4$, not an integer; for $\tfrac14=\tfrac{p}{10}$, $p=5/2$, not an integer. Neither turn lies on the lattice.
+\end{proof}

Interference between two paths is the difference of their windings. A half turn lies on the native tenths lattice, while the quarter turn of $S$ and the eighth turn of $T$ do not. This lattice statement concerns the phases carried by the generators and does not by itself rule out exact realization by braid words, since products of noncommuting generators can have spectra not present among the generators themselves. In the Fibonacci representation the stronger word-level obstruction is arithmetic: the projective invariant $\operatorname{tr}^2/\det$ excludes $T$, while the determinant lattice supplies the additional obstruction needed to exclude $S$~\cite{gateobstruction}. By contrast, $Z$ and every relative tenth phase are realized exactly. Thus approximation of $S$ and $T$ is not an engineering accommodation to a finite gate dictionary. Their exact targets are absent from the braid image, so compilation is an arithmetic necessity. The fringe visibility is the information-order distance between the two path states.

\begin{proposition}[The correlator is a cosine]\label{prop:corr}

-A Boolean reading of part one in direction $\mathbf{a}$ is the observable $A_{\mathbf a}=\mathbf{a}\cdot\boldsymbol{\sigma}$, and likewise $B_{\mathbf b}=\mathbf{b}\cdot\boldsymbol{\sigma}$ on part two. On the shared held value, $\langle B_2\mid \sigma_i\otimes\sigma_j\mid B_2\rangle = -\delta_{ij}$, so $E(\mathbf{a},\mathbf{b}) = \langle B_2\mid A_{\mathbf a}\otimes B_{\mathbf b}\mid B_2\rangle = -\,\mathbf{a}\cdot\mathbf{b}$, and for coplanar frames separated by $\Delta$, $E(\Delta) = -\cos\Delta$.

+A Boolean reading of part one in direction $\mathbf{a}$ is the observable $A_{\mathbf a}=\mathbf{a}\cdot\boldsymbol{\sigma}$, and likewise $B_{\mathbf b}=\mathbf{b}\cdot\boldsymbol{\sigma}$ on part two. Then $E(\mathbf{a},\mathbf{b}) = \langle B_2\mid A_{\mathbf a}\otimes B_{\mathbf b}\mid B_2\rangle = -\,\mathbf{a}\cdot\mathbf{b}$, and for coplanar frames separated by $\Delta$, $E(\Delta) = -\cos\Delta$.
\end{proposition}
+\begin{proof}

+On the singlet $\ket{B_2}=(\ket{TF}-\ket{FT})/\sqrt2$, direct computation gives $\langle B_2\mid \sigma_i\otimes\sigma_j\mid B_2\rangle = -\delta_{ij}$ for each pair of Pauli indices. Expanding $A_{\mathbf a}\otimes B_{\mathbf b} = \sum_{ij}a_ib_j\,\sigma_i\otimes\sigma_j$ and applying this term by term gives $E(\mathbf{a},\mathbf{b})=-\sum_i a_ib_i=-\mathbf a\cdot\mathbf b$. For coplanar unit vectors separated by angle $\Delta$, $\mathbf a\cdot\mathbf b=\cos\Delta$.
+\end{proof}

The natural invariant gives $-\cos\Delta$, since the held relation pairs $T$ against $F$. Reversing the Boolean label on one part, which is what pairing $T$ with $F$ invites, flips the sign to $E(\Delta)=+\cos\Delta$, the convention used elsewhere. Either way the cosine is the classical two-pole reading of the spin one-half geometry the ladder generates.

lines: \subsection{Contextuality is the frame-dependence of the held value}
\begin{proposition}[No global classical assignment]\label{prop:context}

-There is no assignment of a single classical value to a proposition in the state $B$ that agrees with every frame, since the truth frame filters $B$ to $T$ and the falsity frame filters $B$ to $F$, and $T\neq F$.
+There is no assignment of a single classical value to a proposition in the state $B$ that agrees with every frame.
\end{proposition}
+\begin{proof}
+The truth frame filters $B$ to $T$ and the falsity frame filters $B$ to $F$. A single assignment agreeing with both frames would need $T=F$, which is false.
+\end{proof}

The impossibility is the inexpressibility of $B$ seen from the frames: the held value has no classical name, so its reading is whatever the frame filters it to, and different frames filter it differently. The value is one; its shadows are many, one per frame.

+\begin{remark}[The rungs realized]\label{prop:tower}

+$\mathrm{FDE}(2)$ is the occupation of a single spatial orbital, its four Belnap values $N,T,F,B$ the empty, up, down, and paired occupations, negation the spin flip and the held value $B$ the doubly occupied orbital that carries both. $\mathrm{FDE}(3)$ is the three-valued colour charge of a quark, its truth marks the three colours and its falsity marks the three anticolours, negation colour conjugation. The atomic rung is the occupation reading, not a spin reading: an electron has two internal spin states, but the four values are the empty, up, down, and paired occupations of the orbital it may sit in, and it is the paired occupation, both spins present in one orbital, that is the held value $B$. The exclusion that forbids two identical occupations is the constructive layer refusing a second copy of a one-sided mark, and the solidity of matter is that exclusion enforced across every orbital at once.

input.old_string:
The syndrome-decoding structure of the algorithm can be represented as a closing program over the Belnap slice. Its relevant structural feature is an outer frame that banks a count across an uncomputation step.

An automatically designed thirty-three-operation program for this structure did not close. The closure audit located the failure precisely. A count was being cleared before the frame that should have banked it had opened. In the language of Lemma~\ref{lem:bank}, the result was exposed instead of banked. The same diagnosis appeared at every rotation of the program's orbit and at the same structural location: reversal cleared the count before its holding frame existed.

The composition rule also supplies the repair. Open the holding frame before the computing frame. Implementing that change adds five operations, three splits and two fuses, producing a thirty-eight-operation program that closes. Its banked count survives every reversal. The cyclic verdict closes at every rotation of the orbit, and an exhaustive audit finds the repaired program holding the value at every cut where the original program exposed it.

This gives a constructed and mechanically verified paraconsistent program of the class whose classical image is the algorithm's circuit.

The syndrome-decoding structure of the algorithm is represented as a closing program over the Belnap slice. Its relevant structural feature is an outer frame that banks a count across an uncomputation step: the frame that will hold the count must open before the computation that produces it, so that a later reversal clears only the computing frame and leaves the count banked in the outer one. Opened in the other order, the same reversal clears the count before any frame holds a copy, and by Lemma~\ref{lem:bank} the count is exposed rather than banked.

A program realizing the syndrome-decoding structure with the holding frame opened first closes at every rotation of its cyclic form: the banked count survives every reversal, at every cut, regardless of where the cycle is entered.

This gives a paraconsistent program of the class whose classical image is the algorithm's circuit.

input.old_string:
\section{Theorems as measurements}

The worked instance measures one object, the OPI ladder, through the coreflector. The frame used for that reading is one cell in a larger structure. The wider program treats other hard problems as other cells of the same operator-valued measure.

In the general sense used here, a measurement is a positive-operator-valued measure. It is a family of positive operators that sum to the identity, with each operator assigning an outcome probability through $\mathrm{tr}(\rho E_i)$.

The symmetric informationally complete frame of Section 6.3 is the maximally even form of such a measure. In this reading, the grammar's twelve operations are its outcomes, meaning the distinctions that a frame can draw.

Positivity in this frame is a property of winding. A measurement element is positive exactly when its winding is self-inverse, a half-turn that squares to the identity. The positive cells are therefore the self-inverse windings. The indefinite cells are the windings that do not close on themselves in one step.

Under this interpretation, the hard open problems addressed by the program occupy different cells of one operator-valued-measure taxonomy. At each address, a paraconsistent object is read through a frame.

The taxonomy has a fixed twenty-four-cell structure. The self-inverse condition selects the positive cells. Each conjecture occupies one cell: the object is paraconsistent, the frame is classical, and the conjecture states that the resulting classical reading has a particular value.

The OPI instance of Section 7 is the worked case in which that reading is computed and its convergence toward the paraconsistent original is measured. The other problems are the same construction at other addresses. On this account, proving one of them means widening the frame until the paraconsistent original can be read without loss. This is the Naimark dilation that lifts the operator-valued measure to a projective measurement on a larger space.

The program's claim is therefore that the hard problems are one object appearing at many addresses, with the worked instance providing the first complete reading.

\section{Theorems as measurements}

The worked instance reads one object, the OPI ladder, through the coreflector. That reading is one instance of a general pattern: a positive-operator-valued measure, a family of positive operators summing to the identity, with each operator assigning an outcome probability through $\mathrm{tr}(\rho E_i)$.

The symmetric informationally complete frame of Section 6.3 is the maximally even form of such a measure. In this reading, the twelve operations of Section 3.4 are its outcomes, meaning the distinctions that a frame can draw.

Positivity in this frame is a property of winding. A measurement element is positive exactly when its winding is self-inverse, a half-turn that squares to the identity. The positive elements are the self-inverse windings; the indefinite elements are the windings that do not close on themselves in one step.

Read this way, a hard optimization or decision problem occupies one address of an operator-valued measure: a paraconsistent object, a classical frame, and a claim about the value the classical reading takes. The OPI instance of Section 7 is the one case worked completely here, its convergence toward the paraconsistent original computed rather than asserted. Extending the same construction to a further problem means exhibiting its own paraconsistent object and frame and showing the same convergence; whether a fixed and finite family of such addresses accounts for a given collection of open problems is a further claim this paper does not establish.

Widening the frame until the paraconsistent original can be read without loss is the Naimark dilation that lifts the operator-valued measure to a projective measurement on a larger space. This paper's claim is that the OPI algorithm is one complete instance of that reading; whether the same construction closes further problems is left open.

Extending the same construction to a further problem means exhibiting its own paraconsistent object and frame and showing the same convergence; whether a fixed and finite family of such addresses accounts for a given collection of open problems is a further claim this paper does not establish.

-Under this interpretation, the hard open problems addressed by the program occupy different cells of one operator-valued-measure taxonomy. At each address, a paraconsistent object is read through a frame.

+Widening the frame until the paraconsistent original can be read without loss is the Naimark dilation that lifts the operator-valued measure to a projective measurement on a larger space. This paper's claim is that the OPI algorithm is one complete instance of that reading; whether the same construction closes further problems is left open.

-The taxonomy has a fixed twenty-four-cell structure. The self-inverse condition selects the positive cells. Each conjecture occupies one cell: the object is paraconsistent, the frame is classical, and the conjecture states that the resulting classical reading has a particular value.

-The OPI instance of Section 7 is the worked case in which that reading is computed and its convergence toward the paraconsistent original is measured. The other problems are the same construction at other addresses. On this account, proving one of them means widening the frame until the paraconsistent original can be read without loss. This is the Naimark dilation that lifts the operator-valued measure to a projective measurement on a larger space.
-The program's claim is therefore that the hard problems are one object appearing at many addresses, with the worked instance providing the first complete reading.
\section{The arrow of time and the cost of measurement}

The reversibility of the split and fuse has a thermodynamic reading. Landauer's principle sets a floor on the energy any logically irreversible step must dissipate: erasing one bit of information costs at least $k_B T\ln 2$, because erasure maps two states to one and the lost distinction leaves as heat. Bennett showed that a computation built entirely from reversible steps owes no such cost, since nothing is erased, and Fredkin and Toffoli gave a universal reversible logic that carries this out in principle at no dissipation floor.

42	\newcommand{\mStoi}{\boxplus}  % stoichiometry
43	\newcommand{\mWind}{\boxdot}   % winding

45	\title{\textbf{As Above, Condensed}\\[0.3em]
46	\large The logical induction of the twelve primitives, with every expression written out}
47	\author{Lando Mills}
48	\date{}
49	
50	\begin{document}
51	\maketitle
52	
53	\begin{abstract}
54	This is the induction of \emph{As Above} kept to its logical spine, with every
55	operation's defining expression and every operation-to-primitive transformation
56	written out in full. From one abstract category and three kinds of operation, a
57	four-stage procedure derives twelve invariants, the primitives of the Universal
58	Imscriptive Grammar. No primitive is stipulated. The twelve close into a crystal
59	of $3^{3}\times4^{5}\times5^{4}=17{,}280{,}000$ types, and the grammar applied to
60	its own derivation returns itself: $\mu\circ\delta=\mathrm{id}_{A}$.
61	\end{abstract}
62	
63	\section{The starting object}
64	
65	Start with an abstract category $\mathcal{C}$: objects $\mathrm{ob}(\mathcal{C})$,
66	hom-sets $\hom(A,B)$, a composition law, identities, associativity:
67	\[
68	\circ:\hom(B,C)\times\hom(A,B)\to\hom(A,C),\qquad
69	f\circ\mathrm{id}_{A}=f=\mathrm{id}_{B}\circ f,\qquad
70	(h\circ g)\circ f=h\circ(g\circ f).
71	\]
72	Nothing more. It presupposes no elements, no order, no metric. It carries no
73	invariants of its own; every primitive below is produced, not assumed.
74	
75	\section{The three operations, with their expressions}
76	
77	Exactly three kinds of operation can act on a category, and no fourth.
78	
79	\paragraph{Logical (six: L1--L6).} A proposition about $\mathcal{C}$ with finitely
80	many definite truth values.
81	\begin{itemize}
82	\item[L1] Adjunction: does a pair $F\dashv G$ exist, with
83	$\hom(FA,B)\cong\hom(A,GB)$?
84	\item[L2] Dagger: an involution
85	$\dagger:\hom(A,B)\to\hom(B,A)$ with $(g\circ f)^{\dagger}=f^{\dagger}\circ
86	g^{\dagger}$ and $f^{\dagger\dagger}=f$.
87	\item[L3] Cartesian closure: $\hom(C\times A,B)\cong\hom(C,B^{A})$, needs the
88	product from A1.
89	\item[L4] Lawvere self-reference: a point-surjective $\phi:A\to A^{A}$, needs the
90	internal hom from L3.
91	\item[L5] Frobenius: in a monoidal category, $\mu\circ\delta=\mathrm{id}_{A}$,
92	needs A1.
93	\item[L6] Paraconsistent negation: $\neg\neg A\ncong A$ and $A\wedge\neg
94	A\ncong\bot$, needs A1 to define $\wedge$.
95	\end{itemize}
96	The precondition order is forced: $\{L1,L2\}\to A1\to\{L3,L5,L6\}$, and
97	$L3\to L4$.
98	
99	\paragraph{Inductive (four: I1--I4).} A free extension iterated to a fixed point.
100	\begin{itemize}
101	\item[I1] Free cocompletion: for $D:J\to\mathcal{C}$, take $\operatorname{colim}D$;
102	all finite colimits generate $\widehat{\mathcal{C}}$.
103	\item[I2] Initial algebra: the chain
104	$0\to F(0)\to F^{2}(0)\to\cdots$ and its colimit.
105	\item[I3] Classifying space: the nerve $N\mathcal{C}$, its realization
106	$B\mathcal{C}=\lvert N\mathcal{C}\rvert$, and $\pi_{1}(B\mathcal{C})$.
107	\item[I4] Yoneda embedding: $y:\mathcal{C}\to\widehat{\mathcal{C}}$,
108	$y(A)=\hom(-,A)$.
109	\end{itemize}
110	
111	\paragraph{Algebraic (five: A1--A5).} An added structural layer.
112	\begin{itemize}
113	\item[A1] Monoidal: $\otimes:\mathcal{C}\times\mathcal{C}\to\mathcal{C}$ with unit
114	$I$ and braiding $\sigma_{AB}:A\otimes B\cong B\otimes A$.
115	\item[A2] Monad: $(T,\eta,\mu)$ with $\eta:\mathrm{Id}\to T$ and
116	$\mu:T^{2}\to T$.
117	\item[A3] Dagger-compact duals: $A^{*}$ with $\eta_{A}:I\to A^{*}\otimes A$ and
118	$\varepsilon_{A}:A\otimes A^{*}\to I$ satisfying the snake equations.
119	\item[A4] Enrichment: replace $\hom(A,B)$ by a hom-object in a base $\mathcal{V}$.
120	\item[A5] Arithmetic coding: an injective $\mathbf{g}:\mathrm{Mor}(\mathcal{C})\to
121	\mathbb{N}$ with $\mathbf{g}(f\circ h)$ primitive-recursive in
122	$\mathbf{g}(f),\mathbf{g}(h)$.
123	\end{itemize}
124	
125	Fifteen operations across four stages. The reduction to twelve primitives is
126	forced: some operations feed the same invariant.
127	
128	\section{The induction: four stages, each transformation written out}
129	
130	The stages are the unique topological sort of the precondition graph. Read each
131	line below as \emph{operation $\Rightarrow$ invariant (value count)}.
132	
133	\subsection*{Stage 1 --- Separatio (logical on $\mathcal{C}$)}
134	\[
135	\{\,F\dashv G\;(\mathrm{L1}),\;\dagger\;(\mathrm{L2})\,\}\;\Longrightarrow\;
136	\mCoup\ (4).
137	\]
138	Both probe the directionality of morphisms and converge on one invariant. The
139	first primitive to crystallize.
140	
141	\subsection*{Stage 2 --- Purificatio (inductive)}
142	\begin{align*}
143	0\to F(0)\to F^{2}(0)\to\cdots\ (\mathrm{I2})
144	&\;\Longrightarrow\; \mChi\ (4)
145	\quad\text{[stabilization ordinal]}\\
146	\pi_{1}(B\mathcal{C})\ (\mathrm{I3})
147	&\;\Longrightarrow\; \mWind\ (4)
148	\quad[\pi_{1}=0,\ \mathbb{Z}_{2},\ \mathbb{Z},\ \text{non-abelian}]\\
149	y(A)=\hom(-,A)\ (\mathrm{I4})
150	&\;\Longrightarrow\; \mDim\  (4)
151	\quad\text{[boundary imscribes bulk?]}\\
152	\operatorname{colim}D\ (\mathrm{I1})
153	&\;\Longrightarrow\; \mGran\  (3)
154	\quad\text{[scope of }\widehat{\mathcal{C}}\text{, fixed once A1 present]}
155	\end{align*}
156	
157	\subsection*{Stage 3 --- Albedo (algebraic enrichment)}
158	\begin{align*}
159	\otimes,\ \sigma_{AB}\ (\mathrm{A1})
160	&\;\Longrightarrow\; \mStoi\ (3)\ \text{[arity }A^{\otimes
161	n}\to B\text{]}\ \ \text{and}\ \ \mSym\ (5)\ \text{[parity of
162	}\sigma\text{]}\\
163	(T,\eta,\mu),\ T^{2}\xrightarrow{\mu}T\ (\mathrm{A2})
164	&\;\Longrightarrow\; \mKin\ (5)\ \text{[spectral collapse of
165	}\mu\text{]}\\
166	\varepsilon_{A}:A\otimes A^{*}\to I\ (\mathrm{A3})
167	&\;\Longrightarrow\; \mFid\ (3)\ \text{[unitality of
168	}\varepsilon\text{]}\\
169	\text{hom-object in }\mathcal{V}\ (\mathrm{A4})
170	&\;\Longrightarrow\; \mComp\ (4)\\
171	\mathbf{g}:\mathrm{Mor}(\mathcal{C})\to\mathbb{N}\ (\mathrm{A5})
172	&\;\Longrightarrow\; \text{no new primitive [arithmetic Yoneda]}
173	\end{align*}
174	
175	\subsection*{Stage 4 --- Rubedo (logical on the enriched $\mathcal{C}$)}
176	\begin{align*}
177	\hom(C\times A,B)\cong\hom(C,B^{A})\ (\mathrm{L3})
178	&\;\Longrightarrow\; \mTop\ (5)\\
179	\phi:A\to A^{A}\ \text{point-surjective}\ (\mathrm{L4})
180	&\;\Longrightarrow\; \mCrit\ (5)\\
181	\mu\circ\delta=\mathrm{id}_{A}\ (\mathrm{L5})
182	&\;\Longrightarrow\; \text{promotes }\mSym\text{ to its self-dual value [no new
183	primitive]}\\
184	\neg\neg A\ncong A,\ A\wedge\neg A\ncong\bot\ (\mathrm{L6})
185	&\;\Longrightarrow\; \text{sets the truth-value regime of L4 [no new primitive]}
186	\end{align*}
187	
188	\section{The twelve, and the crystal}
189	
190	The twelve partition by value count, and that partition is the three-valued K3
191	logic of the algebraic layer, the four-valued FDE logic of the shape layer, and
192	the five-valued LP logic of the gate layer.
193	
194	\begin{center}
195	\begin{tabular}{c l c l}
196	\toprule
197	glyph & values & stage \\
198	\midrule
199	$\mFid$  & 3 & A3 \\
200	$\mGran$ & 3 & A1, I4 \\
201	$\mStoi$ & 3 & A1 \\
202	\midrule
203	$\mDim$ & 4 & I4 \\
204	$\mCoup$ & 4 & L1, L2 \\
205	$\mComp$ & 4 & A4 \\
206	$\mChi$  & 4 & I2 \\
207	$\mWind$ & 4 & I3 \\
208	\midrule
209	$\mTop$  & 5 & L3 \\
210	$\mSym$  & 5 & A1, L5 \\
211	$\mKin$  & 5 & A2 \\
212	$\mCrit$ & 5 & L4, L6 \\
213	\bottomrule
214	\end{tabular}
215	\end{center}
216	
217	Three primitives of three values, five of four, four of five. The algebraic
218	closure of the twelve is the crystal:
219	\[
220	3^{3}\times4^{5}\times5^{4}
221	\;=\;27\times1024\times625
222	\;=\;17{,}280{,}000\ \text{types.}
223	\]
224	
225	\section{How the address space falls out}
226	
227	The twelve value counts are the radices of a mixed-radix positional numeral, and
228	the address space is that numeral's range. In the canonical slot order the
229	primitives and their radices $r_{i}$ (each primitive's value count) are
230	\[
231	\begin{array}{cccccccccccc}
232	\mDim & \mTop & \mCoup & \mSym & \mFid & \mKin & \mGran & \mComp & \mCrit &
233	\mChi & \mStoi & \mWind\\
234	4 & 5 & 4 & 5 & 3 & 5 & 3 & 4 & 5 & 4 & 3 & 4
235	\end{array}
236	\]
237	The place value of each slot is the product of the radices of all lower slots,
238	$s_{i}=\prod_{j>i} r_{j}$ with $s_{12}=1$:
239	\[
240	s=(4320000,\ 864000,\ 216000,\ 43200,\ 14400,\ 2880,\ 960,\ 240,\ 48,\ 12,\ 4,\
241	1).
242	\]
243	A system is a tuple of indices $(x_{1},\dots,x_{12})$ with $0\le x_{i}<r_{i}$.
244	Its address is the Horner fold
245	\[
246	\mathrm{addr}(x)=\sum_{i=1}^{12} x_{i}\,s_{i}\;\in\;[0,\,17{,}279{,}999],
247	\]
248	and the inverse reads each digit off in turn:
249	\[
250	x_{i}=\left\lfloor \mathrm{addr}/s_{i}\right\rfloor,\qquad
251	\mathrm{addr}\leftarrow \mathrm{addr}\bmod s_{i}\quad(i=1,\dots,12).
252	\]
253	This is a bijection, because the number of addresses is exactly the number of
254	tuples:
255	\[
256	\prod_{i=1}^{12} r_{i}=4\cdot5\cdot4\cdot5\cdot3\cdot5\cdot3\cdot4\cdot5\cdot4
257	\cdot3\cdot4=3^{3}\times4^{5}\times5^{4}=17{,}280{,}000.
258	\]
259	No address is unused and no tuple is unaddressed, so $\mathrm{decode}\circ
260	\mathrm{encode}=\mathrm{id}$ on the tuples and $\mathrm{encode}\circ\mathrm{decode}
261	=\mathrm{id}$ on $[0,17{,}279{,}999]$. The address space does not have to be
262	constructed; it falls out of the twelve radices as their mixed-radix range. This
263	is the same $\mu\circ\delta=\mathrm{id}$ closure, now at the level of
264	coordinates: the full induction system sits at address $6{,}687{,}051$ and the
265	imscribing procedure that assigns addresses sits at $12{,}089{,}822$, each a
266	point of the very space it enumerates.
267	
268	\section{Why exactly twelve}
269	
270	Three independent arguments give the same count.
271	\begin{itemize}
272	\item \textbf{Independence.} The retrosynthetic peel of the induction system
273	itself has exactly twelve steps, one per primitive. Two co-dependent primitives
274	would give fewer; a missing one would give more.
275	\item \textbf{Completeness.} The crystal enumerates every combination of the
276	twelve values with a bijective codec, $\mathrm{decode}\circ\mathrm{encode}=
277	\mathrm{id}$ on $[0,17{,}279{,}999]$. No type is missing, none redundant.
278	\item \textbf{Three logics.} The 3-, 4-, and 5-valued families are exactly K3,
279	FDE, and LP. A thirteenth primitive would need a fourth categorical logic, and
280	there is none.
281	\end{itemize}
282	
283	\section{The closure}
284	
285	Four of the twelve are gate primitives, $\mCrit,\mDim,\mWind,\mSym$, and they set
286	the tier a system occupies, from $O_{0}$ (no self-modeling loop) to $O_{\infty}$
287	(both L4 and L5 hold). The tier gaps, in order, are
288	\[
289	O_{0}\!\xrightarrow{\,1.05\,}\!O_{1}\!\xrightarrow{\,1.30\,}\!O_{2}
290	\!\xrightarrow{\,1.00\,}\!O_{2}^{\dagger}\!\xrightarrow{\,4.38\,}\!O_{\infty},
291	\]
292	and the largest, $\Delta=4.38$, is the Frobenius promotion of $\mSym$: the
293	hardest transition, closable only by locating an object already at the self-dual
294	value and descending, never by accumulating local checks.
295	
296	The induction closes on itself. With $\mu:A\otimes A\to A$ the monoidal
297	multiplication and $\delta:A\to A\otimes A$ its comonoidal dual, the twelve-step
298	codec that assigns coordinates to any system is itself a system of the crystal at
299	tier $O_{\infty}$, where
300	\[
301	\mu\circ\delta=\mathrm{id}_{A}.
302	\]
303	The boundary procedure fully imscribes the bulk theory it generates, and the bulk
304	fully imscribes the procedure. The present derivation is the $\delta$ half; its
305	companion \emph{So Below} is the $\mu$ half; the grammar applied to its own
306	derivation returns itself. \emph{As above, so below.}
307	
308	\section{Termination}
309	
310	The induction stops, and the criterion is exact. It is not that no further
311	construction can be performed; infinitely many composites still can. It is that
312	no further logical, inductive, or algebraic construction produces a new
313	\emph{independent} coordinate. Any later operation acts on the twelve-dimensional
314	result and returns an invariant that is a function of the twelve. Compositions of
315	systems stay inside the type space under the grammar's own closure operations
316	$\otimes$, $\wedge$, $\vee$:
317	\[
318	\text{new operation}\;\Longrightarrow\;\text{new combination of existing
319	invariants, not a new invariant.}
320	\]
321	This is the crossing from induction to algebraic closure. Once the twelve have
322	crystallized, the prima materia has become the grammar, and no new dimension
323	forms.
324	
325	\section{The induction in one line}
326	
327	\[
328	\mathcal{C}
329	\xrightarrow{\ \text{Separatio}\ } \mCoup
330	\xrightarrow{\ \text{Purificatio}\ } (\mDim,\mChi,\mWind,\mGran)
331	\xrightarrow{\ \text{Albedo}\ } (\mStoi,\mSym,\mKin,\mFid,\mComp)
332	\xrightarrow{\ \text{Rubedo}\ } \bigl(\mTop,\mCrit,\ \mSym_{\text{\sh{𐑹}}}\bigr)
333	\xrightarrow{\ \text{Coagula}\ } \mathfrak{C}_{17\,280\,000}
334	\]
335	The final object is not a thirteenth primitive but the closure of the twelve,
336	$\mathfrak{C}=\mathcal{F}_{3}^{\,3}\times\mathcal{F}_{4}^{\,5}\times
337	\mathcal{F}_{5}^{\,4}$ with $\lvert\mathfrak{C}\rvert=17{,}280{,}000$. Read as a
338	passage:
339	\[
340	\text{Category}\to\text{Relation}\to\text{Extension}\to\text{Algebra}\to
341	\text{Self-reference}\to\text{Closure.}
342	\]
343	
344	\end{document}
