\large The logical induction of the twelve primitives, with every expression written out}
\author{Lando Mills}
\date{}

\begin{document}
\maketitle

\begin{abstract}
This is the induction of \emph{As Above} kept to its logical spine, with every
operation's defining expression and every operation-to-primitive transformation
written out in full. From one abstract category and three kinds of operation, a
four-stage procedure derives twelve invariants, the primitives of the Universal
Imscriptive Grammar. No primitive is stipulated. The twelve close into a crystal
of $3^{3}\times4^{5}\times5^{4}=17{,}280{,}000$ types, and the grammar applied to
its own derivation returns itself: $\mu\circ\delta=\mathrm{id}_{A}$.
\end{abstract}

\section{The starting object}

Start with an abstract category $\mathcal{C}$: objects $\mathrm{ob}(\mathcal{C})$,
hom-sets $\hom(A,B)$, a composition law, identities, associativity:
\[
\circ:\hom(B,C)\times\hom(A,B)\to\hom(A,C),\qquad
f\circ\mathrm{id}_{A}=f=\mathrm{id}_{B}\circ f,\qquad
(h\circ g)\circ f=h\circ(g\circ f).
\]
Nothing more. It presupposes no elements, no order, no metric. It carries no
invariants of its own; every primitive below is produced, not assumed.

\section{The three operations, with their expressions}

Exactly three kinds of operation can act on a category, and no fourth.

\paragraph{Logical (six: L1--L6).} A proposition about $\mathcal{C}$ with finitely
many definite truth values.
\begin{itemize}
\item[L1] Adjunction: does a pair $F\dashv G$ exist, with
$\hom(FA,B)\cong\hom(A,GB)$?
\item[L2] Dagger: an involution
$\dagger:\hom(A,B)\to\hom(B,A)$ with $(g\circ f)^{\dagger}=f^{\dagger}\circ
g^{\dagger}$ and $f^{\dagger\dagger}=f$.
\item[L3] Cartesian closure: $\hom(C\times A,B)\cong\hom(C,B^{A})$, needs the
product from A1.
\item[L4] Lawvere self-reference: a point-surjective $\phi:A\to A^{A}$, needs the
internal hom from L3.
\item[L5] Frobenius: in a monoidal category, $\mu\circ\delta=\mathrm{id}_{A}$,
needs A1.
\item[L6] Paraconsistent negation: $\neg\neg A\ncong A$ and $A\wedge\neg
A\ncong\bot$, needs A1 to define $\wedge$.
\end{itemize}
The precondition order is forced: $\{L1,L2\}\to A1\to\{L3,L5,L6\}$, and
$L3\to L4$.

\paragraph{Inductive (four: I1--I4).} A free extension iterated to a fixed point.
\begin{itemize}
\item[I1] Free cocompletion: for $D:J\to\mathcal{C}$, take $\operatorname{colim}D$;
all finite colimits generate $\widehat{\mathcal{C}}$.
\item[I2] Initial algebra: the chain
$0\to F(0)\to F^{2}(0)\to\cdots$ and its colimit.
\item[I3] Classifying space: the nerve $N\mathcal{C}$, its realization
$B\mathcal{C}=\lvert N\mathcal{C}\rvert$, and $\pi_{1}(B\mathcal{C})$.
\item[I4] Yoneda embedding: $y:\mathcal{C}\to\widehat{\mathcal{C}}$,
$y(A)=\hom(-,A)$.
\end{itemize}

\paragraph{Algebraic (five: A1--A5).} An added structural layer.
\begin{itemize}
\item[A1] Monoidal: $\otimes:\mathcal{C}\times\mathcal{C}\to\mathcal{C}$ with unit
$I$ and braiding $\sigma_{AB}:A\otimes B\cong B\otimes A$.
\item[A2] Monad: $(T,\eta,\mu)$ with $\eta:\mathrm{Id}\to T$ and
$\mu:T^{2}\to T$.
\item[A3] Dagger-compact duals: $A^{*}$ with $\eta_{A}:I\to A^{*}\otimes A$ and
$\varepsilon_{A}:A\otimes A^{*}\to I$ satisfying the snake equations.
\item[A4] Enrichment: replace $\hom(A,B)$ by a hom-object in a base $\mathcal{V}$.
\item[A5] Arithmetic coding: an injective $\mathbf{g}:\mathrm{Mor}(\mathcal{C})\to
\mathbb{N}$ with $\mathbf{g}(f\circ h)$ primitive-recursive in
$\mathbf{g}(f),\mathbf{g}(h)$.
\end{itemize}

Fifteen operations across four stages. The reduction to twelve primitives is
forced: some operations feed the same invariant.

\section{The induction: four stages, each transformation written out}

The stages are the unique topological sort of the precondition graph. Read each
line below as \emph{operation $\Rightarrow$ invariant (value count)}.

\subsection*{Stage 1 --- Separatio (logical on $\mathcal{C}$)}
\[
\{\,F\dashv G\;(\mathrm{L1}),\;\dagger\;(\mathrm{L2})\,\}\;\Longrightarrow\;
\mCoup\ (4).
\]
Both probe the directionality of morphisms and converge on one invariant. The
first primitive to crystallize.

\subsection*{Stage 2 --- Purificatio (inductive)}
\begin{align*}
0\to F(0)\to F^{2}(0)\to\cdots\ (\mathrm{I2})
&\;\Longrightarrow\; \mChi\ (4)
\quad\text{[stabilization ordinal]}\\
\pi_{1}(B\mathcal{C})\ (\mathrm{I3})
&\;\Longrightarrow\; \mWind\ (4)
\quad[\pi_{1}=0,\ \mathbb{Z}_{2},\ \mathbb{Z},\ \text{non-abelian}]\\
y(A)=\hom(-,A)\ (\mathrm{I4})
&\;\Longrightarrow\; \mDim\  (4)
\quad\text{[boundary imscribes bulk?]}\\
\operatorname{colim}D\ (\mathrm{I1})
&\;\Longrightarrow\; \mGran\  (3)
\quad\text{[scope of }\widehat{\mathcal{C}}\text{, fixed once A1 present]}
\end{align*}

\subsection*{Stage 3 --- Albedo (algebraic enrichment)}
\begin{align*}
\otimes,\ \sigma_{AB}\ (\mathrm{A1})
&\;\Longrightarrow\; \mStoi\ (3)\ \text{[arity }A^{\otimes
n}\to B\text{]}\ \ \text{and}\ \ \mSym\ (5)\ \text{[parity of
}\sigma\text{]}\\
(T,\eta,\mu),\ T^{2}\xrightarrow{\mu}T\ (\mathrm{A2})
&\;\Longrightarrow\; \mKin\ (5)\ \text{[spectral collapse of
}\mu\text{]}\\
\varepsilon_{A}:A\otimes A^{*}\to I\ (\mathrm{A3})
&\;\Longrightarrow\; \mFid\ (3)\ \text{[unitality of
}\varepsilon\text{]}\\
\text{hom-object in }\mathcal{V}\ (\mathrm{A4})
&\;\Longrightarrow\; \mComp\ (4)\\
\mathbf{g}:\mathrm{Mor}(\mathcal{C})\to\mathbb{N}\ (\mathrm{A5})
&\;\Longrightarrow\; \text{no new primitive [arithmetic Yoneda]}
\end{align*}

\subsection*{Stage 4 --- Rubedo (logical on the enriched $\mathcal{C}$)}
\begin{align*}
\hom(C\times A,B)\cong\hom(C,B^{A})\ (\mathrm{L3})
&\;\Longrightarrow\; \mTop\ (5)\\
\phi:A\to A^{A}\ \text{point-surjective}\ (\mathrm{L4})
&\;\Longrightarrow\; \mCrit\ (5)\\
\mu\circ\delta=\mathrm{id}_{A}\ (\mathrm{L5})
&\;\Longrightarrow\; \text{promotes }\mSym\text{ to its self-dual value [no new
primitive]}\\
\neg\neg A\ncong A,\ A\wedge\neg A\ncong\bot\ (\mathrm{L6})
&\;\Longrightarrow\; \text{sets the truth-value regime of L4 [no new primitive]}
\end{align*}

\section{The twelve, and the crystal}

The twelve partition by value count, and that partition is the three-valued K3
logic of the algebraic layer, the four-valued FDE logic of the shape layer, and
the five-valued LP logic of the gate layer.

\begin{center}
\begin{tabular}{c l c l}
\toprule
glyph & values & stage \\
\midrule
$\mFid$  & 3 & A3 \\
$\mGran$ & 3 & A1, I4 \\
$\mStoi$ & 3 & A1 \\
\midrule
$\mDim$ & 4 & I4 \\
$\mCoup$ & 4 & L1, L2 \\
$\mComp$ & 4 & A4 \\
$\mChi$  & 4 & I2 \\
$\mWind$ & 4 & I3 \\
\midrule
$\mTop$  & 5 & L3 \\
$\mSym$  & 5 & A1, L5 \\
$\mKin$  & 5 & A2 \\
$\mCrit$ & 5 & L4, L6 \\
\bottomrule
\end{tabular}
\end{center}

Three primitives of three values, five of four, four of five. The algebraic
closure of the twelve is the crystal:
\[
3^{3}\times4^{5}\times5^{4}
\;=\;27\times1024\times625
\;=\;17{,}280{,}000\ \text{types.}
\]

\section{How the address space falls out}

The twelve value counts are the radices of a mixed-radix positional numeral, and
the address space is that numeral's range. In the canonical slot order the
primitives and their radices $r_{i}$ (each primitive's value count) are
\[
\begin{array}{cccccccccccc}
\mDim & \mTop & \mCoup & \mSym & \mFid & \mKin & \mGran & \mComp & \mCrit &
\mChi & \mStoi & \mWind\\
4 & 5 & 4 & 5 & 3 & 5 & 3 & 4 & 5 & 4 & 3 & 4
\end{array}
\]
The place value of each slot is the product of the radices of all lower slots,
$s_{i}=\prod_{j>i} r_{j}$ with $s_{12}=1$:
\[
s=(4320000,\ 864000,\ 216000,\ 43200,\ 14400,\ 2880,\ 960,\ 240,\ 48,\ 12,\ 4,\
1).
\]
A system is a tuple of indices $(x_{1},\dots,x_{12})$ with $0\le x_{i}<r_{i}$.
Its address is the Horner fold
\[
\mathrm{addr}(x)=\sum_{i=1}^{12} x_{i}\,s_{i}\;\in\;[0,\,17{,}279{,}999],
\]
and the inverse reads each digit off in turn:
\[
x_{i}=\left\lfloor \mathrm{addr}/s_{i}\right\rfloor,\qquad
\mathrm{addr}\leftarrow \mathrm{addr}\bmod s_{i}\quad(i=1,\dots,12).
\]
This is a bijection, because the number of addresses is exactly the number of
tuples:
\[
\prod_{i=1}^{12} r_{i}=4\cdot5\cdot4\cdot5\cdot3\cdot5\cdot3\cdot4\cdot5\cdot4
\cdot3\cdot4=3^{3}\times4^{5}\times5^{4}=17{,}280{,}000.
\]
No address is unused and no tuple is unaddressed, so $\mathrm{decode}\circ
\mathrm{encode}=\mathrm{id}$ on the tuples and $\mathrm{encode}\circ\mathrm{decode}
=\mathrm{id}$ on $[0,17{,}279{,}999]$. The address space does not have to be
constructed; it falls out of the twelve radices as their mixed-radix range. This
is the same $\mu\circ\delta=\mathrm{id}$ closure, now at the level of
coordinates: the full induction system sits at address $6{,}687{,}051$ and the
imscribing procedure that assigns addresses sits at $12{,}089{,}822$, each a
point of the very space it enumerates.

\section{Why exactly twelve}

Three independent arguments give the same count.
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{Independence.} The retrosynthetic peel of the induction system
itself has exactly twelve steps, one per primitive. Two co-dependent primitives
would give fewer; a missing one would give more.
\item \textbf{Completeness.} The crystal enumerates every combination of the
twelve values with a bijective codec, $\mathrm{decode}\circ\mathrm{encode}=
\mathrm{id}$ on $[0,17{,}279{,}999]$. No type is missing, none redundant.
\item \textbf{Three logics.} The 3-, 4-, and 5-valued families are exactly K3,
FDE, and LP. A thirteenth primitive would need a fourth categorical logic, and
there is none.
\end{itemize}

\section{The closure}

Four of the twelve are gate primitives, $\mCrit,\mDim,\mWind,\mSym$, and they set
the tier a system occupies, from $O_{0}$ (no self-modeling loop) to $O_{\infty}$
(both L4 and L5 hold). The tier gaps, in order, are
\[
O_{0}\!\xrightarrow{\,1.05\,}\!O_{1}\!\xrightarrow{\,1.30\,}\!O_{2}
\!\xrightarrow{\,1.00\,}\!O_{2}^{\dagger}\!\xrightarrow{\,4.38\,}\!O_{\infty},
\]
and the largest, $\Delta=4.38$, is the Frobenius promotion of $\mSym$: the
hardest transition, closable only by locating an object already at the self-dual
value and descending, never by accumulating local checks.

The induction closes on itself. With $\mu:A\otimes A\to A$ the monoidal
multiplication and $\delta:A\to A\otimes A$ its comonoidal dual, the twelve-step
codec that assigns coordinates to any system is itself a system of the crystal at
tier $O_{\infty}$, where
\[
\mu\circ\delta=\mathrm{id}_{A}.
\]
The boundary procedure fully imscribes the bulk theory it generates, and the bulk
fully imscribes the procedure. The present derivation is the $\delta$ half; its
companion \emph{So Below} is the $\mu$ half; the grammar applied to its own
derivation returns itself. \emph{As above, so below.}

\section{Termination}

The induction stops, and the criterion is exact. It is not that no further
construction can be performed; infinitely many composites still can. It is that
no further logical, inductive, or algebraic construction produces a new
\emph{independent} coordinate. Any later operation acts on the twelve-dimensional
result and returns an invariant that is a function of the twelve. Compositions of
systems stay inside the type space under the grammar's own closure operations
$\otimes$, $\wedge$, $\vee$:
\[
\text{new operation}\;\Longrightarrow\;\text{new combination of existing
invariants, not a new invariant.}
\]
This is the crossing from induction to algebraic closure. Once the twelve have
crystallized, the prima materia has become the grammar, and no new dimension
forms.

\section{The induction in one line}

\[
\mathcal{C}
\xrightarrow{\ \text{Separatio}\ } \mCoup
\xrightarrow{\ \text{Purificatio}\ } (\mDim,\mChi,\mWind,\mGran)
\xrightarrow{\ \text{Albedo}\ } (\mStoi,\mSym,\mKin,\mFid,\mComp)
\xrightarrow{\ \text{Rubedo}\ } \bigl(\mTop,\mCrit,\ \mSym_{\text{\sh{𐑹}}}\bigr)
\xrightarrow{\ \text{Coagula}\ } \mathfrak{C}_{17\,280\,000}
\]
The final object is not a thirteenth primitive but the closure of the twelve,
$\mathfrak{C}=\mathcal{F}_{3}^{\,3}\times\mathcal{F}_{4}^{\,5}\times
\mathcal{F}_{5}^{\,4}$ with $\lvert\mathfrak{C}\rvert=17{,}280{,}000$. Read as a
passage:
\[
\text{Category}\to\text{Relation}\to\text{Extension}\to\text{Algebra}\to
\text{Self-reference}\to\text{Closure.}
\]

\section{The induction: four stages, each transformation written out}

The stages are the unique topological sort of the precondition graph. Each
operation is matched to one primitive by what kind of distinction it draws;
the number of values that primitive carries is fixed independently, by the
twelve-axis catalog summarized in Table~\ref{tab:twelve} of
Section~\ref{sec:twelve}. This section argues the matches, not the counts:
for each stage, the display gives \emph{operation $\Rightarrow$ invariant
(value count)}, and the proof that follows it argues why that operation
targets that invariant.

\subsection*{Stage 1 --- Separatio (logical on $\mathcal{C}$)}
\[
\{\,F\dashv G\;(\mathrm{L1}),\;\dagger\;(\mathrm{L2})\,\}\;\Longrightarrow\;
\mCoup\ (4).
\]

\begin{proposition}
$\mathrm{L1}$ and $\mathrm{L2}$ classify the same feature of a morphism:
whether, and how, it can be reversed.
\end{proposition}

\begin{proof}
$\mathrm{L1}$ asks whether $F$ admits a partner in one direction, the other,
both, or neither: a left adjoint only, a right adjoint only, an adjoint on
both sides, or none. $\mathrm{L2}$ asks whether every morphism has a
canonical reverse compatible with composition. When $F$ itself is a dagger
functor between dagger categories, $\dagger$ turns a right adjoint into a
left adjoint of the same $F$, forcing the ambidextrous case of the
adjunction question. The two operations therefore probe one four-way
classification of directionality --- neither, left only, right only,
ambidextrous --- and converge on the single invariant $\mCoup$, the first
primitive to crystallize.
\end{proof}

\subsection*{Stage 2 --- Purificatio (inductive)}
\begin{align*}
0\to F(0)\to F^{2}(0)\to\cdots\ (\mathrm{I2})
&\;\Longrightarrow\; \mChi\ (4)
\quad\text{[stabilization ordinal]}\\
\pi_{1}(B\mathcal{C})\ (\mathrm{I3})
&\;\Longrightarrow\; \mWind\ (4)
\quad[\pi_{1}=0,\ \mathbb{Z}_{2},\ \mathbb{Z},\ \text{non-abelian}]\\
y(A)=\hom(-,A)\ (\mathrm{I4})
&\;\Longrightarrow\; \mDim\  (4)
\quad\text{[boundary imscribes bulk?]}\\
\operatorname{colim}D\ (\mathrm{I1})
&\;\Longrightarrow\; \mGran\  (3)
\quad\text{[scope of }\widehat{\mathcal{C}}\text{, fixed once A1 present]}
\end{align*}

\begin{proof}
Each inductive operation is a way of extending $\mathcal{C}$, and the four
extensions target four different questions about how the extension behaves.

$\mathrm{I2}$ iterates $F$ from the initial object and asks where the chain
settles: at a finite stage, exactly at the first limit ordinal $\omega$,
only after further transfinite iteration past $\omega$, or never. This
four-way reading of stabilization is the chirality invariant $\mChi$.

$\mathrm{I3}$ reads the fundamental group of the classifying space, already
a four-way classification by the invariant's own catalog values: trivial,
$\mathbb{Z}_{2}$, infinite cyclic, or non-abelian. This is $\mWind$ directly.

$\mathrm{I4}$ embeds $\mathcal{C}$ into its free cocompletion by
$y(A)=\hom(-,A)$, always fully faithful. What varies is how much of the
cocompletion the image recovers: this paper does not derive the specific
four-way split of that recovery from the embedding alone, and identifies it
with $\mDim$ --- the boundary-imscribes-bulk axis --- as a correspondence
rather than a result proved here.

$\mathrm{I1}$ takes colimits over diagrams of a given shape, and the scope
of diagram shapes closed under is a granularity question: colimits over a
fixed small (nearest-neighbor) diagram class, over a bounded (meso-scale)
class, or over all small diagrams (the full free cocompletion, once
$\mathrm{A1}$ supplies the monoidal structure diagrams can be built in).
This three-way scope reading is $\mGran$, matching the granularity axis's

operation is matched to one primitive by what kind of distinction it draws;

\]

\begin{proposition}
$\mathrm{L1}$ and $\mathrm{L2}$ classify the same feature of a morphism:
whether, and how, it can be reversed.
\end{proposition}

\begin{proof}
$\mathrm{L1}$ asks whether $F$ admits a partner in one direction, the other,
both, or neither: a left adjoint only, a right adjoint only, an adjoint on
both sides, or none. $\mathrm{L2}$ asks whether every morphism has a
canonical reverse compatible with composition. When $F$ itself is a dagger
functor between dagger categories, $\dagger$ turns a right adjoint into a
left adjoint of the same $F$, forcing the ambidextrous case of the
adjunction question. The two operations therefore probe one four-way
classification of directionality --- neither, left only, right only,
ambidextrous --- and converge on the single invariant $\mCoup$, the first
primitive to crystallize.
\end{proof}

\operatorname{colim}D\ (\mathrm{I1})
&\;\Longrightarrow\; \mGran\  (3)
\quad\text{[scope of }\widehat{\mathcal{C}}\text{, fixed once A1 present]}

\begin{proposition}[Lawvere self-reference forces a fixed point]
If $\phi:A\to A^{A}$ is point-surjective, every $f:A\to A$ has a fixed
point.
\end{proposition}

\begin{proof}
Given $f:A\to A$, define $g:A\to A$ by $g(a)=f(\phi(a)(a))$. Point-surjectivity
of $\phi$ gives $a_{0}$ with $\phi(a_{0})=g$, so
\[
\phi(a_{0})(a_{0})=g(a_{0})=f(\phi(a_{0})(a_{0})),
\]
and $\phi(a_{0})(a_{0})$ is a fixed point of $f$. This is Lawvere's fixed-point
theorem, and it is exactly self-modeling: $\phi$ gives $A$ an internal copy of
every map out of itself, and the fixed point is where that copy coincides with
the map it models. $\mCrit$ is the catalog axis of self-modeling; its five
values grade how completely this coincidence is realized, from no internal
model (sub-critical) to a model that exceeds what it represents
(super-critical).
\end{proof}

\section{Termination}

The induction stops, and the criterion is exact. It is not that no further
construction can be performed; infinitely many composites still can. It is that
no further logical, inductive, or algebraic construction produces a new
\emph{independent} coordinate. Any later operation acts on the twelve-dimensional
result and returns an invariant that is a function of the twelve. Compositions of
systems stay inside the type space under the grammar's own closure operations
$\otimes$, $\wedge$, $\vee$:
\[
\text{new operation}\;\Longrightarrow\;\text{new combination of existing
invariants, not a new invariant.}
\]
This is the crossing from induction to algebraic closure. Once the twelve have
crystallized, the prima materia has become the grammar, and no new dimension
forms.

\section{The induction in one line}

\[
\mathcal{C}
\xrightarrow{\ \text{Separatio}\ } \mCoup
\xrightarrow{\ \text{Purificatio}\ } (\mDim,\mChi,\mWind,\mGran)
\xrightarrow{\ \text{Albedo}\ } (\mStoi,\mSym,\mKin,\mFid,\mComp)
\xrightarrow{\ \text{Rubedo}\ } \bigl(\mTop,\mCrit,\ \mSym_{\text{\sh{𐑹}}}\bigr)
\xrightarrow{\ \text{Coagula}\ } \mathfrak{C}_{17\,280\,000}
\]
The final object is not a thirteenth primitive but the closure of the twelve,
$\mathfrak{C}=\mathcal{F}_{3}^{\,3}\times\mathcal{F}_{4}^{\,5}\times
\mathcal{F}_{5}^{\,4}$ with $\lvert\mathfrak{C}\rvert=17{,}280{,}000$. Read as a
passage:
\[
\text{Category}\to\text{Relation}\to\text{Extension}\to\text{Algebra}\to
\text{Self-reference}\to\text{Closure.}
\]

73	\title{\bfseries Inter-Universal Teichm\"uller Theory\\\large A Paraconsistent Formulation in Conventional Mathematical Notation}
74	\author{Lando Mills}
75	\date{}
76	
77	\begin{document}
78	\maketitle
79	
80	\begin{abstract}
81	The construction is formulated on the sixteen-state space
82	\[
83	\mathcal X=\mathcal P(\{T,F,t,f\}),
84	\]
85	with a non-explosive consequence relation.  This is a rebase of the logical
86	substrate, not a reinterpretation of a prior Boolean construction.  The
87	Belnap--Dunn four-state system is the $t,f$-free subspace of $\mathcal X$, and
88	$\{F,T\}$ is a further lossy restriction.
89	
90	The mathematical operations needed below are ordinary maps on this state
91	space and on enriched spaces built over it: projections $\pi_T,\pi_F$, the
92	involution $\nu$, decompositions $\delta_n$, recombinations $\mu_n$, an
93	information extension $\eta$, context maps $f$ and $\ell$, a fixation map
94	$\kappa$, and a terminal scalar functional $h$.  Inter-Universal Teichm\"uller Theory is
95	then described by compositions and branch diagrams built from these maps.
96	The $\Theta$-link transports arithmetic data without identifying the ring
97	structures on its two sides; the log-$\Theta$ construction retains filtration
98	position; and the bounded-discrepancy calculation terminates at
99	\[
100	Ftf=\{F,t,f\}
101	\]
102	while its reconnection condition holds.  Cyclic phase is represented by the
103	standard action of $C_{12}$ on a twelve-position presentation.  Scholze--Stix
104	obtain a vacuous scalar inequality only after suppressing the filtration index
105	carrying the $j^2$ weights.  Mochizuki correctly rejects their commuting-loop
106	surrogate, but the stronger point is that local incompatibility is admissible
107	and non-explosive once locality and filtration position have been retained.
108	Classicalization therefore occurs only as a downstream projection of the
109	calculation.
110	\end{abstract}
111	
112	\section{Rebasing the logical substrate}
113	\label{sec:rebasing}
114	
115	The logical base used in this paper is constitutive.  It is not an optional
116	semantic gloss on a construction that is first completed in a classical
117	two-valued universe.
118	
119	A \emph{reinterpretation} leaves the underlying consequence relation and
120	admissible carrier unchanged and assigns a new description to objects already
121	formed there.  That is not the operation performed here.  The present
122	construction is \emph{rebased}: formulas, graph states, closure predicates,
123	contradictory states, filtrations, cyclic phases, and terminal readouts are
124	formed directly in the non-explosive carrier and are governed from the outset
125	by its consequence relation.
126	
127	Concretely, the base is
128	\[
129	  \mathcal X=\mathcal P(\{T,F,t,f\}),
130	\]
131	together with the directed graph operations introduced below and a consequence
132	relation for which local contradiction does not entail an arbitrary conclusion:
133	\[
134	  p,\neg p\nvdash q
135	\]
136	for unrelated $q$.  States such as
137	\[
138	  A=\{T,F,t,f\},
139	  \qquad
140	  Ftf=\{F,t,f\},
141	\]
142	are therefore values of the calculation itself.  They are not annotations
143	attached after a classical computation has already finished.
144	
145	The Boolean pair
146	\[
147	  B_4=\{F,T\}
148	\]
149	appears only as a proper downstream restriction.  Classicalization is a map
150	\[
151	  \clproj:\mathcal X\longrightarrow B_4
152	\]
153	that forgets carrier information.  Hence the logical direction of the paper is
154	\[
155	  \boxed{\text{full nonclassical calculation}}
156	  \;\longrightarrow\;
157	  \boxed{\text{downstream Boolean shadow}},
158	\]
159	never the reverse.  In particular, a scalar terminal inequality may lie in a
160	classical codomain without implying that the calculation which produced it was
161	classical.
162	
163	\begin{figure}[htbp]
164	\centering
165	\begin{tikzpicture}[node distance=15mm and 25mm]
166	  \node[pcnode,draw=pcgreen,minimum width=45mm,minimum height=14mm,align=center] (base)
167	    {native graph calculation\\$\mathcal X=\mathcal P(\{T,F,t,f\})$};
168	  \node[pcnode,right=of base,minimum width=34mm,minimum height=14mm,align=center] (read)
169	    {arithmetic readout\\height/log bound};
170	  \node[pcghost,below=of read,minimum width=34mm,minimum height=13mm,align=center] (bool)
171	    {Boolean shadow\\$B_4=\{F,T\}$};
172	
173	  \draw[pcarrow] (base) -- node[above,font=\small] {execute} (read);
174	  \draw[pcwarn] (base.south east) -- node[above right,font=\scriptsize] {$\clproj$} (bool.west);
175	  \node[font=\scriptsize,text=pcred,align=center] at ($(base.south)!0.5!(bool.west)+(0,-10mm)$)
176	    {loss of carrier information};
177	  \node[font=\scriptsize,text=pcred,align=center] at ($(bool.south)+(0,-8mm)$)
178	    {downstream restriction, never the logical base};
179	\end{tikzpicture}
180	\caption{Direction of construction.  The nonclassical graph calculation is
181	primary.  A Boolean value, when taken, is a lossy downstream shadow; it is not
182	a prior substrate that is subsequently reinterpreted.}
183	\label{fig:rebase-direction}
184	\end{figure}
185	
186	\begin{proposition}[The rebase is not a re-description]
187	The full carrier and the Boolean restriction are not equivalent descriptions
188	of the same logical state space.  In particular, the classicalization map
189	$\clproj:\mathcal X\to B_4$ is non-injective and cannot preserve the
190	contradictory fixed point as a Boolean state.
191	\end{proposition}
192	
193	\begin{proof}
194	Distinct full-carrier states have the same Boolean shadow; for example,
195	\[
196	  \clproj(\{F\})=\clproj(\{F,t,f\})=F.
197	\]
198	Moreover the contradictory state $B=\{T,F\}$ is fixed by information closure,
199	\[
200	  \Inc(B)=B,
201	\]
202	whereas every map into $B_4=\{F,T\}$ must return one of the two Boolean poles.
203	Thus classicalization loses states and operations that are native to the
204	calculation.  It cannot be an invertible change of description.
205	\end{proof}
206	
207	This distinction governs every later section.  Transport without
208	ring-identification, controlled indeterminacy, simultaneous graph predicates,
209	the $t,f$ information layer, filtration position, and phase-bearing observables
210	are native data.  None is introduced as commentary on an underlying Boolean
211	calculation.
212	
213	\section{Basic maps on the full state space}
214	\label{sec:basic-maps}
215	
216	Let
217	\[
218	\mathcal X=\mathcal P(\{T,F,t,f\}).
219	\]
220	No special syntax is required.  The construction uses ordinary maps between
221	copies of $\mathcal X$ and, where a retained invariant must be carried, an
222	enriched space $\widehat{\mathcal X}=\mathcal X\times K$ for a suitable record
223	space $K$.
224	
225	Define the involution
226	\[
227	\nu:\mathcal X\to\mathcal X,
228	\qquad
229	\nu(X)=\{\sigma(a):a\in X\},
230	\]
231	where
232	\[
233	\sigma(T)=F,\qquad \sigma(F)=T,
234	\qquad \sigma(t)=f,\qquad \sigma(f)=t.
235	\]
236	The two support projections are
237	\[
238	\pi_T(X)=X\cap\{T,t\},
239	\qquad
240	\pi_F(X)=X\cap\{F,f\}.
241	\]
242	The information extension is
243	\[
244	\eta(X)=X\cup\{t,f\}.
245	\]
246	For $n\ge 2$, recombination is union:
247	\[
248	\mu_n(X_1,\ldots,X_n)=\bigcup_{j=1}^n X_j.
249	\]
250	The two decompositions used explicitly below are
251	\[
252	\delta_2(X)=\bigl(X\cap\{T,t\},\;X\cap\{F,f\}\bigr)
253	\]
254	and
255	\[
256	\delta_3(X)=\bigl(X\cap\{T\},\;X\cap\{t,f\},\;X\cap\{F\}\bigr).
257	\]
258	The order of the three components is fixed throughout:
259	\[
260	[T]\;|\;[t,f]\;|\;[F].
261	\]
262	Thus the $\{t,f\}$ component is the middle arm.  This is the natural diagrammatic
263	placement when the ambient contradictory state is $B=\{T,F\}$: the information
264	arm lies between the two classical flanks rather than appearing as an auxiliary
265	side channel.
266	
267	Context-dependent arithmetic transformations are denoted by ordinary maps
268	\[
269	f,\ell:\mathcal X\to\mathcal X.
270	\]
271	When an additional invariant must be retained, introduce an enriched state
272	space
273	\[
274	\widehat{\mathcal X}=\mathcal X\times K
275	\]
276	and a record update
277	\[
278	\kappa(X,k)=\bigl(X,\Phi(X,k)\bigr).
279	\]
280	Thus
281	\[
282	\operatorname{pr}_{\mathcal X}\circ\kappa
283	=\operatorname{pr}_{\mathcal X};
284	\]
285	the visible carrier value is unchanged while the $K$-component records the
286	invariant.  Fix a reference record $k_0\in K$ and write
287	\[
288	\iota(X)=(X,k_0).
289	\]
290	The final arithmetic quantity is obtained only after the carrier computation,
291	by an ordinary functional
292	\[
293	h:\mathcal X\longrightarrow \mathbb R\cup\{\infty\}.
294	\]
295	
296	\subsection{Decomposition and recombination}
297	
298	For the decompositions above,
299	\[
300	\mu_2\circ\delta_2=\operatorname{id}_{\mathcal X},
301	\qquad
302	\mu_3\circ\delta_3=\operatorname{id}_{\mathcal X}.
303	\]
304	The relevant configuration is not an empty decomposition immediately followed
305	by recombination, but
306	\[
307	X\xrightarrow{\delta_n}(X_1,\ldots,X_n)
308	\xrightarrow{g_1\times\cdots\times g_n}
309	(Y_1,\ldots,Y_n)
310	\xrightarrow{\mu_n}\bigcup_{j=1}^nY_j,
311	\]
312	with genuine branchwise work between $\delta_n$ and $\mu_n$.  Recoverability
313	therefore means recovery after asymmetric transformation, not equality of the
314	intermediate branches.
315	
316	\begin{figure}[htbp]
317	\centering
318	\begin{tikzpicture}[node distance=14mm and 17mm]
319	  \node[pcnode] (x) {$X$};
320	  \node[pcnode,right=of x] (split) {$\delta_3$};
321	  \node[pcnode,above right=8mm and 17mm of split] (aT) {$g_T(X_T)$};
322	  \node[pcnode,right=17mm of split,draw=pcblue,line width=1pt] (aI) {$g_I(X_I)$};
323	  \node[pcnode,below right=8mm and 17mm of split] (aF) {$g_F(X_F)$};
324	  \node[pcnode,right=37mm of split] (fuse) {$\mu_3$};
325	  \node[pcnode,right=of fuse] (xr) {$X'$};
326	  \draw[pcarrow] (x)--(split);
327	  \draw[pctheta] (split)-- node[above left,font=\scriptsize] {$T$} (aT);
328	  \draw[pcinfo] (split)-- node[above,font=\scriptsize] {$t,f$} (aI);
329	  \draw[pcwarn] (split)-- node[below left,font=\scriptsize] {$F$} (aF);
330	  \draw[pctheta] (aT)--(fuse); \draw[pcinfo] (aI)--(fuse); \draw[pcwarn] (aF)--(fuse);
331	  \draw[pcarrow] (fuse)--(xr);
332	  \node[font=\small,align=center,text width=11.2cm,below=19mm of fuse]
333	    {$\mu_3\circ\delta_3=\operatorname{id}$ on information-preserving arms; the middle $\{t,f\}$ component is empty on the classical slice, not removed from the decomposition.};
334	\end{tikzpicture}
335	\caption{Conventional branch diagram for decomposition, asymmetric work, and recombination.  The $\{t,f\}$ component is the middle arm.}
336	\label{fig:dyad}
337	\end{figure}
338	
339	If the construction is represented by a directed graph $G=(V,E)$, the matching
340	between a decomposition vertex and a later recombination vertex is determined
341	by directed ancestry: all incoming branches of the recombination must descend
342	from the same decomposition.  Thus closure is a graph-theoretic property of
343	$E$, not a property of the printed order of formulas.
344	
345	\subsection{The sixteen states}
346	
347	Every state is a subset of $\{T,F,t,f\}$.  Hence $\mathcal X$ has sixteen
348	values.  The four states with no $t$ or $f$ atoms are
349	\[
350	N=\varnothing,\qquad T=\{T\},\qquad F=\{F\},\qquad B=\{T,F\}.
351	\]
352	Values containing $t$ or $f$ are not projected back into this four-state
353	subspace unless a separate classicalization map is explicitly applied.
354	The information order is ordinary inclusion,
355	\[
356	X\le_iY\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad X\subseteq Y.
357	\]
358	Accordingly, information may accumulate without requiring a classical
359	resolution of contradictory support.
360	
361	\section{FOUR inside the full carrier}
362	
363	The full carrier contains the Belnap--Dunn FOUR slice
364	\[
365	\FOUR=\{N,T,F,B\},
366	\]
367	where $N$ carries neither truth nor falsity, $T$ carries truth only, $F$ carries
368	falsity only, and $B$ carries both.  Negation fixes the two nonclassical states,
369	\[
370	\neg N=N,\qquad \neg B=B,
371	\]
372	and exchanges the classical poles $T$ and $F$.  The crucial point is not simply
373	that FOUR has two additional labels.  It allows incompatible information to
374	remain present without identifying that state with arbitrary consequence
375	\cite{belnap,dunn,uno}.
376	
377	The information order is
378	\[
379	N <_{i} T <_{i} B,
380	\qquad
381	N <_{i} F <_{i} B,
382	\]
383	with $T$ and $F$ incomparable.  The truth order is
384	\[
385	F <_{t} N <_{t} T,
386	\qquad
387	F <_{t} B <_{t} T,
388	\]
389	with $N$ and $B$ incomparable.  The same carrier therefore supports different
390	motions without forcing one motion to erase the others.  Contradiction is the
391	top of information, not a detonation command.
392	
393	
394	\begin{figure}[htbp]
395	\centering
396	\begin{tikzpicture}[x=1cm,y=1cm,scale=0.9,transform shape]
397	  \begin{scope}[xshift=-3.7cm]
398	    \node[font=\bfseries] at (0,2.7) {truth order $\le_t$};
399	    \node[pcstate] (tT) at (0,2) {$T$};
400	    \node[pcstate] (tN) at (-1,1) {$N$};
401	    \node[pcstate] (tB) at (1,1) {$B$};
402	    \node[pcstate] (tF) at (0,0) {$F$};
403	    \draw[pcarrow] (tF)--(tN); \draw[pcarrow] (tF)--(tB);
404	    \draw[pcarrow] (tN)--(tT); \draw[pcarrow] (tB)--(tT);
405	  \end{scope}
406	  \begin{scope}[xshift=3.7cm]
407	    \node[font=\bfseries] at (0,2.7) {information order $\le_i$};
408	    \node[pcstate,draw=pcred,line width=1pt] (iB) at (0,2) {$B$};
409	    \node[pcstate] (iT) at (-1,1) {$T$};
410	    \node[pcstate] (iF) at (1,1) {$F$};
411	    \node[pcstate] (iN) at (0,0) {$N$};
412	    \draw[pcinfo] (iN)--(iT); \draw[pcinfo] (iN)--(iF);

438	\subsection{The Boolean shore is internal and lossy}
439	
440	Inside FOUR sits the two-element Boolean core
441	\[
442	B_4=\{F,T\}\subsetneq\FOUR.
443	\]
444	The inclusion $i:B_4\hookrightarrow\FOUR$ has, in the truth order, two canonical
445	adjoints \cite{uno}.  The reflector
446	\[
447	r:\FOUR\to B_4,
448	\qquad
449	r(F)=F,\quad r(T)=T,\quad r(N)=r(B)=T,
450	\]
451	obeys $r\dashv i$.  The coreflector
452	\[
453	c:\FOUR\to B_4,
454	\qquad
455	c(F)=F,\quad c(T)=T,\quad c(N)=c(B)=F,
456	\]
457	obeys $i\dashv c$.  Both are retractions on the Boolean image,
458	\[
459	r\circ i=\operatorname{id}_{B_4},
460	\qquad
461	c\circ i=\operatorname{id}_{B_4},
462	\]
463	but they disagree precisely where the full carrier contains information that the
464	Boolean core excludes.
465	
466	Beside them is the paraconsistent closure
467	\[
468	\Inc:\FOUR\to\FOUR,
469	\qquad
470	\Inc(v)=B.
471	\]
472	It is extensive, monotone, and idempotent in the information order, and
473	\[
474	\Inc(B)=B.
475	\]
476	The three actions on contradiction are therefore
477	\[
478	B\xmapsto{r}T,
479	\qquad
480	B\xmapsto{c}F,
481	\qquad
482	B\xmapsto{\Inc}B.
483	\]
484	The first two do not retain contradiction.  They delete it in opposite
485	directions.

507	\begin{theorem}[Boolean inexpressibility of the contradictory fixed point]
508	There is no endomap $f:B_4\to B_4$ satisfying
509	\[
510	i\circ f=\Inc\circ i.
511	\]
512	Equivalently, no operation internal to the Boolean core reproduces the
513	paraconsistent closure through the inclusion.
514	\end{theorem}
515	
516	\begin{proof}
517	For any $x\in B_4$, one has $\Inc(i(x))=B$.  But $i(f(x))$ lies in
518	$\{F,T\}$, so $i(f(x))\neq B$.  Hence the square cannot commute.
519	\end{proof}

521	This is why the Boolean restriction is unusable wherever the
522	contradiction-bearing state participates in the construction.  It is
523	unsuitable as a carrier because $B\notin B_4$; unsuitable as a transport space
524	because a map into $B_4$ must discard $B$; unsuitable as a closure space because
525	$\Inc$ cannot factor through it; unsuitable as a record of indeterminacy because
526	$N$ and $B$ are exactly the values it excludes; and unsuitable as a faithful
527	readout because $r$ and $c$ replace one full-carrier state by opposite classical
528	poles.  The Boolean world is not a competing sea.  It is an island cut out of
529	the sea by restriction and retraction.

531	\section{IUT: incompatible transport retained}
532	
533	IUT begins with initial $\Theta$-data attached to an elliptic curve over a number
534	field and constructs Hodge theaters carrying arithmetic and geometric data
535	\cite{iut1}.  The point relevant here is the relation between theaters.  The
536	$\Theta$-link relates Frobenioid-theoretic portions of one theater to another in
537	a manner that is deliberately not compatible with the respective ring/scheme
538	structures.  The ring structures on the two sides are not transported as one
539	ring structure.  The theory works instead with what it calls an \emph{alien ring
540	structure}: one side is described from the standpoint of a structure that is not
541	its own.
542	
543	That is already a paraconsistent situation.  The link does not need to say that
544	one ring structure is secretly the other.  It needs to retain enough of both for
545	a meaningful comparison to survive their incompatibility.  The information is
546	therefore not exhausted by either classical pole.  If one insists that every
547	carrier state be reduced to exactly $T$ or exactly $F$, the alien part of the
548	alien ring structure has been removed before the transport runs.
549	
550	The same pattern persists in the three indeterminacies.  They are not a temporary
551	failure to identify the unique classical object that ``really'' exists.  They
552	are controlled latitude in the transport itself.  Some data are retained only
553	up to automorphism, unit action, or upper semi-compatibility.  The relevant
554	question is consequently not ``which side wins?'' but ``what is invariant while
555	incompatible or incomplete determinations remain live?''  That is the ordinary
556	question of a paraconsistent information order.
557	
558	The familiar cartoon of the alien ring structure makes the point sharply.  Take
559	two copies $\mathbb R_0$ and $\mathbb R_1$ and glue them by a bijection that is
560	not a ring homomorphism.  The underlying sets can be put into correspondence
561	without transporting the ring operations.  Describing algebraic information
562	from one copy using the ring structure of the other requires both structures to
563	remain present while their incompatibility is not erased.  The $\Theta$-link is
564	not this cartoon, but the cartoon isolates its relevant logical shape: relation
565	without ring-identification.

667	\section{Indeterminacy without erasure}
668	
669	IUT's three indeterminacies are often described as the price paid for comparing
670	objects across alien structures.  They delimit the live
671	variation directly: they delimit which information is fixed and which information is
672	allowed to vary without destroying the transport.
673	
674	An underdetermined state has the shape of $N$: neither classical determination
675	has yet been supplied.  An overdetermined state has the shape of $B$: both are
676	present.  These need not be globally assigned labels once and for all.  The same
677	construction can move through regions of incompleteness and regions of
678	inconsistency.  The important invariant is that neither state triggers
679	explosion, so local indeterminacy does not license arbitrary conclusions about
680	unrelated parts of the graph.
681	
682	This is why the classical restriction is not merely inconvenient.  Its two
683	canonical collapse maps identify both $N$ and $B$ with a classical pole:
684	\[
685	r(N)=r(B)=T,
686	\qquad
687	c(N)=c(B)=F.
688	\]
689	Thus incompleteness and inconsistency become indistinguishable after either
690	collapse.  IUT, by contrast, repeatedly depends on knowing what survives under a
691	specified indeterminacy.  A carrier restriction that erases the distinction between
692	``not yet determined'' and ``jointly but incompatibly determined'' cannot serve
693	as the carrier for that bookkeeping.
694	
695	\section{Conjugate synchronization as preserved multiplicity}
696	
697	Conjugate synchronization aligns copies of the local Galois group across labels
698	so that theta evaluation can be made without introducing the conjugacy
699	indeterminacy that would otherwise obstruct the comparison.  It does not make
700	the labels one label.  It makes a family jointly readable while preserving the
701	fact that it is a family.
702	
703	Synchronization retains multiplicity.  It does not require the
704	carrier to contract all copies to one classical representative.  It requires a
705	common relation that can be carried across several simultaneously present
706	copies.  In carrier language the useful state is therefore not ``one lane has
707	won'' but ``the lanes have acquired a common image.''  The all-lane state $A$
708	is an extreme example of that phenomenon: every base atom is present in one
709	carrier state without that state becoming trivial.
710	
711	The distinction matters because $A$ is not the statement that every proposition
712	is derivable.  It is one value of one carrier at one point in one graph.  Local
713	saturation of information is not global logical explosion.
714	
715	\section{Frobenius-like and \texorpdfstring{\'etale}{etale}-like motion}
716	
717	IUT repeatedly contrasts Frobenius-like, order-conscious constructions with
718	\'etale-like structures in which certain ordering information has been forgotten
719	or made permutation-invariant \cite{iut1,iut2}.  The full carrier carries this contrast because the same carrier supports more than one
720	order.  Nothing requires us to identify a particular IUT axis once and for all
721	with a particular lattice order.  The stronger and safer claim is structural:
722	IUT needs simultaneous order-sensitive and order-insensitive descriptions of
723	related data, while a bilattice/trilattice carrier is built precisely to let one
724	state participate in several orderings without being duplicated into separate
725	worlds.
726	
727	This matters for the $\Theta$-link and Log-link.  A horizontal or vertical move
728	in the log-theta-lattice changes what is being transported or forgotten, but it
729	does not require a new logical universe.  The same value can be compared under another
730	order without leaving the carrier.  The noncommutativity of
731	moves is then allowed to remain noncommutative.  There is no requirement that two
732	paths through the lattice collapse to a single Boolean equality before the
733	result can be meaningful.
734	
735	\section{Paper I: the theater is already non-Boolean}
736	
737	Paper I constructs the Hodge theaters and the links among them \cite{iut1}.  Its
738	central act is not the production of a globally shared ring structure.  It is
739	the controlled passage among structures after precisely such a shared ring
740	structure has been relinquished.
741	
742	The geometric and arithmetic symmetries of the labels coexist inside a theater.
743	The $\Theta$-link then passes from one theater to another through structures that
744	are sufficiently stripped of ring rigidity to admit the link.  What survives is
745	not an equality of ringed spaces but a package of invariants that can be
746	recognized on both sides.  The alien ring structure is therefore not an
747	exception occurring after a classical construction.  It is the condition that
748	makes the inter-universal movement possible.
749	
750	Paper I establishes a carrier large enough for mutually
751	alien determinations to remain simultaneously addressable.  The mono-analytic
752	core is valuable not because it secretly reconstructs one common classical
753	ring, but because it identifies content that survives when the surrounding ring
754	structures do not coincide.  This is the same informational logic expressed by
755	FOUR: keep the information that is jointly supported, keep track of what is
756	missing or incompatible, and do not infer everything from the incompatibility.
757	
758	\subsection{Chains of theaters}
759	
760	The chain of $\Theta$-Hodge theaters is especially clear in this execution.  Each
761	link is a transport step whose admissibility depends on forgetting enough local
762	structure to move and retaining enough invariant structure to recognize the
763	result.  The chain does not become meaningful by restoring a single global ring
764	at every step.  It becomes meaningful because each step has a controlled
765	interface.
766	
767	This is exactly the role of unfilled ports in a directed graph.  An unfilled port is not an
768	error; it is a living end, a place where another component can bind.  A theater
769	that exposes only the structure needed for the next link behaves like a
770	component with a typed living end.  Completion is not demanded prematurely.
771	
772	\section{Paper II: evaluation across alien descriptions}
773	
774	Paper II develops the Hodge--Arakelov-theoretic evaluation and the Kummer theory
775	relating Frobenius-like and Galois-theoretic forms of the theta data
776	\cite{iut2}.  The crucial operation is not the elimination of multiplicity but
777	the ability to evaluate coherently across it.
778	
779	Multiradiality is an information-preserving change
780	of viewpoint.  A uniradial description is tied to one spoke; a multiradial
781	description can speak from several spokes.  What must remain fixed is the coric
782	content that survives these shifts.  The indeterminacies specify which changes
783	of representation are tolerated.  They do not designate noise to be thrown
784	away.
785	
786	Cyclotomic, discrete, and constant-multiple rigidities are useful precisely
787	because they survive the admissible spread.  A rigidity is an invariant under
788	the relevant movement.  In the carrier, there is content
789	that survives even while other atoms are added, swapped, projected, or held in
790	contradictory combination.  Information growth around an invariant is not the
791	same as loss of the invariant.
792	
793	The Gaussian Frobenioid constructions sharpen the point.  The theory can pass
794	between Frobenius-like and \`etale-like presentations of theta values without
795	requiring the two presentations to be literally identical structures.  Their
796	relation is carried by Kummer theory and the stated invariants.  The carrier retains the relation itself, not merely its two endpoints.

\title{\bfseries Inter-Universal Teichm\"uller Theory\\\large A Paraconsistent Formulation in Conventional Mathematical Notation}
\author{Lando Mills}
\date{}

\begin{document}
\maketitle

\begin{abstract}
The construction is formulated on the sixteen-state space
\[
\mathcal X=\mathcal P(\{T,F,t,f\}),
\]
with a non-explosive consequence relation.  This is a rebase of the logical
substrate, not a reinterpretation of a prior Boolean construction.  The
Belnap--Dunn four-state system is the $t,f$-free subspace of $\mathcal X$, and
$\{F,T\}$ is a further lossy restriction.

The mathematical operations needed below are ordinary maps on this state
space and on enriched spaces built over it: projections $\pi_T,\pi_F$, the
involution $\nu$, decompositions $\delta_n$, recombinations $\mu_n$, an
information extension $\eta$, context maps $f$ and $\ell$, a fixation map
$\kappa$, and a terminal scalar functional $h$.  Inter-Universal Teichm\"uller Theory is
then described by compositions and branch diagrams built from these maps.
The $\Theta$-link transports arithmetic data without identifying the ring
structures on its two sides; the log-$\Theta$ construction retains filtration
position; and the bounded-discrepancy calculation terminates at
\[
Ftf=\{F,t,f\}
\]
while its reconnection condition holds.  Cyclic phase is represented by the
standard action of $C_{12}$ on a twelve-position presentation.  Scholze--Stix
obtain a vacuous scalar inequality only after suppressing the filtration index
carrying the $j^2$ weights.  Mochizuki correctly rejects their commuting-loop
surrogate, but the stronger point is that local incompatibility is admissible
and non-explosive once locality and filtration position have been retained.
Classicalization therefore occurs only as a downstream projection of the
calculation.
\end{abstract}

\section{Rebasing the logical substrate}
\label{sec:rebasing}

The logical base used in this paper is constitutive.  It is not an optional
semantic gloss on a construction that is first completed in a classical
two-valued universe.

A \emph{reinterpretation} leaves the underlying consequence relation and
admissible carrier unchanged and assigns a new description to objects already
formed there.  That is not the operation performed here.  The present
construction is \emph{rebased}: formulas, graph states, closure predicates,
contradictory states, filtrations, cyclic phases, and terminal readouts are
formed directly in the non-explosive carrier and are governed from the outset
by its consequence relation.

Concretely, the base is
\[
  \mathcal X=\mathcal P(\{T,F,t,f\}),
\]
together with the directed graph operations introduced below and a consequence
relation for which local contradiction does not entail an arbitrary conclusion:
\[
  p,\neg p\nvdash q
\]
for unrelated $q$.  States such as
\[
  A=\{T,F,t,f\},
  \qquad
  Ftf=\{F,t,f\},
\]
are therefore values of the calculation itself.  They are not annotations
attached after a classical computation has already finished.

The Boolean pair
\[
  B_4=\{F,T\}
\]
appears only as a proper downstream restriction.  Classicalization is a map
\[
  \clproj:\mathcal X\longrightarrow B_4
\]
that forgets carrier information.  Hence the logical direction of the paper is
\[
  \boxed{\text{full nonclassical calculation}}
  \;\longrightarrow\;
  \boxed{\text{downstream Boolean shadow}},
\]
never the reverse.  In particular, a scalar terminal inequality may lie in a
classical codomain without implying that the calculation which produced it was
classical.

\label{fig:rebase-direction}

\begin{proposition}[The rebase is not a re-description]
The full carrier and the Boolean restriction are not equivalent descriptions
of the same logical state space.  In particular, the classicalization map
$\clproj:\mathcal X\to B_4$ is non-injective and cannot preserve the
contradictory fixed point as a Boolean state.
\end{proposition}

\begin{proof}
Distinct full-carrier states have the same Boolean shadow; for example,
\[
  \clproj(\{F\})=\clproj(\{F,t,f\})=F.
\]
Moreover the contradictory state $B=\{T,F\}$ is fixed by information closure,
\[
  \Inc(B)=B,
\]
whereas every map into $B_4=\{F,T\}$ must return one of the two Boolean poles.
Thus classicalization loses states and operations that are native to the
calculation.  It cannot be an invertible change of description.
\end{proof}

This distinction governs every later section.  Transport without
ring-identification, controlled indeterminacy, simultaneous graph predicates,
the $t,f$ information layer, filtration position, and phase-bearing observables
are native data.  None is introduced as commentary on an underlying Boolean
calculation.

\section{Basic maps on the full state space}
\label{sec:basic-maps}

Let
\[
\mathcal X=\mathcal P(\{T,F,t,f\}).
\]
No special syntax is required.  The construction uses ordinary maps between
copies of $\mathcal X$ and, where a retained invariant must be carried, an
enriched space $\widehat{\mathcal X}=\mathcal X\times K$ for a suitable record
space $K$.

Define the involution
\[
\nu:\mathcal X\to\mathcal X,
\qquad
\nu(X)=\{\sigma(a):a\in X\},
\]
where
\[
\sigma(T)=F,\qquad \sigma(F)=T,
\qquad \sigma(t)=f,\qquad \sigma(f)=t.
\]
The two support projections are
\[
\pi_T(X)=X\cap\{T,t\},
\qquad
\pi_F(X)=X\cap\{F,f\}.
\]
The information extension is
\[
\eta(X)=X\cup\{t,f\}.
\]
For $n\ge 2$, recombination is union:
\[
\mu_n(X_1,\ldots,X_n)=\bigcup_{j=1}^n X_j.
\]
The two decompositions used explicitly below are
\[
\delta_2(X)=\bigl(X\cap\{T,t\},\;X\cap\{F,f\}\bigr)
\]
and
\[
\delta_3(X)=\bigl(X\cap\{T\},\;X\cap\{t,f\},\;X\cap\{F\}\bigr).
\]
The order of the three components is fixed throughout:
\[
[T]\;|\;[t,f]\;|\;[F].
\]
Thus the $\{t,f\}$ component is the middle arm.  This is the natural diagrammatic
placement when the ambient contradictory state is $B=\{T,F\}$: the information
arm lies between the two classical flanks rather than appearing as an auxiliary
side channel.

Context-dependent arithmetic transformations are denoted by ordinary maps
\[
f,\ell:\mathcal X\to\mathcal X.
\]
When an additional invariant must be retained, introduce an enriched state
space
\[
\widehat{\mathcal X}=\mathcal X\times K
\]
and a record update
\[
\kappa(X,k)=\bigl(X,\Phi(X,k)\bigr).
\]
Thus
\[
\operatorname{pr}_{\mathcal X}\circ\kappa
=\operatorname{pr}_{\mathcal X};
\]
the visible carrier value is unchanged while the $K$-component records the
invariant.  Fix a reference record $k_0\in K$ and write
\[
\iota(X)=(X,k_0).
\]
The final arithmetic quantity is obtained only after the carrier computation,
by an ordinary functional
\[
h:\mathcal X\longrightarrow \mathbb R\cup\{\infty\}.
\]

\subsection{Decomposition and recombination}

For the decompositions above,
\[
\mu_2\circ\delta_2=\operatorname{id}_{\mathcal X},
\qquad
\mu_3\circ\delta_3=\operatorname{id}_{\mathcal X}.
\]
The relevant configuration is not an empty decomposition immediately followed
by recombination, but
\[
X\xrightarrow{\delta_n}(X_1,\ldots,X_n)
\xrightarrow{g_1\times\cdots\times g_n}
(Y_1,\ldots,Y_n)
\xrightarrow{\mu_n}\bigcup_{j=1}^nY_j,
\]
with genuine branchwise work between $\delta_n$ and $\mu_n$.  Recoverability
therefore means recovery after asymmetric transformation, not equality of the
intermediate branches.

If the construction is represented by a directed graph $G=(V,E)$, the matching
between a decomposition vertex and a later recombination vertex is determined
by directed ancestry: all incoming branches of the recombination must descend
from the same decomposition.  Thus closure is a graph-theoretic property of
$E$, not a property of the printed order of formulas.

\subsection{The sixteen states}

Every state is a subset of $\{T,F,t,f\}$.  Hence $\mathcal X$ has sixteen
values.  The four states with no $t$ or $f$ atoms are
\[
N=\varnothing,\qquad T=\{T\},\qquad F=\{F\},\qquad B=\{T,F\}.
\]
Values containing $t$ or $f$ are not projected back into this four-state
subspace unless a separate classicalization map is explicitly applied.
The information order is ordinary inclusion,
\[
X\le_iY\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad X\subseteq Y.
\]
Accordingly, information may accumulate without requiring a classical
resolution of contradictory support.

\section{FOUR inside the full carrier}

The full carrier contains the Belnap--Dunn FOUR slice
\[
\FOUR=\{N,T,F,B\},
\]
where $N$ carries neither truth nor falsity, $T$ carries truth only, $F$ carries
falsity only, and $B$ carries both.  Negation fixes the two nonclassical states,
\[
\neg N=N,\qquad \neg B=B,
\]
and exchanges the classical poles $T$ and $F$.  The crucial point is not simply
that FOUR has two additional labels.  It allows incompatible information to
remain present without identifying that state with arbitrary consequence
\cite{belnap,dunn,uno}.

The information order is
\[
N <_{i} T <_{i} B,
\qquad
N <_{i} F <_{i} B,
\]
with $T$ and $F$ incomparable.  The truth order is
\[
F <_{t} N <_{t} T,
\qquad
F <_{t} B <_{t} T,
\]
with $N$ and $B$ incomparable.  The same carrier therefore supports different
motions without forcing one motion to erase the others.  Contradiction is the
top of information, not a detonation command.

\[

and consequently
\[
p,\neg p\nvdash q.
\]
The contradiction remains local to $p$.  Nothing in the simultaneous presence
of $p$ and $\neg p$ licenses an arbitrary $q$.  This local retention is the
logical condition under which an alien structure can be carried without
collapsing the rest of the construction.

\subsection{The Boolean shore is internal and lossy}

Inside FOUR sits the two-element Boolean core
\[
B_4=\{F,T\}\subsetneq\FOUR.
\]
The inclusion $i:B_4\hookrightarrow\FOUR$ has, in the truth order, two canonical
adjoints \cite{uno}.  The reflector
\[
r:\FOUR\to B_4,
\qquad
r(F)=F,\quad r(T)=T,\quad r(N)=r(B)=T,
\]
obeys $r\dashv i$.  The coreflector
\[
c:\FOUR\to B_4,
\qquad
c(F)=F,\quad c(T)=T,\quad c(N)=c(B)=F,
\]
obeys $i\dashv c$.  Both are retractions on the Boolean image,
\[
r\circ i=\operatorname{id}_{B_4},
\qquad
c\circ i=\operatorname{id}_{B_4},
\]
but they disagree precisely where the full carrier contains information that the
Boolean core excludes.

Beside them is the paraconsistent closure
\[
\Inc:\FOUR\to\FOUR,
\qquad
\Inc(v)=B.
\]
It is extensive, monotone, and idempotent in the information order, and
\[
\Inc(B)=B.
\]
The three actions on contradiction are therefore
\[
B\xmapsto{r}T,
\qquad
B\xmapsto{c}F,
\qquad
B\xmapsto{\Inc}B.
\]
The first two do not retain contradiction.  They delete it in opposite
directions.

\begin{theorem}[Boolean inexpressibility of the contradictory fixed point]
There is no endomap $f:B_4\to B_4$ satisfying
\[
i\circ f=\Inc\circ i.
\]
Equivalently, no operation internal to the Boolean core reproduces the
paraconsistent closure through the inclusion.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
For any $x\in B_4$, one has $\Inc(i(x))=B$.  But $i(f(x))$ lies in
$\{F,T\}$, so $i(f(x))\neq B$.  Hence the square cannot commute.
\end{proof}

This is why the Boolean restriction is unusable wherever the
contradiction-bearing state participates in the construction.  It is
unsuitable as a carrier because $B\notin B_4$; unsuitable as a transport space
because a map into $B_4$ must discard $B$; unsuitable as a closure space because
$\Inc$ cannot factor through it; unsuitable as a record of indeterminacy because
$N$ and $B$ are exactly the values it excludes; and unsuitable as a faithful
readout because $r$ and $c$ replace one full-carrier state by opposite classical
poles.  The Boolean world is not a competing sea.  It is an island cut out of
the sea by restriction and retraction.

\section{IUT: incompatible transport retained}

IUT begins with initial $\Theta$-data attached to an elliptic curve over a number
field and constructs Hodge theaters carrying arithmetic and geometric data
\cite{iut1}.  The point relevant here is the relation between theaters.  The
$\Theta$-link relates Frobenioid-theoretic portions of one theater to another in
a manner that is deliberately not compatible with the respective ring/scheme
structures.  The ring structures on the two sides are not transported as one
ring structure.  The theory works instead with what it calls an \emph{alien ring
structure}: one side is described from the standpoint of a structure that is not
its own.

That is already a paraconsistent situation.  The link does not need to say that
one ring structure is secretly the other.  It needs to retain enough of both for
a meaningful comparison to survive their incompatibility.  The information is
therefore not exhausted by either classical pole.  If one insists that every
carrier state be reduced to exactly $T$ or exactly $F$, the alien part of the
alien ring structure has been removed before the transport runs.

The same pattern persists in the three indeterminacies.  They are not a temporary
failure to identify the unique classical object that ``really'' exists.  They
are controlled latitude in the transport itself.  Some data are retained only
up to automorphism, unit action, or upper semi-compatibility.  The relevant
question is consequently not ``which side wins?'' but ``what is invariant while
incompatible or incomplete determinations remain live?''  That is the ordinary
question of a paraconsistent information order.

The familiar cartoon of the alien ring structure makes the point sharply.  Take
two copies $\mathbb R_0$ and $\mathbb R_1$ and glue them by a bijection that is
not a ring homomorphism.  The underlying sets can be put into correspondence
without transporting the ring operations.  Describing algebraic information
from one copy using the ring structure of the other requires both structures to
remain present while their incompatibility is not erased.  The $\Theta$-link is
not this cartoon, but the cartoon isolates its relevant logical shape: relation
without ring-identification.

\section{The \texorpdfstring{$\Theta$}{Theta}-link as a branchwise transport}
\label{sec:theta-conventional}

The supplied $\Theta$-link calculation can be written without an operator
inventory.  Let $X_0\in\mathcal X$ denote the incoming state and let
\[
(X_T,X_I,X_F)=\delta_3(X_0).
\]
The three components are transformed separately,
\[
Y_T=g_T(X_T),\qquad
Y_I=g_I(X_I),\qquad
Y_F=g_F(X_F),
\]
where the $T$ and $F$ branches carry the incompatible arithmetic
determinations and the middle branch carries the $t,f$ information component.
The transported state is then
\[
Y=\mu_3(Y_T,Y_I,Y_F).
\]
For the engaging calculation supplied with this paper, the terminal state is
\[
Y=A=\{T,F,t,f\}.
\]
The reconnection statement and the value of $Y$ answer different mathematical
questions: the first is a property of the branch diagram; the second is the
state carried by the completed transport.  They are simultaneous properties of
one construction.

Under the classical projection
\[
\pi_{\mathrm{cl}}(X)=X\cap\{T,F\},
\]
one obtains
\[
\pi_{\mathrm{cl}}(A)=\{T,F\}=B.
\]
The projection therefore deletes the middle information component while leaving
even the classical coordinates contradictory.

The transport does not choose one of the two incompatible arithmetic

\[
\eta(X)=X\cup\{t,f\}.
\]
Thus a reconnection condition may hold while the resulting state remains

\section{Indeterminacy without erasure}

IUT's three indeterminacies are often described as the price paid for comparing
objects across alien structures.  They delimit the live
variation directly: they delimit which information is fixed and which information is
allowed to vary without destroying the transport.

An underdetermined state has the shape of $N$: neither classical determination
has yet been supplied.  An overdetermined state has the shape of $B$: both are
present.  These need not be globally assigned labels once and for all.  The same
construction can move through regions of incompleteness and regions of
inconsistency.  The important invariant is that neither state triggers
explosion, so local indeterminacy does not license arbitrary conclusions about
unrelated parts of the graph.

This is why the classical restriction is not merely inconvenient.  Its two
canonical collapse maps identify both $N$ and $B$ with a classical pole:
\[
r(N)=r(B)=T,
\qquad
c(N)=c(B)=F.
\]
Thus incompleteness and inconsistency become indistinguishable after either
collapse.  IUT, by contrast, repeatedly depends on knowing what survives under a
specified indeterminacy.  A carrier restriction that erases the distinction between
``not yet determined'' and ``jointly but incompatibly determined'' cannot serve
as the carrier for that bookkeeping.

\section{Conjugate synchronization as preserved multiplicity}

Conjugate synchronization aligns copies of the local Galois group across labels
so that theta evaluation can be made without introducing the conjugacy
indeterminacy that would otherwise obstruct the comparison.  It does not make
the labels one label.  It makes a family jointly readable while preserving the
fact that it is a family.

Synchronization retains multiplicity.  It does not require the
carrier to contract all copies to one classical representative.  It requires a
common relation that can be carried across several simultaneously present
copies.  In carrier language the useful state is therefore not ``one lane has
won'' but ``the lanes have acquired a common image.''  The all-lane state $A$
is an extreme example of that phenomenon: every base atom is present in one
carrier state without that state becoming trivial.

The distinction matters because $A$ is not the statement that every proposition
is derivable.  It is one value of one carrier at one point in one graph.  Local
saturation of information is not global logical explosion.

\section{Frobenius-like and \texorpdfstring{\'etale}{etale}-like motion}

IUT repeatedly contrasts Frobenius-like, order-conscious constructions with
\'etale-like structures in which certain ordering information has been forgotten
or made permutation-invariant \cite{iut1,iut2}.  The full carrier carries this contrast because the same carrier supports more than one
order.  Nothing requires us to identify a particular IUT axis once and for all
with a particular lattice order.  The stronger and safer claim is structural:
IUT needs simultaneous order-sensitive and order-insensitive descriptions of
related data, while a bilattice/trilattice carrier is built precisely to let one
state participate in several orderings without being duplicated into separate
worlds.

This matters for the $\Theta$-link and Log-link.  A horizontal or vertical move
in the log-theta-lattice changes what is being transported or forgotten, but it
does not require a new logical universe.  The same value can be compared under another
order without leaving the carrier.  The noncommutativity of
moves is then allowed to remain noncommutative.  There is no requirement that two
paths through the lattice collapse to a single Boolean equality before the
result can be meaningful.

\section{Paper I: the theater is already non-Boolean}

Paper I constructs the Hodge theaters and the links among them \cite{iut1}.  Its
central act is not the production of a globally shared ring structure.  It is
the controlled passage among structures after precisely such a shared ring
structure has been relinquished.

The geometric and arithmetic symmetries of the labels coexist inside a theater.
The $\Theta$-link then passes from one theater to another through structures that
are sufficiently stripped of ring rigidity to admit the link.  What survives is
not an equality of ringed spaces but a package of invariants that can be
recognized on both sides.  The alien ring structure is therefore not an
exception occurring after a classical construction.  It is the condition that
makes the inter-universal movement possible.

Paper I establishes a carrier large enough for mutually
alien determinations to remain simultaneously addressable.  The mono-analytic
core is valuable not because it secretly reconstructs one common classical
ring, but because it identifies content that survives when the surrounding ring
structures do not coincide.  This is the same informational logic expressed by
FOUR: keep the information that is jointly supported, keep track of what is
missing or incompatible, and do not infer everything from the incompatibility.

\subsection{Chains of theaters}

The chain of $\Theta$-Hodge theaters is especially clear in this execution.  Each
link is a transport step whose admissibility depends on forgetting enough local
structure to move and retaining enough invariant structure to recognize the
result.  The chain does not become meaningful by restoring a single global ring
at every step.  It becomes meaningful because each step has a controlled
interface.

This is exactly the role of unfilled ports in a directed graph.  An unfilled port is not an
error; it is a living end, a place where another component can bind.  A theater
that exposes only the structure needed for the next link behaves like a
component with a typed living end.  Completion is not demanded prematurely.

\section{Paper II: evaluation across alien descriptions}

Paper II develops the Hodge--Arakelov-theoretic evaluation and the Kummer theory
relating Frobenius-like and Galois-theoretic forms of the theta data
\cite{iut2}.  The crucial operation is not the elimination of multiplicity but
the ability to evaluate coherently across it.

Multiradiality is an information-preserving change
of viewpoint.  A uniradial description is tied to one spoke; a multiradial
description can speak from several spokes.  What must remain fixed is the coric
content that survives these shifts.  The indeterminacies specify which changes
of representation are tolerated.  They do not designate noise to be thrown
away.

Cyclotomic, discrete, and constant-multiple rigidities are useful precisely
because they survive the admissible spread.  A rigidity is an invariant under
the relevant movement.  In the carrier, there is content
that survives even while other atoms are added, swapped, projected, or held in
contradictory combination.  Information growth around an invariant is not the
same as loss of the invariant.

The Gaussian Frobenioid constructions sharpen the point.  The theory can pass
between Frobenius-like and \`etale-like presentations of theta values without
requiring the two presentations to be literally identical structures.  Their
relation is carried by Kummer theory and the stated invariants.  The carrier retains the relation itself, not merely its two endpoints.

\section{Paper III: the log-theta-lattice in motion}

Paper III makes the multidirectional character of the construction explicit in
the log-theta-lattice \cite{iut3}.  Horizontal and vertical transports coexist.
The log-link and the theta-related links do not need to commute into one classical
identity to be usable.  Their difference is part of the geometry of the lattice.

arising from distinct sides of the relevant correspondence can be held together.
Containment is therefore primitive.  Equality is a special case, not the only

information order $\subseteq$ on the sixteen-state carrier: one state may
contain another without being equal to it, and additional information can be
present without invalidating what was already present.

The upper semi-compatibility of the log-Kummer correspondence has that
direction.  The relation is one-sided where equality would demand too much.
The Boolean restriction has no state
for the distinction between exact coincidence and a controlled containment that
retains extra information.  The full carrier does.

The three indeterminacies of the multiradial logarithmic Gaussian procession
monoids then become operational rather than apologetic.  They delimit an orbit
of admissible descriptions.  An invariant is something that survives that orbit.
The construction asks what can be transported throughout the orbit, not which
representative should be canonized as the one classically true object.

\section{Paper IV: bounded discrepancy as executable geometry}

Paper IV brings the accumulated transport to log-volume estimates and the
bounded-discrepancy inequality \cite{iut4}.  A representative form is
\[
\mathrm{ht}_{\omega_X(D)}
\;\lesssim\;
(1+\epsilon)
\bigl(\log\text{-}\mathrm{diff}_X+\log\text{-}\mathrm{cond}_D\bigr).
\]
The output is an inequality with bounded discrepancy rather than an identity.
The construction does not claim that every inequality is paraconsistent or
that the analytic estimate can be derived from FOUR.  The relevant point is more
specific: the IUT construction reaches its arithmetic conclusion after a long
sequence in which equality of alien structures was never required.  The terminal
bound is produced after a computation whose fundamental comparison is ordered
containment rather than forced identity.

The supplied calculation for ``the inequality of bounded discrepancy classes''
turns this structural claim into a concrete directed graph.

\xrightarrow{f}T
\xrightarrow{\pi_T}T
\xrightarrow{\nu}N

This line is a projection of the execution onto the visible carrier state.  In
particular, the arrow labelled $\mu_3$ suppresses the underlying three inputs to
recombination, and the arrow labelled $\kappa$ suppresses the auxiliary
$K$-component.  It should therefore not be read as a claim that $\mu_3$ is
unary or that $\kappa$ acts only on $\mathcal X$.

The two-arm diagram in Figure~\ref{fig:bd-circuit} and this three-arm register
trace record different aspects of the supplied calculation.  The former shows

Thus the terminal carrier state is
\[

The literal projection to the classical slice gives

\]

information-layer atoms.  The calculation has not ended in classical falsity.  It has
ended in a strictly richer state whose classical shadow is falsity.

whole state is replaced by $F$, the $t,f$ content that records the engaged
information layer disappears.  The terminal carrier state therefore provides a concrete
example of the general theorem above: a Boolean image can be computed, but the

1179	\section{From the \texorpdfstring{$\Theta$}{Theta}-link to bounded discrepancy}

1191	\text{source}&\longrightarrow\text{split}\longrightarrow\text{asymmetric work}
1192	\longrightarrow\text{engagement}\\
1193	&\longrightarrow\text{fixation}\longrightarrow\text{fuse}\longrightarrow\text{readout}.

1197	$\{F,T\}$.  Indeed, the extension $\eta$ is specifically an operation whose purpose is

1199	operation's result in order to remain classical.

1202	structures, preserves specified invariants across controlled indeterminacy, and
1203	terminates in an ordered arithmetic bound.  In conventional notation this act is: decompose the object,
1204	let the arms acquire asymmetric information, rejoin them, retain the
1205	contradictory/nonclassical content, and read out a bound-bearing state.

1207	\section{Why the final inequality is not a return to classicality}
1208

1210	the construction has finally returned to a Boolean restriction.  A numerical
1211	inequality can be the readout of a nonclassical computation.  The codomain of the
1212	last scalar estimate does not retroactively determine the carrier of
1213	the transformations that produced it.
1214	
1215	This is already visible in the bounded-discrepancy calculation.  The terminal readout is the
1216	``logarithmic bound,'' yet the carrier state at that anchor is $Ftf$, not $T$ or $F$.
1217	The graph can therefore end at a perfectly definite inequality while retaining
1218	non-Boolean information about how that inequality was obtained.
1219

1221	inter-universal transport preceding it can be represented inside the Boolean
1222	restriction.  The final bound is a scalar shadow of a richer construction.  The
1223	shadow can be classical even when the carrier that casts it is not.

1228	of the theory \cite{iut4}.  A species gives formulas that determine a category in
1229	different realizations; mutations transport the presentation; cores are
1230	what survive the mutation.  The emphasis is again on invariance across changes
1231	of realization rather than identity of all realization-level presentations.

1235	transformations remain meaningful.  This variation of realization does not

1237	non-explosive consequence relation and the same full carrier; realization
1238	independence is therefore not permission to return to a Boolean foundation.  Its type is carried by organized relations,

1443	\subsection{A formal model of downstream Boolean projection}
1444	\label{subsec:ss-gatecheck}
1445	
1446	The supplied Lean model named
1447	\texttt{ScholzeStixBooleanProjectionAtO2} does not begin with a two-state
1448	calculation.  Its internal construction contains distinct truth and falsity
1449	restrictions, an explicit both-valued information step, reversal, recombination,
1450	and fixation before the terminal boundary.  In conventional notation the
1451	relevant direction is therefore
1452	\[
1453	\mathcal X
1454	\xrightarrow{\;\text{nonclassical maps}\;}
1455	\mathcal X
1456	\xrightarrow{\;\pi_{\mathrm{cl}}\;}
1457	\{F,T\},
1458	\]
1459	not a Boolean calculation followed by a nonclassical re-description.
1460	
1461	The same file proves the ground-level identity
1462	\[
1463	\mu(x,x)=x.
1464	\]
1465	This formal model is not a formalization of the Scholze--Stix manuscript, so it
1466	cannot by itself decide their historical objection.  Its value here is narrower:
1467	it exhibits Boolean projection and recoverability as downstream operations on a
1468	richer typed object.
1469	
1470	\subsection{Mochizuki's reply, and where it stops short}
1471	\label{subsec:mochizuki-ss}
1472	
1473	Mochizuki's published response correctly identifies a real defect in the
1474	Scholze--Stix surrogate diagram.  In his comments on their manuscript he states
1475	that the proof of IUT III, Corollary 3.12 does not require the simultaneous
1476	identification of the various copies of $\mathbb R$, does not identify the
1477	$\Theta$- and $q$-side scalar objects in the manner drawn by Scholze--Stix, and
1478	does not contain the commuting loop on which their monodromy argument is based
1479	\cite{mochizukiCmt2018}.  His report on the March discussions makes the same
1480	point geometrically: identifying the two endpoints of a segment creates a loop,
1481	and the incompatibility of the $\Theta$-link with arithmetic degree may then
1482	appear as nontrivial monodromy; IUT instead keeps the domain and codomain
1483	distinct \cite{mochizukiRpt2018}.
1484	
1485	That answer is important, but it is not the strongest answer available.  From
1486	the logical base of the present paper, Mochizuki's response still grants too
1487	much to the classical criterion that generated the objection.  He describes
1488	the incompatibility produced by the loop as a ``contradiction'' that is
1489	\emph{avoided} by distinguishing the two sides.  Distinguishing the sides is
1490	mathematically correct; treating the avoidance of contradiction as the
1491	foundational reason for doing so is not.
1492	
1493	The distinction of labels has a more precise role.  It preserves locality:
1494	different ring structures, filtration positions, and transport histories remain
1495	different data.  It need not guarantee that every readout formed from those data
1496	is classically consistent.  If a local comparison carries both a determination
1497	and an incompatible determination, that state remains a legitimate state of the
1498	calculation.  What is forbidden is unrestricted explosion, not contradiction
1499	itself.
1500	
1501	This gives two residual misunderstandings in Mochizuki's response, relative to
1502	the rebase developed here.
1503	
1504	\begin{enumerate}
1505	\item \textbf{The avoidance misunderstanding.}
1506	  The role of distinct labels is described as preventing a contradiction from
1507	  arising.  Here their role is instead to prevent the \emph{loss of locality}.
1508	  Contradictory information may remain live after locality has been preserved.
1509	
1510	\item \textbf{The scalar-stage misunderstanding.}
1511	  Mochizuki answers the Scholze--Stix loop mainly by denying that the loop occurs
1512	  in the proof and by appealing to the single log-volume on the common
1513	  multiradial container.  That is true as a description of his construction,
1514	  but it does not isolate the decisive defect in the Scholze--Stix reduction:
1515	  their scalar diagram has already forgotten the tensor-filtration position at
1516	  which the $j^2$ weights live.  The stronger objection is therefore not merely
1517	  ``your loop is not my diagram''.  It is ``your scalar diagram is not a
1518	  faithful readout of the filtered tensor object''.
1519	\end{enumerate}

1531	retain locality and tensor position $\to$ permit local incompatibility
1532	without explosion $\to$ retain $j^2$ $\to$ filtered readout.
1533	\end{tabularx}
1534	\end{center}
