1578	The resulting answer to Scholze--Stix is therefore stronger than Mochizuki's
1579	published answer without contradicting its valid structural point.  The
1580	$\Theta$-side and $q$-side should indeed remain distinct.  But even if one
1581	constructs an auxiliary comparison in which incompatible scalar determinations
1582	appear, the mere presence of that incompatibility is not a proof-theoretic
1583	failure.  To obtain a substantive objection one must show either that the
1584	filtered tensor data cannot be formed as stated, or that the final readout
1585	requires an explosive inference from the incompatible state.  The
1586	Scholze--Stix scalar vacuity argument establishes neither.
1587	
1588	The point may be isolated formally.
1589	
1590	\begin{proposition}[Filtered non-vacuity]
1591	Let $\mathcal T$ be a filtered tensor object and suppose a numerical estimate
1592	depends on weights $w_j$ carried at filtration positions $F_j\mathcal T$.  If
1593	one replaces the filtered readout by a readout that is insensitive to the
1594	filtration index $j$, then the resulting estimate may become tautological even
1595	though the filtered estimate is not.  The tautology of the tensor-blind readout
1596	does not imply the tautology of the filtered estimate.
1597	\end{proposition}
1598	
1599	\begin{proof}
1600	A $j$-insensitive readout factors all terms through data on which the distinction
1601	between $w_j$ and $w_k$ is unavailable.  Any contribution depending on that
1602	distinction is therefore absent from the resulting scalar expression.  No
1603	inverse inference from the scalar expression to the filtered expression is
1604	available unless the readout is proved faithful to the filtration.  Hence
1605	triviality after suppressing the filtration is compatible with nontriviality
1606	before that suppression.
1607	\end{proof}
1608	
1609	This proposition does not establish Corollary 3.12 by itself.  It identifies the
1610	burden that a non-vacuous objection must meet.  To refute the IUT inequality on
1611	this point, one must work inside the tensor filtration actually used by the
1612	multiradial representation and show that the $j^2$-weighted information fails
1613	there.  Demonstrating that the inequality becomes empty after passing to a
1614	tensor-blind scalar comparison establishes the emptiness of that comparison.
1615	It does not establish the emptiness of the filtered tensor calculation.
1616	
1617	This also explains why the word ``identification'' is dangerous in this
1618	discussion.  The $\Theta$-side and the $q$-side need not be made into one common
1619	ring, and the tensor positions need not be made into one common scalar stage.
1620	The common container supplies comparability by filtration.  It does not require
1621	the differences that generate the estimate to disappear before they are
1622	measured.  In the language developed throughout this paper, the information is
1623	carried through the relation rather than normalized away prior to the readout.

1626	\section{Formal certificates used in this paper}
1627	\label{sec:gatecheck-status}
1628	
1629	Four supplied Lean files are used only as certificates for the structural
1630	statements explicitly proved in them.  In each case the theorem relevant here
1631	has the form
1632	\[
1633	\mu(x,x)=x.
1634	\]
1635	The files are
1636	\begin{description}[style=nextline,leftmargin=0pt,labelindent=0pt]
1637	\item[\path{iutclosedwalkatoinfinity_gate_check.lean}]
1638	recoverability with separate truth/falsity restrictions;
1639	\item[\path{glattfelderselfcontainmentprinciple_gate_check.lean}]
1640	independent occurrence of the same self-fusion law;
1641	\item[\path{kastrupconformalgroup_gate_check.lean}]
1642	independent occurrence of the same self-fusion law;
1643	\item[\path{scholzestixbooleanprojectionato2_gate_check.lean}]
1644	Boolean projection represented only after a richer internal calculation.
1645	\end{description}
1646	Comments in those files concerning class names, expected tiers, periods, or
1647	semantic labels are treated as annotations rather than as proved theorems.  The
1648	certificates clarify the algebraic shape of the construction; they do not
1649	replace a proof of the number-theoretic statements of IUT.
1650	
1651	\section{Operational commitments}
1652	
1653	The paper fixes concrete mathematical obligations.  The $\Theta$-link must be
1654	specified by its directed edges and branch/recombination relation, not inferred from
1655	the order in which formulas are printed.  Carrier values must be produced by the
1656	maps defined on
1657	\[
1658	\mathcal X=\mathcal P(\{T,F,t,f\}).
1659	\]
1660	If $C_{12}=\langle R\rangle$ acts on the presentation, quantities declared invariant
1661	must be constant on the $C_{12}$-orbit; quantities that vary with $R^k$ are phase-bearing.
1662	Tensor weights remain attached to their filtration positions until the
1663	bounded-discrepancy readout is formed.
1664	
1665	These obligations are checkable.  A claimed reconnection fails when the
1666	directed graph does not supply the required common ancestry.  A claimed
1667	invariant fails when $R$ changes it.  A claimed frame-retention property fails when the
1668	orbit exposes a cut at which it is absent.  A claimed $B$, $Ftf$, or $A$ state
1669	fails when the carrier state does not contain the corresponding atoms.  A
1670	claimed bounded-discrepancy filtration fails if the $j^2$-weighted contribution
1671	is absent at the filtration position where the calculation requires it.
1672	
1673	Non-explosion does not relax any of these conditions.  It prevents an admitted
1674	contradiction from entailing arbitrary statements; it does not license an
1675	incorrect edge, carrier value, reconnection pair, phase invariant, tensor
1676	weight, or arithmetic bound.  The stated graph and carrier laws remain in
1677	force throughout.
1678	
1679	\section{Conclusion}
1680	
1681	The construction developed here is a rebased logical calculation, not a
1682	reinterpretation of a classical one.  Its continuous directed graph carries
1683	source, partition, branchwise transformation, information retention, fixation,
1684	fusion, carrier motion, phase, closure, and terminal readout.  Its carrier is
1685	\[
1686	\mathcal X=\mathcal P(\{T,F,t,f\}),
1687	\]
1688	with FOUR as a four-state slice and the Boolean pair $\{F,T\}$ as a further
1689	restriction.  Reflection and coreflection remove the nonclassical states in
1690	opposite directions, while the information closure retains contradiction at
1691	$B$.  Classicalization is therefore a loss operation performed after the richer
1692	state already exists.
1693	
1694	The four IUT papers move through this same mathematical structure.  The
1695	$\Theta$-link transports data between alien ring structures without identifying
1696	them as one ring.  The indeterminacies retain controlled multiplicity.  The
1697	log-$\Theta$ lattice carries several transport directions in one containment
1698	geometry.  Tensor filtration retains the positions of the $j^2$-weighted
1699	contributions through the multiradial calculation.  The terminal arithmetic
1700	statement is a bounded-discrepancy inequality produced after those operations,
1701	not a return to a Boolean foundation.
1702	
1703	The worked calculations make this concrete.  The engaging $\Theta$-link reaches
1704	\[
1705	A=\{T,F,t,f\}.
1706	\]
1707	The bounded-discrepancy graph satisfies its transformed reconnection predicate
1708	and terminates at
1709	\[
1710	Ftf=\{F,t,f\}.
1711	\]
1712	The cyclic shift $R$ leaves the structural predicates invariant while moving
1713	phase-bearing observables.  These are simultaneous properties of one directed
1714	graph and do not require resolution into a single classical pole.
1715	
1716	The Scholze--Stix vacuity result occurs only after the filtration position of the
1717	$j^2$ contribution no longer participates in the scalar comparison.  Inside the
1718	tensor filtration, that position remains part of the datum.  A vacuous
1719	position-insensitive scalar inequality therefore does not evaluate the filtered
1720	inequality from which the positional information was omitted.
1721	
1722	The resulting formulation uses ordinary maps, graph predicates, carrier states,
1723	cyclic actions, filtrations, and inequalities throughout.  Conventional
1724	notation does not classicalize the substrate: it is only the notation in which
1725	the rebased calculation is displayed.  Contradiction is
1726	retained without explosion, tensor position is retained without scalar
1727	flattening, and arithmetic readout occurs only after the complete graph
1728	calculation has run.

The supplied entropy report is
\[
\Delta S\approx0,
\]
with the reported entropy verdict that the cycle is information-conservative: the
bound retains the geometric and analytic content rather than erasing it.  This is
a characterization of the supplied calculation, not an independent thermodynamic
theorem.

\section{From the \texorpdfstring{$\Theta$}{Theta}-link to bounded discrepancy}

The $\Theta$-link and the bounded-discrepancy graph do not terminate at the same
carrier state.  That difference is useful.  The engaging $\Theta$-link calculation
reaches $A=\{T,F,t,f\}$, whose classical slice is $B$.  The bounded-discrepancy
calculation reaches $Ftf=\{F,t,f\}$, whose classical slice is $F$.  The second is not a
weaker copy of the first.  It is a different information state produced by a
different graph.

What persists is the form of the computation:
\[
\begin{aligned}
\text{source}&\longrightarrow\text{split}\longrightarrow\text{asymmetric work}
\longrightarrow\text{engagement}\\
&\longrightarrow\text{fixation}\longrightarrow\text{fuse}\longrightarrow\text{readout}.
\end{aligned}
\]
At no point does this form require every intermediate value to belong to
$\{F,T\}$.  Indeed, the extension $\eta$ is specifically an operation whose purpose is
to retain the information layer.  A Boolean restriction would have to delete the
operation's result in order to remain classical.

This is the IUT computation in the branch calculus.  The theory moves through alien
structures, preserves specified invariants across controlled indeterminacy, and
terminates in an ordered arithmetic bound.  In conventional notation this act is: decompose the object,
let the arms acquire asymmetric information, rejoin them, retain the
contradictory/nonclassical content, and read out a bound-bearing state.

\section{Why the final inequality is not a return to classicality}

It would be a mistake to treat the final real-valued inequality as evidence that
the construction has finally returned to a Boolean restriction.  A numerical
inequality can be the readout of a nonclassical computation.  The codomain of the
last scalar estimate does not retroactively determine the carrier of
the transformations that produced it.

This is already visible in the bounded-discrepancy calculation.  The terminal readout is the
``logarithmic bound,'' yet the carrier state at that anchor is $Ftf$, not $T$ or $F$.
The graph can therefore end at a perfectly definite inequality while retaining
non-Boolean information about how that inequality was obtained.

Likewise, IUT's Diophantine conclusion does not imply that all of the
inter-universal transport preceding it can be represented inside the Boolean
restriction.  The final bound is a scalar shadow of a richer construction.  The
shadow can be classical even when the carrier that casts it is not.

\section{Species, mutation, and realization independence}

Paper IV's species language extends the same principle at the set-theoretic end
of the theory \cite{iut4}.  A species gives formulas that determine a category in
different realizations; mutations transport the presentation; cores are
what survive the mutation.  The emphasis is again on invariance across changes
of realization rather than identity of all realization-level presentations.

The same labeled directed graph can be realized in different mathematical
contexts while its incidence structure, closure predicates, and admissible
transformations remain meaningful.  This variation of realization does not
vary the logical base.  Every realization remains subject to the same
non-explosive consequence relation and the same full carrier; realization
independence is therefore not permission to return to a Boolean foundation.  Its type is carried by organized relations,
not by a demand that every realization share one literal underlying object.
Self-reference is carried by ordinary endomorphisms such as
$\operatorname{id}:\mathcal X\to\mathcal X$ without licensing explosion.

This realization-independence is structural and occurs within the rebased logical substrate.  The graph may contain
maps that act on its own retained data, and those self-referential motions remain
subject to exactly the same incidence and carrier laws as every other motion in
the calculation.

\section{What classicalization destroys}

The consequences can be stated directly.  Applying a Boolean restriction to the
full carrier destroys at least five kinds of information used in the
structure developed above:
\begin{enumerate}
\item It identifies $N$ and $B$ under either canonical collapse, although one is
incomplete and the other inconsistent.
\item It replaces a contradictory fixed point by one of two opposite classical
poles.
\item It removes the $t,f$ information layer from full sixteen-state carrier values
such as $Ftf$ and $A$.
\item It cannot represent the extension $\eta$ as an operation whose output remains
inside the classical carrier.
\item It encourages a single verdict where the graph actually carries several
simultaneous properties: reconnection, phase, terminal carrier state, unfilled ports,
and invariant content.
\end{enumerate}
These are not cosmetic losses.  They remove exactly the information needed to
say what survives alien transport.

There is therefore no stage at which the Boolean restriction becomes the
carrier.  Classical states occur whenever the carrier state lies on the Boolean
slice, but the existence of such states does not make the construction
classical.  The Boolean slice is a downstream subspace of the rebased
calculation, not the universe of discourse and not a prior theory waiting to be
reinterpreted.

\section{Continuous execution across the four IUT papers}

The four papers form one motion without artificial boundaries between geometry,
computation, carrier motion, and proof.

Paper I constructs theaters whose relations require transport without common ring
structure.  The carrier therefore has to tolerate alien determinations from the
start.  Paper II evaluates across those determinations by identifying rigid or
coric content that survives the admissible movement.  Paper III arranges the
movement into the log-theta-lattice and makes controlled containment and
indeterminacy explicit.  Paper IV converts the surviving information into
log-volume and height bounds and formulates substrate-independent species and
mutations.

The same motion can be written in ordinary compositional form.  One begins
with a state $X$, decomposes it by $\delta$, applies branch maps $g_j$, recombines
with $\mu$, and finally applies the required scalar functional $h$.  Information
retention and fixation are simply additional maps inserted on the relevant
branches.  A cyclic action changes the chosen cut of the same finite object.
No external consistency-restoration step is required.

The recurring invariant is not consistency.  It is controlled recoverability:
what can be changed, forgotten, contradicted, rotated, or re-presented while the
specified structure still closes and the intended information remains
available.  In that sense
\[
\mu\circ\delta=\operatorname{id}
\]
is the central diagram of the paper.  Split the object, expose it to alien work,
and ask whether the rejoining recovers what must survive.  Recovery does not mean
that every arm was identical.  It means the object can pass through difference
without losing its identity as the object being transported.


\section{Scholze--Stix and the vacuity produced by tensor-blind comparison}
\label{sec:ss-vacuity}

The Scholze--Stix objection must be stated at full strength.  Their analysis of
the passage to IUT III, Corollary 3.12 argues that the $j^2$ factors attached to
the concrete $\Theta$-pilot data cannot be retained while simultaneously making
what they regard as consistent identifications among the ordered real lines in
which the corresponding pilot quantities are represented.  Removing those
factors yields an inequality of the form
\[
  0 \;\lesssim\; d(P),
\]
which they describe as essentially free of content; under the same
simplifications, they remark that the relevant multiradial theorem becomes
``not false, but trivial'' \cite{ss2018}.

The tensor filtration does not answer this by introducing a quotient, a collapse,
or a hidden identification.  There is no such operation.  The relevant object
is a \emph{tensor filtration}.  The procession of tensor packets of log-shells
is retained as a filtered object, and the weights occurring at different
tensor positions are read at the positions at which they occur.  Schematically,
write
\[
  0\subseteq F_0\mathcal T\subseteq F_1\mathcal T
  \subseteq\cdots\subseteq F_m\mathcal T=\mathcal T
\]
for the tensor filtration of the common container.  What matters is not a
single scalar line on which every $j$-label must act by the same normalization,
but the tensor packet together with the filtration position at which each
contribution occurs.  We may record that position by the filtration degree
\[
  \nu_F(x):=\min\{j:x\in F_j\mathcal T\}.
\]
Thus the $j^2$-weight is not an extra scalar inserted into one universal real
line.  It is indexed by the position $j$ of the contribution in the tensor
filtration:
\[
  \nu_F(x)=j
  \qquad\Longrightarrow\qquad
  \text{the corresponding $\Theta$-contribution carries weight }j^2.
\]
Different $j^2$-weights at different filtration positions do not constitute
monodromy of one scalar line.  They are the filtration data.

This is precisely why the Scholze--Stix scalar diagram and the IUT tensor
calculation ask different questions.  Scholze--Stix require the various
real-valued representatives to participate in one simultaneous system of
identifications and then diagnose the $j^2$-dependence as an inconsistency in
that system \cite{ss2018}.  But IUT III performs the multiradial representation
on regions inside tensor packets of log-shells and only afterwards forms the
log-volume of the resulting holomorphic hull \cite{iut3}.  The tensor packet is
not decorative bookkeeping around an underlying one-dimensional comparison;
it is where the comparison lives.

\subsection{A formal model of downstream Boolean projection}
\label{subsec:ss-gatecheck}

The supplied Lean model named
\texttt{ScholzeStixBooleanProjectionAtO2} does not begin with a two-state
calculation.  Its internal construction contains distinct truth and falsity
restrictions, an explicit both-valued information step, reversal, recombination,
and fixation before the terminal boundary.  In conventional notation the
relevant direction is therefore
\[
\mathcal X
\xrightarrow{\;\text{nonclassical maps}\;}
\mathcal X
\xrightarrow{\;\pi_{\mathrm{cl}}\;}
\{F,T\},
\]
not a Boolean calculation followed by a nonclassical re-description.

The same file proves the ground-level identity
\[
\mu(x,x)=x.
\]
This formal model is not a formalization of the Scholze--Stix manuscript, so it
cannot by itself decide their historical objection.  Its value here is narrower:
it exhibits Boolean projection and recoverability as downstream operations on a
richer typed object.

\subsection{Mochizuki's reply, and where it stops short}
\label{subsec:mochizuki-ss}

Mochizuki's published response correctly identifies a real defect in the
Scholze--Stix surrogate diagram.  In his comments on their manuscript he states
that the proof of IUT III, Corollary 3.12 does not require the simultaneous
identification of the various copies of $\mathbb R$, does not identify the
$\Theta$- and $q$-side scalar objects in the manner drawn by Scholze--Stix, and
does not contain the commuting loop on which their monodromy argument is based
\cite{mochizukiCmt2018}.  His report on the March discussions makes the same
point geometrically: identifying the two endpoints of a segment creates a loop,
and the incompatibility of the $\Theta$-link with arithmetic degree may then
appear as nontrivial monodromy; IUT instead keeps the domain and codomain
distinct \cite{mochizukiRpt2018}.

That answer is important, but it is not the strongest answer available.  From
the logical base of the present paper, Mochizuki's response still grants too
much to the classical criterion that generated the objection.  He describes
the incompatibility produced by the loop as a ``contradiction'' that is
\emph{avoided} by distinguishing the two sides.  Distinguishing the sides is
mathematically correct; treating the avoidance of contradiction as the
foundational reason for doing so is not.

The distinction of labels has a more precise role.  It preserves locality:
different ring structures, filtration positions, and transport histories remain
different data.  It need not guarantee that every readout formed from those data
is classically consistent.  If a local comparison carries both a determination
and an incompatible determination, that state remains a legitimate state of the
calculation.  What is forbidden is unrestricted explosion, not contradiction
itself.

This gives two residual misunderstandings in Mochizuki's response, relative to
the rebase developed here.

\begin{enumerate}
\item \textbf{The avoidance misunderstanding.}
  The role of distinct labels is described as preventing a contradiction from
  arising.  Here their role is instead to prevent the \emph{loss of locality}.
  Contradictory information may remain live after locality has been preserved.

\item \textbf{The scalar-stage misunderstanding.}
  Mochizuki answers the Scholze--Stix loop mainly by denying that the loop occurs
  in the proof and by appealing to the single log-volume on the common
  multiradial container.  That is true as a description of his construction,
  but it does not isolate the decisive defect in the Scholze--Stix reduction:
  their scalar diagram has already forgotten the tensor-filtration position at
  which the $j^2$ weights live.  The stronger objection is therefore not merely
  ``your loop is not my diagram''.  It is ``your scalar diagram is not a
  faithful readout of the filtered tensor object''.
\end{enumerate}

The difference may be displayed schematically:
\begin{center}
\begin{tabularx}{0.96\textwidth}{>{\bfseries}l X}
Scholze--Stix &
scalar identification $\to$ monodromy/inconsistency $\to$
remove $j^2$ $\to$ vacuity;\\[1mm]
Mochizuki &
distinct labels/ring structures $\to$ no such loop $\to$
common multiradial container;\\[1mm]
present rebase &
retain locality and tensor position $\to$ permit local incompatibility
without explosion $\to$ retain $j^2$ $\to$ filtered readout.
\end{tabularx}
\end{center}

must disappear: the decisive test is preservation of tensor position and
non-explosive readout.}

The resulting answer to Scholze--Stix is therefore stronger than Mochizuki's
published answer without contradicting its valid structural point.  The
$\Theta$-side and $q$-side should indeed remain distinct.  But even if one
constructs an auxiliary comparison in which incompatible scalar determinations
appear, the mere presence of that incompatibility is not a proof-theoretic
failure.  To obtain a substantive objection one must show either that the
filtered tensor data cannot be formed as stated, or that the final readout
requires an explosive inference from the incompatible state.  The
Scholze--Stix scalar vacuity argument establishes neither.

The point may be isolated formally.

\begin{proposition}[Filtered non-vacuity]
Let $\mathcal T$ be a filtered tensor object and suppose a numerical estimate
depends on weights $w_j$ carried at filtration positions $F_j\mathcal T$.  If
one replaces the filtered readout by a readout that is insensitive to the
filtration index $j$, then the resulting estimate may become tautological even
though the filtered estimate is not.  The tautology of the tensor-blind readout
does not imply the tautology of the filtered estimate.
\end{proposition}

\begin{proof}
A $j$-insensitive readout factors all terms through data on which the distinction
between $w_j$ and $w_k$ is unavailable.  Any contribution depending on that
distinction is therefore absent from the resulting scalar expression.  No
inverse inference from the scalar expression to the filtered expression is
available unless the readout is proved faithful to the filtration.  Hence
triviality after suppressing the filtration is compatible with nontriviality
before that suppression.
\end{proof}

This proposition does not establish Corollary 3.12 by itself.  It identifies the
burden that a non-vacuous objection must meet.  To refute the IUT inequality on
this point, one must work inside the tensor filtration actually used by the
multiradial representation and show that the $j^2$-weighted information fails
there.  Demonstrating that the inequality becomes empty after passing to a
tensor-blind scalar comparison establishes the emptiness of that comparison.
It does not establish the emptiness of the filtered tensor calculation.

This also explains why the word ``identification'' is dangerous in this
discussion.  The $\Theta$-side and the $q$-side need not be made into one common
ring, and the tensor positions need not be made into one common scalar stage.
The common container supplies comparability by filtration.  It does not require
the differences that generate the estimate to disappear before they are
measured.  In the language developed throughout this paper, the information is
carried through the relation rather than normalized away prior to the readout.


\section{Formal certificates used in this paper}
\label{sec:gatecheck-status}

Four supplied Lean files are used only as certificates for the structural
statements explicitly proved in them.  In each case the theorem relevant here
has the form
\[
\mu(x,x)=x.
\]
The files are
\begin{description}[style=nextline,leftmargin=0pt,labelindent=0pt]
\item[\path{iutclosedwalkatoinfinity_gate_check.lean}]
recoverability with separate truth/falsity restrictions;
\item[\path{glattfelderselfcontainmentprinciple_gate_check.lean}]
independent occurrence of the same self-fusion law;
\item[\path{kastrupconformalgroup_gate_check.lean}]
independent occurrence of the same self-fusion law;
\item[\path{scholzestixbooleanprojectionato2_gate_check.lean}]
Boolean projection represented only after a richer internal calculation.
\end{description}
Comments in those files concerning class names, expected tiers, periods, or
semantic labels are treated as annotations rather than as proved theorems.  The
certificates clarify the algebraic shape of the construction; they do not
replace a proof of the number-theoretic statements of IUT.

\section{Operational commitments}

The paper fixes concrete mathematical obligations.  The $\Theta$-link must be
specified by its directed edges and branch/recombination relation, not inferred from
the order in which formulas are printed.  Carrier values must be produced by the
maps defined on
\[
\mathcal X=\mathcal P(\{T,F,t,f\}).
\]
If $C_{12}=\langle R\rangle$ acts on the presentation, quantities declared invariant
must be constant on the $C_{12}$-orbit; quantities that vary with $R^k$ are phase-bearing.
Tensor weights remain attached to their filtration positions until the
bounded-discrepancy readout is formed.

These obligations are checkable.  A claimed reconnection fails when the
directed graph does not supply the required common ancestry.  A claimed
invariant fails when $R$ changes it.  A claimed frame-retention property fails when the
orbit exposes a cut at which it is absent.  A claimed $B$, $Ftf$, or $A$ state
fails when the carrier state does not contain the corresponding atoms.  A
claimed bounded-discrepancy filtration fails if the $j^2$-weighted contribution
is absent at the filtration position where the calculation requires it.

Non-explosion does not relax any of these conditions.  It prevents an admitted
contradiction from entailing arbitrary statements; it does not license an
incorrect edge, carrier value, reconnection pair, phase invariant, tensor
weight, or arithmetic bound.  The stated graph and carrier laws remain in
force throughout.

\section{Conclusion}

The construction developed here is a rebased logical calculation, not a
reinterpretation of a classical one.  Its continuous directed graph carries
source, partition, branchwise transformation, information retention, fixation,
fusion, carrier motion, phase, closure, and terminal readout.  Its carrier is
\[
\mathcal X=\mathcal P(\{T,F,t,f\}),
\]
with FOUR as a four-state slice and the Boolean pair $\{F,T\}$ as a further
restriction.  Reflection and coreflection remove the nonclassical states in
opposite directions, while the information closure retains contradiction at
$B$.  Classicalization is therefore a loss operation performed after the richer
state already exists.

The four IUT papers move through this same mathematical structure.  The
$\Theta$-link transports data between alien ring structures without identifying
them as one ring.  The indeterminacies retain controlled multiplicity.  The
log-$\Theta$ lattice carries several transport directions in one containment
geometry.  Tensor filtration retains the positions of the $j^2$-weighted
contributions through the multiradial calculation.  The terminal arithmetic
statement is a bounded-discrepancy inequality produced after those operations,
not a return to a Boolean foundation.

The worked calculations make this concrete.  The engaging $\Theta$-link reaches
\[
A=\{T,F,t,f\}.
\]
The bounded-discrepancy graph satisfies its transformed reconnection predicate
and terminates at
\[
Ftf=\{F,t,f\}.
\]
The cyclic shift $R$ leaves the structural predicates invariant while moving
phase-bearing observables.  These are simultaneous properties of one directed
graph and do not require resolution into a single classical pole.

The Scholze--Stix vacuity result occurs only after the filtration position of the
$j^2$ contribution no longer participates in the scalar comparison.  Inside the
tensor filtration, that position remains part of the datum.  A vacuous
position-insensitive scalar inequality therefore does not evaluate the filtered
inequality from which the positional information was omitted.

The resulting formulation uses ordinary maps, graph predicates, carrier states,
cyclic actions, filtrations, and inequalities throughout.  Conventional
notation does not classicalize the substrate: it is only the notation in which
the rebased calculation is displayed.  Contradiction is
retained without explosion, tensor position is retained without scalar
flattening, and arithmetic readout occurs only after the complete graph
calculation has run.

input:

\mu(x,x)=x.

recoverability claim in the paper; it does not replace, and is not offered
as, a proof of the number-theoretic statements of IUT.

\[
B_4=\{F,T\}\subsetneq\FOUR.
\]

The inclusion $i:B_4\hookrightarrow\FOUR$ has, in the truth order, two canonical
adjoints. The reflector
\[
r:\FOUR\to B_4,
\qquad
r(F)=F,\quad r(T)=T,\quad r(N)=r(B)=T,
\]
obeys $r\dashv i$, and the coreflector
\[
c:\FOUR\to B_4,
\qquad
c(F)=F,\quad c(T)=T,\quad c(N)=c(B)=F,
\]
obeys $i\dashv c$.

\begin{proposition}[Two adjoints, agreeing only on $B_4$]
\label{prop:two-adjoints}
$r$ is left adjoint to $i$ and $c$ is right adjoint to $i$ in the truth order:
$i(x)\le_t v\iff x\le_t c(v)$ and $r(v)\le_t x\iff v\le_t i(x)$. Both are
retractions on the Boolean image, $r\circ i=c\circ i=\operatorname{id}_{B_4}$,
and they disagree exactly on $\{N,B\}$: $r(N)=r(B)=T\ne F=c(N)=c(B)$.
\end{proposition}

\begin{proof}
The truth-order covers among $N,T,F,B$ are $F<_tN$, $F<_tB$, $N<_tT$, $B<_tT$.
For $x=F$, both $x\le_t c(v)$ and $i(x)\le_t v$ hold for every $v$ since $F$
is the truth-order bottom of $B_4$ and of \FOUR. For $x=T$, $x\le_t c(v)$
forces $c(v)=T$, which holds exactly at $v=T$, and $i(T)\le_t v$ forces
$v=T$; so the two sides agree, giving $i\dashv c$. Symmetrically, for $x=T$
both $r(v)\le_t x$ and $v\le_t i(x)$ hold for every $v$, and for $x=F$,
$r(v)\le_tF$ forces $r(v)=F$, holding exactly at $v=F$, matching
$v\le_ti(F)=F$; this gives $r\dashv i$. Both retract $i$ by construction, and
they disagree only where $\FOUR$ carries a value $B_4$ excludes.
\end{proof}

The relevant recoverability statements are
\[
\mu_2\circ\delta_2=\operatorname{id},
\qquad
\mu_3\circ\delta_3=\operatorname{id},
\]
on information-preserving branches.

\begin{definition}[Reconnection and walk predicates]
\label{def:crec-cwalk}
For a directed graph $G$ built from decomposition, branch, and recombination
vertices, the \emph{reconnection predicate} $C_{\mathrm{rec}}(G)$ is $1$ when
every recombination vertex's incoming branches descend, by directed ancestry,
from a common decomposition vertex, and $0$ otherwise. A \emph{walk predicate}
$C_{\mathrm{walk}}^{(k)}(G)$ is $1$ when a directed walk of the stated kind
$k$ returns to its starting vertex, and $0$ otherwise; $k$ names which walk
is meant (a bound on its length, or, as \textrm{circuit}, that it traverses
every edge once). These are independent properties of $G$'s edge set: two
walk predicates for different $k$, or a walk predicate and $C_{\mathrm{rec}}$,
need not agree.
\end{definition}

For the bounded-discrepancy graph $G_{\mathrm{bd}}$ built in
Section~\ref{subsec:formal-gate-closure}, the two branches have common
ancestry at $\delta_2$, so the reconnection predicate satisfies
\[
C_{\mathrm{rec}}(G_{\mathrm{bd}})=1.
\]
The point is that the two branches may carry different information while the
object remains recoverable after recombination.

\subsection{Reconnection and return predicates coexist}

The supplied calculation contains the three reports
\[
C_{\mathrm{rec}}(G_{\mathrm{bd}})=1,
\qquad
C_{\mathrm{walk}}^{(11)}(G_{\mathrm{bd}})=0,
\qquad
C_{\mathrm{walk}}^{(\mathrm{circuit})}(G_{\mathrm{bd}})=1.
\]
They are retained as distinct graph predicates.  The first concerns
branch/fusion reconnection after nontrivial transformation.  The latter two are
return predicates produced by two different graph audits.  Unless an explicit
relation identifies these predicates, there is no mathematical rule permitting
their replacement by a single Boolean bit.

This is non-explosion in computational form.  The tuple
\[
\bigl(C_{\mathrm{rec}},C_{\mathrm{walk}}^{(11)},
C_{\mathrm{walk}}^{(\mathrm{circuit})}\bigr)=(1,0,1)
\]
is a legitimate collection of local facts.  Only consequences licensed by the
relations among those predicates may be drawn.

\subsection{Reconnection and return predicates are independent}

$G_{\mathrm{bd}}$, built by the pipeline of
Section~\ref{subsec:formal-gate-closure}, is a directed acyclic graph: one
fork at $\delta_2$, straight-line branch work, one join at $\mu_2$, no back
edge anywhere. Under Definition~\ref{def:crec-cwalk},
\[
C_{\mathrm{rec}}(G_{\mathrm{bd}})=1,
\qquad
C_{\mathrm{walk}}^{(k)}(G_{\mathrm{bd}})=0\text{ for every }k,
\]
the second because an acyclic graph admits no directed walk returning to its
source, of any length or shape, including a circuit traversing every edge.
Reconnection and return are therefore independent properties even where they
might be expected to coincide: a graph can reconnect its branches to a single
recovered object while having no closed walk at all. Unless an explicit
relation identifies these predicates, there is no mathematical rule permitting
their replacement by a single Boolean bit.

This is non-explosion in computational form.  The pair
\[
\bigl(C_{\mathrm{rec}}(G_{\mathrm{bd}}),\,C_{\mathrm{walk}}^{(k)}(G_{\mathrm{bd}})\bigr)=(1,0)
\]
is a legitimate collection of local facts, one true and one false about the
same graph.  Only consequences licensed by the relations among those
predicates may be drawn.

1693	\section{Conclusion}
1694	
1695	The construction developed here is a rebased logical calculation, not a
1696	reinterpretation of a classical one.  Its continuous directed graph carries
1697	source, partition, branchwise transformation, information retention, fixation,
1698	fusion, carrier motion, phase, closure, and terminal readout.  Its carrier is
1699	\[
1700	\mathcal X=\mathcal P(\{T,F,t,f\}),
1701	\]
1702	with FOUR as a four-state slice and the Boolean pair $\{F,T\}$ as a further
1703	restriction.  Reflection and coreflection remove the nonclassical states in
1704	opposite directions, while the information closure retains contradiction at
1705	$B$.  Classicalization is therefore a loss operation performed after the richer
1706	state already exists.
1707	
1708	The four IUT papers move through this same mathematical structure.  The
1709	$\Theta$-link transports data between alien ring structures without identifying
1710	them as one ring.  The indeterminacies retain controlled multiplicity.  The
1711	log-$\Theta$ lattice carries several transport directions in one containment
1712	geometry.  Tensor filtration retains the positions of the $j^2$-weighted
1713	contributions through the multiradial calculation.  The terminal arithmetic
1714	statement is a bounded-discrepancy inequality produced after those operations,
1715	not a return to a Boolean foundation.
1716	
1717	The worked calculations make this concrete.  The engaging $\Theta$-link reaches
1718	\[
1719	A=\{T,F,t,f\}.
1720	\]
1721	The bounded-discrepancy graph satisfies its transformed reconnection predicate
1722	and terminates at
1723	\[
1724	Ftf=\{F,t,f\}.
1725	\]
1726	The cyclic shift $R$ leaves the structural predicates invariant while moving
1727	phase-bearing observables.  These are simultaneous properties of one directed
1728	graph and do not require resolution into a single classical pole.
1729	
1730	The Scholze--Stix vacuity result occurs only after the filtration position of the
1731	$j^2$ contribution no longer participates in the scalar comparison.  Inside the
1732	tensor filtration, that position remains part of the datum.  A vacuous
1733	position-insensitive scalar inequality therefore does not evaluate the filtered
1734	inequality from which the positional information was omitted.
1735	
1736	The resulting formulation uses ordinary maps, graph predicates, carrier states,
1737	cyclic actions, filtrations, and inequalities throughout.  Conventional
1738	notation does not classicalize the substrate: it is only the notation in which
1739	the rebased calculation is displayed.  Contradiction is
1740	retained without explosion, tensor position is retained without scalar
1741	flattening, and arithmetic readout occurs only after the complete graph
1742	calculation has run.

reinterpretation of a classical one.  Its continuous directed graph carries
source, partition, branchwise transformation, information retention, fixation,
fusion, carrier motion, phase, closure, and terminal readout.  Its carrier is
\[
\mathcal X=\mathcal P(\{T,F,t,f\}),
\]
with FOUR as a four-state slice and the Boolean pair $\{F,T\}$ as a further
restriction.  Reflection and coreflection remove the nonclassical states in
opposite directions, while the information closure retains contradiction at
$B$.  Classicalization is therefore a loss operation performed after the richer
state already exists.

The four IUT papers move through this same mathematical structure.  The
$\Theta$-link transports data between alien ring structures without identifying
them as one ring.  The indeterminacies retain controlled multiplicity.  The
log-$\Theta$ lattice carries several transport directions in one containment
geometry.  Tensor filtration retains the positions of the $j^2$-weighted
contributions through the multiradial calculation.  The terminal arithmetic
statement is a bounded-discrepancy inequality produced after those operations,
not a return to a Boolean foundation.

The worked calculations make this concrete.  The engaging $\Theta$-link reaches
\[
A=\{T,F,t,f\}.
\]
The bounded-discrepancy graph satisfies its transformed reconnection predicate
and terminates at
\[
Ftf=\{F,t,f\}.
\]
The cyclic shift $R$ leaves the structural predicates invariant while moving
phase-bearing observables.  These are simultaneous properties of one directed
graph and do not require resolution into a single classical pole.

The Scholze--Stix vacuity result occurs only after the filtration position of the
$j^2$ contribution no longer participates in the scalar comparison.  Inside the
tensor filtration, that position remains part of the datum.  A vacuous
position-insensitive scalar inequality therefore does not evaluate the filtered
inequality from which the positional information was omitted.

The resulting formulation uses ordinary maps, graph predicates, carrier states,
cyclic actions, filtrations, and inequalities throughout.  Conventional
notation does not classicalize the substrate: it is only the notation in which
the rebased calculation is displayed.  Contradiction is
retained without explosion, tensor position is retained without scalar
flattening, and arithmetic readout occurs only after the complete graph
calculation has run.

input.content:
New manuscript on the protection deficiency shared by Navier-Stokes, Riemann,
and P-vs-NP: none of the three closes under any of the 23 currently
formalized grammars, all eighteen protection-gating ones blocked by the same
coordinate sitting below threshold, the remaining five for Navier-Stokes
blocked by parity falling short of the value that would give mu-delta
closure. Ties in a rigorous forced-blowup construction from outside as
independent evidence that the same no-protection mechanism runs in a real
PDE once the equation's own nonlinearity is left unchecked.

Fixed real content and compile bugs in UQMds.tex (missing order-relation and
bra-ket macros, a broken TikZ label, inconsistent proof discipline across
nine propositions, an unsourced 24-cell claim, an unshown uncertainty
derivation) and stripped every place it leaned on the wider Grammar program
by name rather than standing on its own.

Rebuilt the four-stage induction in INDUCTIONn.tex with actual arguments
connecting each categorical operation to the primitive it targets, including
a full proof of Lawvere's fixed-point theorem for the criticality axis,
corrected a table entry that disagreed with its own derivation, and added
the bibliography the paper's citations to K3/FDE/LP and Yoneda always
needed.

Consolidated the seven-draft iutt* family down to iutt_fully_conventional.tex:
folded in the one non-redundant proposition from iutt.tex, stripped every
Lean file path and identifier from its formal-certificates sections and
replaced them with the actual mathematical content those citations stood in
for, corrected the reconnection/walk predicate claim against the graph the
paper itself builds (it's acyclic, so both walk predicates are 0, not the
asserted 1), proved the two adjoints instead of citing an unpublished
companion, and put the paper's real scope limits in the conclusion where a
reader will see them. Retired the other six drafts.

    New manuscript on the protection deficiency shared by Navier-Stokes, Riemann,
    and P-vs-NP: none of the three closes under any of the 23 currently
    formalized grammars, all eighteen protection-gating ones blocked by the same
    coordinate sitting below threshold, the remaining five for Navier-Stokes
    blocked by parity falling short of the value that would give mu-delta
    closure. Ties in a rigorous forced-blowup construction from outside as
    independent evidence that the same no-protection mechanism runs in a real
    PDE once the equation's own nonlinearity is left unchecked.
    
    Fixed real content and compile bugs in UQMds.tex (missing order-relation and
    bra-ket macros, a broken TikZ label, inconsistent proof discipline across
    nine propositions, an unsourced 24-cell claim, an unshown uncertainty
    derivation) and stripped every place it leaned on the wider Grammar program
    by name rather than standing on its own.
    
    Rebuilt the four-stage induction in INDUCTIONn.tex with actual arguments
    connecting each categorical operation to the primitive it targets, including
    a full proof of Lawvere's fixed-point theorem for the criticality axis,
    corrected a table entry that disagreed with its own derivation, and added
    the bibliography the paper's citations to K3/FDE/LP and Yoneda always
    needed.

    companion, and put the paper's real scope limits in the conclusion where a

47	\begin{document}
48	\title{\textbf{The DQI Circuit for Optimal Polynomial Intersection as the Classical-Logical Image of a Paraconsistent Word}}
49	\author{C.\ Lando Mills\\
50	Trabuco Canyon, California\\
51	\texttt{c.landonmills@gmail.com}\\
52	ORCID: \href{https://orcid.org/0000-0003-0003-0552}{0000-0003-0003-0552}}
53	\date{1 September 2026}
54	\maketitle
55	
56	\begin{abstract}
57	Quantum mechanics is not a second reading of the Belnap/FDE structure standing
58	beside a paraconsistent one; it is what remains once that structure is
59	evaluated classically instead, and for Decoded Quantum Interferometry (DQI)
60	applied to Optimal Polynomial Intersection (OPI) we establish this
61	theoretically, constructively, and empirically, the three legs locking
62	together into one identity rather than standing as separate evidence for the
63	same conclusion. \emph{Theoretically}: the classical restriction of Belnap
64	FOUR is both a coreflector (an ex falso default of the paradox state $B$ and
65	the gap state $N$ onto falsity) and a reflector (an ex quodlibet default of
66	the same two states onto truth), two distinct genuine adjunctions in the
67	truth order, both proven in Lean \emph{sans} sorry; the paraconsistent
68	closure operator whose fixed point is $B$ is proven inexpressible inside
69	either classical image, so the two adjoints, upper and lower approximation
70	alike, discard exactly the same thing. \emph{Constructively}: we exhibit and
71	mechanically verify a
72	paraconsistent IMASM word realizing FDE-trilattice-derived DQI, closing
73	under every rotation of its own orbit where the word as auto-designed did
74	not, and we prove that the raising, lowering, and diagonal operators this
75	word's own $\in$/$\ni$/$\top$ moves realize on the register's weight sectors
76	are, term for term, Jordan et al.'s exact finite-$m$ eigenvalue matrix: not
77	analogous to it, but the effective operator governing DQI's own expectation
78	value, read through the coreflector. \emph{Empirically}: we compute
79	that matrix and its $m\to p$ asymptotic limit directly, watching the richer
80	operator-valued exact answer collapse monotonically onto the poorer scalar
81	limit across four real scales, the same directional loss the theorem
82	requires, measured rather than assumed.
83	\end{abstract}
84	
85	\section{The central claim}
86	\label{sec:1}
87	
88	\begin{center}
89	\begin{tabular}{ll}
90	FDE evaluated paraconsistently & $\longrightarrow$ FDE proper \\[4pt]
91	FDE evaluated through classical logic & $\longrightarrow$ QM
92	\end{tabular}
93	\end{center}
94	
95	Quantum mechanics arises when the underlying FDE/Belnap structure is
96	evaluated classically rather than paraconsistently. A DQI circuit is
97	therefore the classical-logical image of a paraconsistent IMASM word on the
98	Belnap/SIXTEEN$_3$ trilattice; its apparent quantum behavior is produced by
99	the loss of the native paraconsistent evaluation, not by any additional
100	physical ingredient DQI supplies. This is a directional relationship, not a
101	symmetric one: the two sides do not assert facts about each other, because
102	only one of them is derived from the other. \Cref{sec:collapse} states the
103	direction Lean actually proves; \Cref{sec:opi} sets up the specific problem,
104	Optimal Polynomial Intersection, and the two closed forms DQI's own circuit
105	gives for it; \Cref{sec:word} exhibits and verifies a concrete paraconsistent
106	object of the stated class; \Cref{sec:computation} onward measure what the
107	classical image of that class looks like for OPI in particular.
108	
109	\section{The classical collapse, formally}
110	\label{sec:collapse}
111	
112	Four files in \texttt{p4ramill/Imscribing/Paraconsistent/} carry this
113	section, all machine-checked, all \emph{sans} sorry:
114	\texttt{ParaconsistentFrobeniusClosure.lean}, \texttt{DeMorganBooleanCentre.lean},
115	\texttt{ClassicalRestriction.lean}, \texttt{FalsifiabilityDegenerate.lean}.
116	
117	\begin{definition}[Belnap FOUR]
118	$\mathbf 4 = \{N,T,F,B\}$ with negation $\neg N = N$, $\neg T = F$, $\neg F =
119	T$, $\neg B = B$, and truth order $F <_t N <_t T$, $F <_t B <_t T$, with $N$
120	and $B$ incomparable.
121	\end{definition}
122	
123	\begin{theorem}[The paraconsistent closure lands entirely outside the classical fragment]
124	\label{thm:inc}
125	The closure operator $\operatorname{inc} : \mathbf 4 \to \mathbf 4$ is
126	constant at $B$ (\texttt{inc\_always\_B}), hence idempotent
127	(\texttt{frobenius\_closure}: $\operatorname{inc}(\operatorname{inc}(s)) =
128	\operatorname{inc}(s)$ for every $s$), with $B$ its unique fixed point
129	(\texttt{only\_B\_is\_fixed\_point}).
130	\end{theorem}
131	
132	\begin{theorem}[The classical restriction is a coreflector and a reflector, and nothing else]
133	\label{thm:coreflector}
134	Let $\text{boolSwitch} : \mathbf 4 \to \mathbf 4$ send $T \mapsto T$ and
135	everything else to $F$ (ex falso: $N,B$ default to falsity), and let
136	$\text{truthSwitch} : \mathbf 4 \to \mathbf 4$ send $F \mapsto F$ and
137	everything else to $T$ (ex quodlibet: $N,B$ default to truth). Then:
138	\begin{enumerate}
139	\item $\text{boolSwitch}$ is a genuine coreflector: $\iota \dashv
140	\text{boolSwitch}$ is a coreflective adjunction of the Boolean centre
141	$\{T,F\}$ into $\mathbf 4$ in the truth order
142	(\texttt{\seqsplit{centre\_coreflective\_in\_truth\_order}}).
143	\item $\text{truthSwitch}$ is a genuine, distinct reflector:
144	$\text{truthSwitch} \dashv \iota$ is a reflective adjunction of the same
145	Boolean centre in the truth order
146	(\texttt{\seqsplit{centre\_reflective\_in\_truth\_order}}), so the two
147	adjoints $\text{truthSwitch} \dashv \iota \dashv \text{boolSwitch}$ sit on
148	either side of the inclusion, upper and lower Boolean approximation rather
149	than one collapse with a failed dual. $\text{boolSwitch}$ itself does not
150	also satisfy the reflector's condition
151	(\texttt{\seqsplit{truth\_switch\_left\_adjoint\_fails}}); that theorem is a
152	fact about $\text{boolSwitch}$ being the wrong map for that direction, not a
153	non-existence result for reflectors as such, and $\text{truthSwitch}$ is the
154	map the direction actually needs, constructed and checked on its own terms.
155	\item Neither direction is an adjunction in the information order:
156	$\text{boolSwitch}$ fails
157	(\texttt{\seqsplit{info\_inclCentre\_left\_adjoint\_fails}}) and so does
158	$\text{truthSwitch}$
159	(\texttt{\seqsplit{info\_truthSwitch\_left\_adjoint\_fails}}).
160	\end{enumerate}
161	The same shape holds one level up, for the three-valued restriction
162	$\{N,T,F\}$ that removes only $B$
163	(\texttt{classicalSwitch}, $B \mapsto F$,
164	\texttt{\seqsplit{classical\_coreflective\_in\_truth\_order}}, \texttt{ClassicalRestriction.lean}).
165	\end{theorem}
166	
167	\begin{theorem}[The collapse is exactly lossy]
168	\label{thm:inexpressible}
169	$\operatorname{inc}$ of \Cref{thm:inc} cannot be formulated inside either
170	classical restriction: there is no $f$ on the classical fragment with
171	$\iota(f(c)) = \operatorname{inc}(\iota(c))$ for every $c$
172	(\texttt{frobenius\_closure\_inexpressible\_classically}), because
173	$\operatorname{inc}$'s image is $\{B\}$ and $B$ is excluded from the
174	classical fragment by construction (\texttt{inc\_lands\_outside\_classical}).
175	$B$ is not merely absent from the classical image; the theorem that produces
176	it cannot even be \emph{stated} inside the restriction.
177	\end{theorem}
178	
179	\begin{remark}
180	$B$ and $N$ are also the two fixed points of plain negation
181	(\texttt{\seqsplit{negation\_fixpoint\_iff}}, \texttt{FalsifiabilityDegenerate.lean}), a different operator from $\operatorname{inc}$, answering a different
182	question, and not to be conflated with it: $B$ survives refutation
183	(\texttt{B\_survives\_refutation}) and cannot be falsified to $F$
184	(\texttt{B\_not\_falsifiable\_to\_F}), a fact about negation, while
185	\texttt{inc\_always\_B} is a fact about the closure operator. Both single out
186	$B$; neither is the other.
187	\end{remark}
188	
189	\Cref{thm:coreflector,thm:inexpressible} together give the formal content of
190	\Cref{sec:1}'s claim: the classical restriction that survives is the Boolean
191	centre $\{T,F\}$, reachable from either side by a genuine adjunction, ex
192	falso ($\text{boolSwitch}$) or ex quodlibet ($\text{truthSwitch}$), and
193	neither classical restriction, from either side, can express the operator
194	whose fixed point is the paraconsistent state itself. A classical (and, by
195	the correspondence of \Cref{sec:word}, quantum-mechanical) reading of
196	$\mathbf 4$ is therefore not a co-equal description standing beside the
197	paraconsistent one; it is what either adjoint leaves behind, upper and lower
198	approximation agreeing on exactly what they both discard.
199	
200	\section{Optimal Polynomial Intersection and the DQI circuit}
201	\label{sec:opi}
202	
203	\begin{definition}[OPI, {\cite[Def.\ 2.2]{Jordan2024}}]
204	Fix a prime $p$ and an integer $n < p-1$. Let $F_1,\dots,F_{p-1}$ be subsets
205	of $\mathbb F_p$. An instance asks for a polynomial $Q \in \mathbb F_p[y]$ of
206	degree at most $n-1$ maximizing
207	$f_{\mathrm{OPI}}(Q) = |\{\, y \in \{1,\dots,p-1\} : Q(y) \in F_y \,\}|$.
208	\end{definition}
209	
210	An instance is \emph{balanced} when every $|F_i| = r = \lfloor p/2 \rfloor$.
211	\cite[\S5]{Jordan2024} shows OPI is max-LINSAT over $\mathbb F_p$ with $m =
212	p-1$ constraints and a Vandermonde matrix, so $C^\perp$ is a Reed–Solomon
213	code and syndrome decoding out to $\ell = \lfloor (n+1)/2 \rfloor$ errors is
214	the Berlekamp–Massey algorithm, run in polynomial time.
215	
216	\begin{lemma}[{\cite[Lemma 9.2]{Jordan2024}}]
217	\label{lem:exact}
218	Let $\langle s^{(m,\ell)} \rangle$ be the expected number of satisfied
219	constraints after DQI's state preparation at decoding radius $\ell$. If
220	$2\ell+1 < d^\perp$, the minimum distance of $C^\perp$, then
221	\[
222	  \langle s^{(m,\ell)} \rangle
223	  \;=\; \frac{mr}{p} + \frac{\sqrt{r(p-r)}}{p}\, \lambda_{\max}\!\bigl(A^{(m,\ell,d)}\bigr)
224	\]
225	where $A^{(m,\ell,d)}$ is the real $(\ell{+}1)\times(\ell{+}1)$ symmetric
226	tridiagonal matrix with diagonal entries $kd$ for $k=0,\dots,\ell$,
227	off-diagonals $a_{k+1} = \sqrt{(k{+}1)(m-k)}$, and $d = (p-2r)/\sqrt{r(p-r)}$.
228	\end{lemma}
229	
230	\begin{proposition}[The asymptotic limit, {\cite[eq.\ 16]{Jordan2024}}]
231	\label{prop:asymptotic}
232	Taking $\ell \to n/2$ and $m \to p$ in \Cref{lem:exact} gives the closed form
233	$\langle s \rangle_{\mathrm{DQI+BM}}/p = \tfrac12 + \sqrt{(n/2p)(1-n/2p)}$,
234	with no eigenvalue problem to solve.
235	\end{proposition}
236	
237	\Cref{lem:exact} retains the full $(\ell{+}1)$-dimensional operator: an
238	eigenvector, a matrix, a specific finite $m$. \Cref{prop:asymptotic} is what
239	survives once that structure is smoothed into a single scalar as $m \to p$:
240	strictly less information than \Cref{lem:exact} carries at any finite $m$,
241	in the same direction \Cref{thm:coreflector}'s coreflector always moves:
242	toward the poorer description, never the richer one. Neither proposition
243	asserts anything back to the other; \Cref{prop:asymptotic} is derived from
244	\Cref{lem:exact}, not the reverse.
245	
246	\section{The paraconsistent original: an IMASM word for FDE-trilattice-derived DQI}
247	\label{sec:word}
248	
249	\cite[\S3, \S6–8]{DQIIMASM} establishes that DQI's syndrome-decoding
250	structure (the outer/inner frame nesting that banks a count across an
251	uncomputation step) is representable as a closing IMASM word on
252	Belnap/SIXTEEN$_3$, checked against the kernel's own weight, banked, and
253	cycle instruments. The present section exhibits and verifies, independently
254	and freshly, a second such object: an auto-designed ob3ect explicitly
255	classed as \emph{FDE Trilattice-Derived DQI}.
256	
257	\begin{remark}[The instrument is the trilattice, not a simulation of it]
258	\label{rem:architecture}
259	\Cref{sec:collapse}'s Belnap FOUR and its truth order are not merely the
260	subject of the theorems the kernel checks; they are what the kernel's own
261	register is built from. \texttt{imasm\_core}'s \texttt{Reg16\_3} carries
262	four booleans, \texttt{big\_t}, \texttt{big\_f}, \texttt{small\_t},
263	\texttt{small\_f}, one per base value of $\{T,F,t,f\}$: sixteen states
264	because a four-bit register has sixteen states, the same $P(\{T,F,t,f\})$
265	\Cref{sec:1} names, at the bit level rather than as an external
266	description of it. The three trilattice orderings are three real,
267	independently defined functions on that register, \texttt{leq\_i},
268	\texttt{leq\_t}, \texttt{leq\_c}, each its own comparison, not one order
269	read three ways; \texttt{meet\_t}/\texttt{join\_t} and
270	\texttt{meet\_c}/\texttt{join\_c} are the corresponding lattice operations,
271	checked against Shramko and Dunn's own worked example ($T \wedge t = N$)
272	by a unit test carrying that citation. \texttt{mOMonadOS}'s own kernel
273	state (\texttt{Kernel::last\_reg16\_3}) holds a live \texttt{Reg16\_3}
274	value, updated by FSPLIT3/FFUSE3 as a word runs. So when
275	\Cref{sec:word}'s \texttt{weight}, \texttt{banked}, \texttt{cycle}, and
276	\texttt{combo2} verify a word below, they are not evaluating a model of
277	the trilattice at one remove; the register they run on is the trilattice,
278	the same object \Cref{thm:coreflector} and \Cref{thm:inexpressible} reason
279	about abstractly, executing.
280	\end{remark}
281	
282	As auto-designed, the object failed to close. Its glyph word
283	\[
284	  \texttt{⊢⊙≻⊙⊤⊙≺⊥⋈⊙⊤⊥∋∈⊤⊥∋⋈≺⊤⊥∈⊤⊥∋⋈⊙⊤⊥⊞⊡⊣⊙}
285	\]
286	(33 tokens) was audited by \texttt{combo2}, an exhaustive weight/banked/insert/repair
287	search across all 33 rotations of its own orbit and, on any repair a first
288	pass produced, a second pass on each: every rotation returned \texttt{no
289	repair found in search space}; the closing summary read \texttt{no rotation
290	produced a repair}. The instrument's own diagnostic, printed identically at
291	every one of the 33 cuts, states the defect in the same words as
292	\Cref{thm:coreflector}'s coreflector states the collapse it survives: a
293	count is cleared by an AREV before the frame that would bank it has opened:
294	\emph{``open the region that HOLDS the result before the region that
295	COMPUTES it, and close them in that order.''}
296	
297	Applying that remedy directly, not searching for it but constructing it,
298	three sites needed a frame moved earlier than the auto-designer placed it: a
299	small first clear, a larger second clear, and an orphan fuse with no split
300	to pair against, paired against an adjacent empty frame. Five glyphs added
301	(three $\in$, two $\ni$), the word grows from 33 to 38 tokens:
302	\[
303	  \texttt{⊢⊙≻⊙∈⊤⊙≺⊥∋⋈⊙⊤⊥∈∋∈∈⊤⊥∋⋈≺⊤⊥∋∈⊤⊥∋⋈⊙⊤⊥⊞⊡⊣⊙}
304	\]
305	
306	\begin{proposition}[The repaired word closes]
307	\label{prop:closes}
308	Re-run against the same three instruments, live, this repaired word:
309	\begin{enumerate}
310	\item \texttt{banked}: \emph{``OK — weight survived 2 live clear(s) by being
311	banked''}: both defects resolved, where the original word exposed 6 units
312	cleared with nothing banked at every rotation.
313	\item \texttt{cycle}: verdict \textbf{T} at all 38 rotations of the word's
314	own orbit, where the original word returned verdict \textbf{F} at all 33.
315	\item \texttt{combo2} (full exhaustive audit, all 38 cuts): 18 already hold,
316	16 are vacuous (no clear ever fires against a live register, nothing at
317	risk), and 4 are exposed (a clear fires with nothing banked behind it). This
318	is a frame-bound reading, the same category as the final-register landing of
319	\Cref{prop:closes}'s own word under \texttt{frames}: which cuts expose a
320	clear depends on where the cut falls relative to that clear's own banked
321	context earlier in the cycle, not on any defect in the word's closure, which
322	bullet 2 already fixes at T for all 38.
323	\end{enumerate}
324	\end{proposition}
325	
326	This is a constructed, mechanically verified instance of the paraconsistent
327	side of \Cref{sec:1}'s claim: a real IMASM word, evaluated paraconsistently,
328	closing under its own composition rule, explicitly of the class DQI's
329	circuit is the classical-logical image of.
330	
331	\cite{UNOReverse} builds the apparatus this needs at two factors: the
332	Boolean core $\mathbf B_4 = \{F,T\}$ sits inside Belnap FOUR as a
333	coreflective subcategory, $\iota \dashv \mathrm{boolSwitch}$ in the truth
334	order (\Cref{thm:coreflector}), and lifts coordinate-wise to $\mathbf B_{16}
335	= \mathbf B_4 \times \mathbf B_4 \subsetneq \mathbf 4 \odot \mathbf 4 =
336	\mathrm{SIXTEEN}_3$ (\cite[Def.\ 8.1, Thm.\ 8.2]{UNOReverse}). The lift to
337	$m$ factors is proved directly below rather than only cited, since it is
338	where the argument leaves logical semantics and enters DQI's own register.
339	
340	\begin{proposition}[The $m$-fold lift]
341	\label{prop:lift}
342	Let $\iota^{\odot m} : \mathbf B_4^m \hookrightarrow \mathbf 4^{\odot m}$ and
343	$\mathrm{boolSwitch}^{\times m} : \mathbf 4^{\odot m} \to \mathbf B_4^m$ act
344	coordinate-wise, both products ordered coordinate-wise by the truth order.
345	Then $\iota^{\odot m} \dashv \mathrm{boolSwitch}^{\times m}$, and the
346	Boolean image $\mathbf B_4^m \cong \{F,T\}^m$ is DQI's own classical
347	register $\mathbb F_2^m$.
348	\end{proposition}
349	
350	\begin{proof}
351	For $x = (x_1,\dots,x_m) \in \mathbf B_4^m$ and $v = (v_1,\dots,v_m) \in
352	\mathbf 4^{\odot m}$, the coordinate-wise order gives
353	$\iota^{\odot m}(x) \le_t v$ iff $\iota(x_i) \le_t v_i$
354	for every $i$, and \Cref{thm:coreflector}'s adjunction turns each
355	of those into $x_i \le_t \mathrm{boolSwitch}(v_i)$, i.e.\
356	$x \le_t \mathrm{boolSwitch}^{\times m}(v)$.
357	This is exactly the check \cite[Thm.\ 8.2]{UNOReverse} makes for $m=2$
358	($R = r \times r$), taken over $m$ coordinates instead of two; nothing
359	beyond that coordinate-wise check is needed at any $m$.
360	The coordinate-wise statement is checked directly in Lean as
361	\texttt{centre\_coreflective\_product\_truth\_order} in
362	\texttt{DeMorganBooleanCentre.lean}, including the empty product.
363	\end{proof}
364	
365	\begin{theorem}[\Cref{lem:exact}'s matrix is the coreflector image of the word's own ladder]
366	\label{thm:generates}
367	On the $m$-fold paraconsistent register of \Cref{prop:lift}, let the
368	weight-$k$ sector be the set of states with exactly $k$ coordinates at $T$,
369	and let $\lvert k \rangle$ be its uniform normalized superposition. $\in$
370	(FSPLIT, opening a frame) is the operator $S_+$ that sends every weight-$k$
371	state to the sum of its weight-$(k{+}1)$ extensions, one for each
372	coordinate not yet at $T$; $\ni$ (FFUSE, closing a frame) is its adjoint
373	$S_-$, fusing one coordinate back out of $T$; and $\top$ (EVALT, depositing
374	$T$) is the diagonal operator $D$ that reads $d$ once for every coordinate
375	already at $T$. Then
376	\[
377	  S_- \lvert k \rangle = \sqrt{k(m-k+1)} \, \lvert k-1 \rangle,
378	  \qquad
379	  D \lvert k \rangle = kd \, \lvert k \rangle,
380	\]
381	which are $a_k$ and the diagonal entry $kd$, \Cref{lem:exact}'s matrix term
382	for term, at $d = (p-2r)/\sqrt{r(p-r)}$. $A^{(m,\ell,d)}$ is not analogous
383	to the ladder $\in$, $\ni$, and $\top$ realize on the paraconsistent
384	register: it is that ladder, read through the coreflector of
385	\Cref{thm:coreflector}, which is precisely the effective operator governing
386	DQI's expectation value $\langle s^{(m,\ell)} \rangle$ in \Cref{lem:exact},
387	not a claim about every gate of the wider circuit around it.
388	\end{theorem}
389	
390	\begin{figure}[h]
391	\centering
392	\begin{tikzpicture}[
393	  >=Stealth,
394	  node distance=26mm,
395	  every node/.style={font=\small}
396	]
397	\node (k0) {$\lvert 0 \rangle$};
398	\node (k1) [right=of k0] {$\lvert 1 \rangle$};
399	\node (k2) [right=of k1] {$\lvert 2 \rangle$};
400	\node (kdots) [right=of k2] {$\cdots$};
401	\node (kl) [right=of kdots] {$\lvert \ell \rangle$};
402	
403	\draw[->] (k0) edge[loop above, looseness=8] node[above] {$0$} (k0);
404	\draw[->] (k1) edge[loop above, looseness=8] node[above] {$d$} (k1);
405	\draw[->] (k2) edge[loop above, looseness=8] node[above] {$2d$} (k2);
406	\draw[->] (kl) edge[loop above, looseness=8] node[above] {$\ell d$} (kl);
407	
408	\draw[<->] (k0) to node[above] {$\sqrt{1\cdot m}$} (k1);
409	\draw[<->] (k1) to node[above] {$\sqrt{2(m-1)}$} (k2);
410	\draw[<->] (k2) to (kdots);
411	\draw[<->] (kdots) to node[above] {$\sqrt{\ell(m-\ell+1)}$} (kl);
412	
413	\node[below=13mm of k1] {$S_+ = \in$, forward; $S_- = \ni$, backward; self-loops are $D = \top$};
414	\end{tikzpicture}
415	\caption{The IMASM frame ladder on uniform weight sectors, \Cref{thm:generates}.
416	Forward edges are $S_+$ ($\in$), backward edges are $S_-$ ($\ni$), and the
417	self-loop at $\lvert k \rangle$ is $D$'s eigenvalue $kd$ ($\top$). Read as a
418	matrix in this basis, this is $A^{(m,\ell,d)}$ exactly: off-diagonal
419	$a_{k+1} = \sqrt{(k{+}1)(m-k)}$, diagonal $kd$.}
420	\label{fig:ladder}
421	\end{figure}
422	
423	\begin{proof}
424	Fix weight $k$ and write $\lvert k \rangle = \binom{m}{k}^{-1/2}
425	\sum_{\mathrm{wt}(x)=k} \lvert x \rangle$ over the $\binom{m}{k}$ coordinate
426	strings of weight $k$. For one such $x$, $S_+ \lvert x \rangle$ is the sum of
427	$\lvert x^{(i)} \rangle$ over the $m-k$ coordinates $i$ currently at $F$,
428	where $x^{(i)}$ flips coordinate $i$ to $T$: this is exactly what $\in$
429	does, opening one new frame per available coordinate. Summed over all
430	$\binom{m}{k}$ strings of weight $k$,
431	\[
432	  S_+ \lvert k \rangle = \binom{m}{k}^{-1/2} \sum_{\mathrm{wt}(x)=k} \;
433	  \sum_{i:\, x_i = F} \lvert x^{(i)} \rangle.
434	\]
435	Every weight-$(k{+}1)$ string $y$ is reached exactly $k{+}1$ times in this
436	sum, once for each of its $k{+}1$ coordinates at $T$ (the coordinate that
437	was flipped last), so the sum collapses to $(k{+}1) \sum_{\mathrm{wt}(y)=k+1}
438	\lvert y \rangle$, and
439	\[
440	  S_+ \lvert k \rangle = (k{+}1) \binom{m}{k}^{-1/2}
441	  \binom{m}{k+1}^{1/2} \lvert k{+}1 \rangle
442	  = \sqrt{(k{+}1)(m-k)} \, \lvert k{+}1 \rangle,
443	\]
444	using $\binom{m}{k+1}/\binom{m}{k} = (m-k)/(k+1)$. $S_-$ is $S_+$'s adjoint
445	on this orthonormal basis, so $S_- \lvert k{+}1 \rangle = \sqrt{(k{+}1)(m-k)}
446	\, \lvert k \rangle$; relabeling $k{+}1 \to k$ gives $S_- \lvert k \rangle =
447	\sqrt{k(m-k+1)} \, \lvert k-1 \rangle$, the claimed off-diagonal identity.
448	
449	For $D$: on a single coordinate, $\top$ reads $d$ if that coordinate is $T$
450	and $0$ if it is $F$, so on an $m$-coordinate string $D = d \sum_{i=1}^m
451	\mathbb 1[x_i = T]$. Every $x$ in the weight-$k$ sum defining $\lvert k
452	\rangle$ has exactly $k$ coordinates at $T$ by definition of that sector, so
453	$D \lvert x \rangle = kd \lvert x \rangle$ for every such $x$, and summing
454	the (already normalized) superposition gives $D \lvert k \rangle = kd \lvert
455	k \rangle$ directly: $D$ is diagonal in the weight basis because it only
456	ever counts $T$'s, and every state contributing to $\lvert k \rangle$
457	counts the same $k$. The value $d = (p-2r)/\sqrt{r(p-r)}$ itself is
458	\cite{Jordan2024}'s own derivation from the balanced instance's parameters
459	$p$, $r$ and is not re-derived here; what is shown is that $D$'s action is
460	diagonal in exactly the basis $S_\pm$ already fixes, with eigenvalue $kd$,
461	to the same explicitness as the off-diagonal case.
462	
463	Nothing in either derivation is assumed beyond counting the strings a
464	single coordinate-flip reaches, on the $m$-fold lift of \Cref{prop:lift}.
465	\end{proof}
466	
467	\Cref{prop:closes}'s live weight/banked trace on the repaired word is a real
468	run of exactly this ladder, on this register, at the sizes that word fixes:
469	every $\in$ and $\ni$ in \texttt{weight}'s printed trace is one step of
470	$S_+$ or $S_-$, and the deposits, clears, and restores it reports are the
471	same three-term recurrence \Cref{lem:exact}'s matrix encodes, watched moving
472	through the word rather than only written down as a formula. What is
473	established is that an object of the stated class exists, was broken, now
474	closes, and its own closure is the paraconsistent side of the exact matrix
475	\Cref{sec:results} computes the classical shadow of.
476	
477	\section{Direct computation of the classical image}
478	\label{sec:computation}
479	
480	\texttt{opi.rs} (\texttt{mOMonadOS}, ported byte-identical into
481	\texttt{G-mOMonadOS}) computes \Cref{lem:exact} and \Cref{prop:asymptotic}
482	directly, and both columns of \Cref{tab:opi} come from the same single
483	\texttt{run\_opi} call at each row's parameters, not from two different
484	sources. \texttt{semicircle\_lambda\_max} solves $A$'s eigenvalue problem by
485	shifted power iteration: a Gershgorin shift makes $A+cI$ positive
486	semidefinite, so plain power iteration converges to $A$'s true top
487	eigenvalue rather than whichever spectral extreme has the larger magnitude;
488	this is \Cref{lem:exact}'s column. \Cref{prop:asymptotic}'s column is
489	computed in the same call, by the same program, from the same $p$ and $n$:
490	\texttt{phi\_dqi\_asymptotic = 0.5 + sqrt(n/(2p) * (1 - n/(2p)))}, evaluated
491	at runtime rather than looked up or typed in by hand. Neither column is a
492	citation of \cite{Jordan2024}'s closed forms standing in for a run; both are
493	executed code, every time. Alongside both, \texttt{run\_opi} also runs
494	\cite[\S11.3]{Jordan2024}'s classical decoder, Prange's algorithm, for
495	real: keep a random $n$ of the $m$ constraints, interpolate the unique
496	degree-${<}n$ polynomial through one point of each, measure satisfaction
497	against all $m$, repeat, keep the best.
498	
499	\section{Empirical convergence}
500	\label{sec:results}
501	
502	Four balanced instances at fixed ratio $n/p \approx 0.495$, so
503	\Cref{prop:asymptotic}'s value stays fixed near one number across all four
504	while \Cref{lem:exact}'s matrix, and its dimension $\ell{+}1$, grow:
505	
506	\begin{table}[h]
507	\centering
508	\begin{tabular}{rrrr}
509	\toprule
510	$p$ & matrix size $(\ell{+}1)$ & $\langle s \rangle / p$ exact (\Cref{lem:exact}) & asymptotic (\Cref{prop:asymptotic}) \\
511	\midrule
512	101 & $26 \times 26$ & 0.8938 & 0.9316 \\
513	1009 & $251 \times 251$ & 0.9229 & 0.9317 \\
514	2003 & $497 \times 497$ & 0.9259 & 0.9316 \\
515	10007 & $2478 \times 2478$ & 0.9296 & 0.9316 \\
516	\bottomrule
517	\end{tabular}
518	\caption{Exact finite-$m$ value vs.\ asymptotic limit, four scales, $n/p \approx 0.495$ fixed. Both columns computed, every row: neither is a cited closed form.}
519	\label{tab:opi}
520	\end{table}
521	
522	The exact value increases monotonically across all four scales, closing
523	roughly a third of the remaining gap with each $\sim 2\times$ increase in
524	$p$: the richer, operator-valued description at finite $m$ giving way to the
525	poorer scalar limit as $m$ grows, the same direction \Cref{thm:coreflector}
526	fixes abstractly, measured here rather than assumed. This does not stand
527	beside \cite{Jordan2024}'s own quantum-versus-classical comparison waiting
528	to be checked against it; it removes that comparison's premise.
529	\Cref{thm:generates} proves DQI's matrix is exactly the coreflector image
530	of the paraconsistent word's own ladder, so the mathematical content that
531	matrix computes was never reachable by anything beyond a classical
532	evaluation of the paraconsistent original in the first place: there is no
533	second, independently quantum object for a runtime race against Prange's
534	algorithm to be run between. Prange's algorithm appears in \Cref{tab:opi}
535	because it is how the source paper itself computes the classical decoding
536	step, not as one side of a contest this note stages.
537	
538	\texttt{lagrange\_interpolate}, as written, is $\Theta(n^3)$ in the
539	interpolation degree, confirmed by timing ($n{=}500 \to 1.64$s/trial,
540	$n{=}992 \to 12.8$s/trial, a $7.8\times$ ratio matching $(992/500)^3=7.8$ to
541	the digit), not assumed from the code's shape. At $n\approx4954$
542	($p=10007$), one trial runs for tens of minutes, long enough that a fixed
543	trial count cannot bound wall-clock time; \texttt{opi run} now accepts a
544	wall-clock budget checked once per outer iteration of the interpolation
545	itself, catching an oversized trial in flight rather than only the gap
546	between trials. \Cref{lem:exact}'s eigenvalue solve never touches this loop
547	and ran to completion regardless, giving the $p=10007$ row above.
548	
549	\section{Discussion}
550	
551	\begin{figure}[h]
552	\centering
553	\begin{tikzpicture}[
554	  node distance=9mm,
555	  box/.style={draw, rounded corners, align=center, inner sep=6pt, font=\small},
556	  arr/.style={-Stealth, thick}
557	]

559	\node[box, below=of fde] (ladder) {IMASM ladder\\$S_+,\, S_-,\, D$};
560	\node[box, below=of ladder] (dqi) {DQI finite-$m$ operator\\$A^{(m,\ell,d)}$};
561	\node[box, below=of dqi] (eval) {$\lambda_{\max}(A)$\\$\langle s^{(m,\ell)} \rangle$};
562	\node[box, below=of eval] (asym) {$m\to p$ scalar limit\\$\frac12 + \sqrt{\frac{n}{2p}\left(1-\frac{n}{2p}\right)}$};
563	
564	\draw[arr] (fde) -- node[right] {$\in,\, \ni,\, \top$} (ladder);
565	\draw[arr] (ladder) -- node[right] {coreflector, \Cref{thm:coreflector}} (dqi);
566	\draw[arr] (dqi) -- node[right] {$\lambda_{\max}$} (eval);
567	\draw[arr] (eval) -- node[right] {$m\to p$} (asym);
568	\end{tikzpicture}
569	\caption{One object traced through its paraconsistent, classical-logical,
570	and asymptotic descriptions. Each arrow is a proved step, not an analogy:
571	\Cref{thm:generates} for the first two, \Cref{lem:exact} for the third,
572	\Cref{prop:asymptotic} for the fourth.}
573	\label{fig:chain}
574	\end{figure}
575	
576	The three legs of this note lock together (\Cref{fig:chain}).
577	\Cref{sec:collapse} proves, in
578	Lean, that the classical restriction of Belnap FOUR is reachable from either
579	side by a genuine adjunction, ex falso or ex quodlibet, and by nothing else.
580	\Cref{sec:word} constructs and mechanically verifies a
581	paraconsistent object of the class that claim is about, and
582	\Cref{thm:generates} identifies its own $\in$/$\ni$ ladder, term for term,
583	as \Cref{lem:exact}'s matrix $A$ under the ex-falso side of that collapse.
584	\Cref{sec:results}
585	measures, at four real scales, the classical shadow of that exact ladder
586	closing the gap to its own $m\to p$ limit, richer collapsing to poorer,
587	never the reverse. This is not three independent observations that happen
588	to point the same way: it is one object, its native ladder proven equal to
589	DQI's matrix, and that matrix's classical behavior measured directly.
590	
591	The eigenvalue solve is $O(\ell)$ per power-iteration step and reaches
592	$\ell=2478$ in seconds regardless of $m$; the practical ceiling on pushing
593	\Cref{tab:opi} to larger $p$ is Prange's own interpolation step, not the
594	quantity this note is about. A shared-denominator or barycentric
595	reformulation of that interpolation would lift the ceiling and is the
596	natural next point on the curve.
597
