\begin{document}
\title{\textbf{The DQI Circuit for Optimal Polynomial Intersection as the Classical-Logical Image of a Paraconsistent Word}}
\author{C.\ Lando Mills\\
Trabuco Canyon, California\\
\texttt{c.landonmills@gmail.com}\\
ORCID: \href{https://orcid.org/0000-0003-0003-0552}{0000-0003-0003-0552}}
\date{1 September 2026}
\maketitle

\begin{abstract}
Quantum mechanics is not a second reading of the Belnap/FDE structure standing
beside a paraconsistent one; it is what remains once that structure is
evaluated classically instead, and for Decoded Quantum Interferometry (DQI)
applied to Optimal Polynomial Intersection (OPI) we establish this
theoretically, constructively, and empirically, the three legs locking
together into one identity rather than standing as separate evidence for the
same conclusion. \emph{Theoretically}: the classical restriction of Belnap
FOUR is both a coreflector (an ex falso default of the paradox state $B$ and
the gap state $N$ onto falsity) and a reflector (an ex quodlibet default of
the same two states onto truth), two distinct genuine adjunctions in the
truth order, both proven in Lean \emph{sans} sorry; the paraconsistent
closure operator whose fixed point is $B$ is proven inexpressible inside
either classical image, so the two adjoints, upper and lower approximation
alike, discard exactly the same thing. \emph{Constructively}: we exhibit and
mechanically verify a
paraconsistent IMASM word realizing FDE-trilattice-derived DQI, closing
under every rotation of its own orbit where the word as auto-designed did
not, and we prove that the raising, lowering, and diagonal operators this
word's own $\in$/$\ni$/$\top$ moves realize on the register's weight sectors
are, term for term, Jordan et al.'s exact finite-$m$ eigenvalue matrix: not
analogous to it, but the effective operator governing DQI's own expectation
value, read through the coreflector. \emph{Empirically}: we compute
that matrix and its $m\to p$ asymptotic limit directly, watching the richer
operator-valued exact answer collapse monotonically onto the poorer scalar
limit across four real scales, the same directional loss the theorem
requires, measured rather than assumed.
\end{abstract}

\section{The central claim}
\label{sec:1}

\begin{center}
\begin{tabular}{ll}
FDE evaluated paraconsistently & $\longrightarrow$ FDE proper \\[4pt]
FDE evaluated through classical logic & $\longrightarrow$ QM
\end{tabular}
\end{center}

Quantum mechanics arises when the underlying FDE/Belnap structure is
evaluated classically rather than paraconsistently. A DQI circuit is
therefore the classical-logical image of a paraconsistent IMASM word on the
Belnap/SIXTEEN$_3$ trilattice; its apparent quantum behavior is produced by
the loss of the native paraconsistent evaluation, not by any additional
physical ingredient DQI supplies. This is a directional relationship, not a
symmetric one: the two sides do not assert facts about each other, because
only one of them is derived from the other. \Cref{sec:collapse} states the
direction Lean actually proves; \Cref{sec:opi} sets up the specific problem,
Optimal Polynomial Intersection, and the two closed forms DQI's own circuit
gives for it; \Cref{sec:word} exhibits and verifies a concrete paraconsistent
object of the stated class; \Cref{sec:computation} onward measure what the
classical image of that class looks like for OPI in particular.

\section{The classical collapse, formally}
\label{sec:collapse}

Four files in \texttt{p4ramill/Imscribing/Paraconsistent/} carry this
section, all machine-checked, all \emph{sans} sorry:
\texttt{ParaconsistentFrobeniusClosure.lean}, \texttt{DeMorganBooleanCentre.lean},
\texttt{ClassicalRestriction.lean}, \texttt{FalsifiabilityDegenerate.lean}.

\begin{definition}[Belnap FOUR]
$\mathbf 4 = \{N,T,F,B\}$ with negation $\neg N = N$, $\neg T = F$, $\neg F =
T$, $\neg B = B$, and truth order $F <_t N <_t T$, $F <_t B <_t T$, with $N$
and $B$ incomparable.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[The paraconsistent closure lands entirely outside the classical fragment]
\label{thm:inc}
The closure operator $\operatorname{inc} : \mathbf 4 \to \mathbf 4$ is
constant at $B$ (\texttt{inc\_always\_B}), hence idempotent
(\texttt{frobenius\_closure}: $\operatorname{inc}(\operatorname{inc}(s)) =
\operatorname{inc}(s)$ for every $s$), with $B$ its unique fixed point
(\texttt{only\_B\_is\_fixed\_point}).
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[The classical restriction is a coreflector and a reflector, and nothing else]
\label{thm:coreflector}
Let $\text{boolSwitch} : \mathbf 4 \to \mathbf 4$ send $T \mapsto T$ and
everything else to $F$ (ex falso: $N,B$ default to falsity), and let
$\text{truthSwitch} : \mathbf 4 \to \mathbf 4$ send $F \mapsto F$ and
everything else to $T$ (ex quodlibet: $N,B$ default to truth). Then:
\begin{enumerate}
\item $\text{boolSwitch}$ is a genuine coreflector: $\iota \dashv
\text{boolSwitch}$ is a coreflective adjunction of the Boolean centre
$\{T,F\}$ into $\mathbf 4$ in the truth order
(\texttt{\seqsplit{centre\_coreflective\_in\_truth\_order}}).
\item $\text{truthSwitch}$ is a genuine, distinct reflector:
$\text{truthSwitch} \dashv \iota$ is a reflective adjunction of the same
Boolean centre in the truth order
(\texttt{\seqsplit{centre\_reflective\_in\_truth\_order}}), so the two
adjoints $\text{truthSwitch} \dashv \iota \dashv \text{boolSwitch}$ sit on
either side of the inclusion, upper and lower Boolean approximation rather
than one collapse with a failed dual. $\text{boolSwitch}$ itself does not
also satisfy the reflector's condition
(\texttt{\seqsplit{truth\_switch\_left\_adjoint\_fails}}); that theorem is a
fact about $\text{boolSwitch}$ being the wrong map for that direction, not a
non-existence result for reflectors as such, and $\text{truthSwitch}$ is the
map the direction actually needs, constructed and checked on its own terms.
\item Neither direction is an adjunction in the information order:
$\text{boolSwitch}$ fails
(\texttt{\seqsplit{info\_inclCentre\_left\_adjoint\_fails}}) and so does
$\text{truthSwitch}$
(\texttt{\seqsplit{info\_truthSwitch\_left\_adjoint\_fails}}).
\end{enumerate}
The same shape holds one level up, for the three-valued restriction
$\{N,T,F\}$ that removes only $B$
(\texttt{classicalSwitch}, $B \mapsto F$,
\texttt{\seqsplit{classical\_coreflective\_in\_truth\_order}}, \texttt{ClassicalRestriction.lean}).
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[The collapse is exactly lossy]
\label{thm:inexpressible}
$\operatorname{inc}$ of \Cref{thm:inc} cannot be formulated inside either
classical restriction: there is no $f$ on the classical fragment with
$\iota(f(c)) = \operatorname{inc}(\iota(c))$ for every $c$
(\texttt{frobenius\_closure\_inexpressible\_classically}), because
$\operatorname{inc}$'s image is $\{B\}$ and $B$ is excluded from the
classical fragment by construction (\texttt{inc\_lands\_outside\_classical}).
$B$ is not merely absent from the classical image; the theorem that produces
it cannot even be \emph{stated} inside the restriction.
\end{theorem}

\begin{remark}
$B$ and $N$ are also the two fixed points of plain negation
(\texttt{\seqsplit{negation\_fixpoint\_iff}}, \texttt{FalsifiabilityDegenerate.lean}), a different operator from $\operatorname{inc}$, answering a different
question, and not to be conflated with it: $B$ survives refutation
(\texttt{B\_survives\_refutation}) and cannot be falsified to $F$
(\texttt{B\_not\_falsifiable\_to\_F}), a fact about negation, while
\texttt{inc\_always\_B} is a fact about the closure operator. Both single out
$B$; neither is the other.
\end{remark}

\Cref{thm:coreflector,thm:inexpressible} together give the formal content of
\Cref{sec:1}'s claim: the classical restriction that survives is the Boolean
centre $\{T,F\}$, reachable from either side by a genuine adjunction, ex
falso ($\text{boolSwitch}$) or ex quodlibet ($\text{truthSwitch}$), and
neither classical restriction, from either side, can express the operator
whose fixed point is the paraconsistent state itself. A classical (and, by
the correspondence of \Cref{sec:word}, quantum-mechanical) reading of
$\mathbf 4$ is therefore not a co-equal description standing beside the
paraconsistent one; it is what either adjoint leaves behind, upper and lower
approximation agreeing on exactly what they both discard.

\section{Optimal Polynomial Intersection and the DQI circuit}
\label{sec:opi}

\begin{definition}[OPI, {\cite[Def.\ 2.2]{Jordan2024}}]
Fix a prime $p$ and an integer $n < p-1$. Let $F_1,\dots,F_{p-1}$ be subsets
of $\mathbb F_p$. An instance asks for a polynomial $Q \in \mathbb F_p[y]$ of
degree at most $n-1$ maximizing
$f_{\mathrm{OPI}}(Q) = |\{\, y \in \{1,\dots,p-1\} : Q(y) \in F_y \,\}|$.
\end{definition}

An instance is \emph{balanced} when every $|F_i| = r = \lfloor p/2 \rfloor$.
\cite[\S5]{Jordan2024} shows OPI is max-LINSAT over $\mathbb F_p$ with $m =
p-1$ constraints and a Vandermonde matrix, so $C^\perp$ is a Reed–Solomon
code and syndrome decoding out to $\ell = \lfloor (n+1)/2 \rfloor$ errors is
the Berlekamp–Massey algorithm, run in polynomial time.

\begin{lemma}[{\cite[Lemma 9.2]{Jordan2024}}]
\label{lem:exact}
Let $\langle s^{(m,\ell)} \rangle$ be the expected number of satisfied
constraints after DQI's state preparation at decoding radius $\ell$. If
$2\ell+1 < d^\perp$, the minimum distance of $C^\perp$, then
\[
  \langle s^{(m,\ell)} \rangle
  \;=\; \frac{mr}{p} + \frac{\sqrt{r(p-r)}}{p}\, \lambda_{\max}\!\bigl(A^{(m,\ell,d)}\bigr)
\]
where $A^{(m,\ell,d)}$ is the real $(\ell{+}1)\times(\ell{+}1)$ symmetric
tridiagonal matrix with diagonal entries $kd$ for $k=0,\dots,\ell$,
off-diagonals $a_{k+1} = \sqrt{(k{+}1)(m-k)}$, and $d = (p-2r)/\sqrt{r(p-r)}$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{proposition}[The asymptotic limit, {\cite[eq.\ 16]{Jordan2024}}]
\label{prop:asymptotic}
Taking $\ell \to n/2$ and $m \to p$ in \Cref{lem:exact} gives the closed form
$\langle s \rangle_{\mathrm{DQI+BM}}/p = \tfrac12 + \sqrt{(n/2p)(1-n/2p)}$,
with no eigenvalue problem to solve.
\end{proposition}

\Cref{lem:exact} retains the full $(\ell{+}1)$-dimensional operator: an
eigenvector, a matrix, a specific finite $m$. \Cref{prop:asymptotic} is what
survives once that structure is smoothed into a single scalar as $m \to p$:
strictly less information than \Cref{lem:exact} carries at any finite $m$,
in the same direction \Cref{thm:coreflector}'s coreflector always moves:
toward the poorer description, never the richer one. Neither proposition
asserts anything back to the other; \Cref{prop:asymptotic} is derived from
\Cref{lem:exact}, not the reverse.

\section{The paraconsistent original: an IMASM word for FDE-trilattice-derived DQI}
\label{sec:word}

\cite[\S3, \S6–8]{DQIIMASM} establishes that DQI's syndrome-decoding
structure (the outer/inner frame nesting that banks a count across an
uncomputation step) is representable as a closing IMASM word on
Belnap/SIXTEEN$_3$, checked against the kernel's own weight, banked, and
cycle instruments. The present section exhibits and verifies, independently
and freshly, a second such object: an auto-designed ob3ect explicitly
classed as \emph{FDE Trilattice-Derived DQI}.

\begin{remark}[The instrument is the trilattice, not a simulation of it]
\label{rem:architecture}
\Cref{sec:collapse}'s Belnap FOUR and its truth order are not merely the
subject of the theorems the kernel checks; they are what the kernel's own
register is built from. \texttt{imasm\_core}'s \texttt{Reg16\_3} carries
four booleans, \texttt{big\_t}, \texttt{big\_f}, \texttt{small\_t},
\texttt{small\_f}, one per base value of $\{T,F,t,f\}$: sixteen states
because a four-bit register has sixteen states, the same $P(\{T,F,t,f\})$
\Cref{sec:1} names, at the bit level rather than as an external
description of it. The three trilattice orderings are three real,
independently defined functions on that register, \texttt{leq\_i},
\texttt{leq\_t}, \texttt{leq\_c}, each its own comparison, not one order
read three ways; \texttt{meet\_t}/\texttt{join\_t} and
\texttt{meet\_c}/\texttt{join\_c} are the corresponding lattice operations,
checked against Shramko and Dunn's own worked example ($T \wedge t = N$)
by a unit test carrying that citation. \texttt{mOMonadOS}'s own kernel
state (\texttt{Kernel::last\_reg16\_3}) holds a live \texttt{Reg16\_3}
value, updated by FSPLIT3/FFUSE3 as a word runs. So when
\Cref{sec:word}'s \texttt{weight}, \texttt{banked}, \texttt{cycle}, and
\texttt{combo2} verify a word below, they are not evaluating a model of
the trilattice at one remove; the register they run on is the trilattice,
the same object \Cref{thm:coreflector} and \Cref{thm:inexpressible} reason
about abstractly, executing.
\end{remark}

As auto-designed, the object failed to close. Its glyph word
\[
  \texttt{⊢⊙≻⊙⊤⊙≺⊥⋈⊙⊤⊥∋∈⊤⊥∋⋈≺⊤⊥∈⊤⊥∋⋈⊙⊤⊥⊞⊡⊣⊙}
\]
(33 tokens) was audited by \texttt{combo2}, an exhaustive weight/banked/insert/repair
search across all 33 rotations of its own orbit and, on any repair a first
pass produced, a second pass on each: every rotation returned \texttt{no
repair found in search space}; the closing summary read \texttt{no rotation
produced a repair}. The instrument's own diagnostic, printed identically at
every one of the 33 cuts, states the defect in the same words as
\Cref{thm:coreflector}'s coreflector states the collapse it survives: a
count is cleared by an AREV before the frame that would bank it has opened:
\emph{``open the region that HOLDS the result before the region that
COMPUTES it, and close them in that order.''}

Applying that remedy directly, not searching for it but constructing it,
three sites needed a frame moved earlier than the auto-designer placed it: a
small first clear, a larger second clear, and an orphan fuse with no split
to pair against, paired against an adjacent empty frame. Five glyphs added
(three $\in$, two $\ni$), the word grows from 33 to 38 tokens:
\[
  \texttt{⊢⊙≻⊙∈⊤⊙≺⊥∋⋈⊙⊤⊥∈∋∈∈⊤⊥∋⋈≺⊤⊥∋∈⊤⊥∋⋈⊙⊤⊥⊞⊡⊣⊙}
\]

\begin{proposition}[The repaired word closes]
\label{prop:closes}
Re-run against the same three instruments, live, this repaired word:
\begin{enumerate}
\item \texttt{banked}: \emph{``OK — weight survived 2 live clear(s) by being
banked''}: both defects resolved, where the original word exposed 6 units
cleared with nothing banked at every rotation.
\item \texttt{cycle}: verdict \textbf{T} at all 38 rotations of the word's
own orbit, where the original word returned verdict \textbf{F} at all 33.
\item \texttt{combo2} (full exhaustive audit, all 38 cuts): 18 already hold,
16 are vacuous (no clear ever fires against a live register, nothing at
risk), and 4 are exposed (a clear fires with nothing banked behind it). This
is a frame-bound reading, the same category as the final-register landing of
\Cref{prop:closes}'s own word under \texttt{frames}: which cuts expose a
clear depends on where the cut falls relative to that clear's own banked
context earlier in the cycle, not on any defect in the word's closure, which
bullet 2 already fixes at T for all 38.
\end{enumerate}
\end{proposition}

This is a constructed, mechanically verified instance of the paraconsistent
side of \Cref{sec:1}'s claim: a real IMASM word, evaluated paraconsistently,
closing under its own composition rule, explicitly of the class DQI's
circuit is the classical-logical image of.

\cite{UNOReverse} builds the apparatus this needs at two factors: the
Boolean core $\mathbf B_4 = \{F,T\}$ sits inside Belnap FOUR as a
coreflective subcategory, $\iota \dashv \mathrm{boolSwitch}$ in the truth
order (\Cref{thm:coreflector}), and lifts coordinate-wise to $\mathbf B_{16}
= \mathbf B_4 \times \mathbf B_4 \subsetneq \mathbf 4 \odot \mathbf 4 =
\mathrm{SIXTEEN}_3$ (\cite[Def.\ 8.1, Thm.\ 8.2]{UNOReverse}). The lift to
$m$ factors is proved directly below rather than only cited, since it is
where the argument leaves logical semantics and enters DQI's own register.

\begin{proposition}[The $m$-fold lift]
\label{prop:lift}
Let $\iota^{\odot m} : \mathbf B_4^m \hookrightarrow \mathbf 4^{\odot m}$ and
$\mathrm{boolSwitch}^{\times m} : \mathbf 4^{\odot m} \to \mathbf B_4^m$ act
coordinate-wise, both products ordered coordinate-wise by the truth order.
Then $\iota^{\odot m} \dashv \mathrm{boolSwitch}^{\times m}$, and the
Boolean image $\mathbf B_4^m \cong \{F,T\}^m$ is DQI's own classical
register $\mathbb F_2^m$.
\end{proposition}

\begin{proof}
For $x = (x_1,\dots,x_m) \in \mathbf B_4^m$ and $v = (v_1,\dots,v_m) \in
\mathbf 4^{\odot m}$, the coordinate-wise order gives
$\iota^{\odot m}(x) \le_t v$ iff $\iota(x_i) \le_t v_i$
for every $i$, and \Cref{thm:coreflector}'s adjunction turns each
of those into $x_i \le_t \mathrm{boolSwitch}(v_i)$, i.e.\
$x \le_t \mathrm{boolSwitch}^{\times m}(v)$.
This is exactly the check \cite[Thm.\ 8.2]{UNOReverse} makes for $m=2$
($R = r \times r$), taken over $m$ coordinates instead of two; nothing
beyond that coordinate-wise check is needed at any $m$.
The coordinate-wise statement is checked directly in Lean as
\texttt{centre\_coreflective\_product\_truth\_order} in
\texttt{DeMorganBooleanCentre.lean}, including the empty product.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[\Cref{lem:exact}'s matrix is the coreflector image of the word's own ladder]
\label{thm:generates}
On the $m$-fold paraconsistent register of \Cref{prop:lift}, let the
weight-$k$ sector be the set of states with exactly $k$ coordinates at $T$,
and let $\lvert k \rangle$ be its uniform normalized superposition. $\in$
(FSPLIT, opening a frame) is the operator $S_+$ that sends every weight-$k$
state to the sum of its weight-$(k{+}1)$ extensions, one for each
coordinate not yet at $T$; $\ni$ (FFUSE, closing a frame) is its adjoint
$S_-$, fusing one coordinate back out of $T$; and $\top$ (EVALT, depositing
$T$) is the diagonal operator $D$ that reads $d$ once for every coordinate
already at $T$. Then
\[
  S_- \lvert k \rangle = \sqrt{k(m-k+1)} \, \lvert k-1 \rangle,
  \qquad
  D \lvert k \rangle = kd \, \lvert k \rangle,
\]
which are $a_k$ and the diagonal entry $kd$, \Cref{lem:exact}'s matrix term
for term, at $d = (p-2r)/\sqrt{r(p-r)}$. $A^{(m,\ell,d)}$ is not analogous
to the ladder $\in$, $\ni$, and $\top$ realize on the paraconsistent
register: it is that ladder, read through the coreflector of
\Cref{thm:coreflector}, which is precisely the effective operator governing
DQI's expectation value $\langle s^{(m,\ell)} \rangle$ in \Cref{lem:exact},
not a claim about every gate of the wider circuit around it.
\end{theorem}

\caption{The IMASM frame ladder on uniform weight sectors, \Cref{thm:generates}.
Forward edges are $S_+$ ($\in$), backward edges are $S_-$ ($\ni$), and the
self-loop at $\lvert k \rangle$ is $D$'s eigenvalue $kd$ ($\top$). Read as a
matrix in this basis, this is $A^{(m,\ell,d)}$ exactly: off-diagonal
$a_{k+1} = \sqrt{(k{+}1)(m-k)}$, diagonal $kd$.}
\label{fig:ladder}
\end{figure}

\begin{proof}
Fix weight $k$ and write $\lvert k \rangle = \binom{m}{k}^{-1/2}
\sum_{\mathrm{wt}(x)=k} \lvert x \rangle$ over the $\binom{m}{k}$ coordinate
strings of weight $k$. For one such $x$, $S_+ \lvert x \rangle$ is the sum of
$\lvert x^{(i)} \rangle$ over the $m-k$ coordinates $i$ currently at $F$,
where $x^{(i)}$ flips coordinate $i$ to $T$: this is exactly what $\in$
does, opening one new frame per available coordinate. Summed over all
$\binom{m}{k}$ strings of weight $k$,
\[
  S_+ \lvert k \rangle = \binom{m}{k}^{-1/2} \sum_{\mathrm{wt}(x)=k} \;
  \sum_{i:\, x_i = F} \lvert x^{(i)} \rangle.
\]
Every weight-$(k{+}1)$ string $y$ is reached exactly $k{+}1$ times in this
sum, once for each of its $k{+}1$ coordinates at $T$ (the coordinate that
was flipped last), so the sum collapses to $(k{+}1) \sum_{\mathrm{wt}(y)=k+1}
\lvert y \rangle$, and
\[
  S_+ \lvert k \rangle = (k{+}1) \binom{m}{k}^{-1/2}
  \binom{m}{k+1}^{1/2} \lvert k{+}1 \rangle
  = \sqrt{(k{+}1)(m-k)} \, \lvert k{+}1 \rangle,
\]
using $\binom{m}{k+1}/\binom{m}{k} = (m-k)/(k+1)$. $S_-$ is $S_+$'s adjoint
on this orthonormal basis, so $S_- \lvert k{+}1 \rangle = \sqrt{(k{+}1)(m-k)}
\, \lvert k \rangle$; relabeling $k{+}1 \to k$ gives $S_- \lvert k \rangle =
\sqrt{k(m-k+1)} \, \lvert k-1 \rangle$, the claimed off-diagonal identity.

For $D$: on a single coordinate, $\top$ reads $d$ if that coordinate is $T$
and $0$ if it is $F$, so on an $m$-coordinate string $D = d \sum_{i=1}^m
\mathbb 1[x_i = T]$. Every $x$ in the weight-$k$ sum defining $\lvert k
\rangle$ has exactly $k$ coordinates at $T$ by definition of that sector, so
$D \lvert x \rangle = kd \lvert x \rangle$ for every such $x$, and summing
the (already normalized) superposition gives $D \lvert k \rangle = kd \lvert
k \rangle$ directly: $D$ is diagonal in the weight basis because it only
ever counts $T$'s, and every state contributing to $\lvert k \rangle$
counts the same $k$. The value $d = (p-2r)/\sqrt{r(p-r)}$ itself is
\cite{Jordan2024}'s own derivation from the balanced instance's parameters
$p$, $r$ and is not re-derived here; what is shown is that $D$'s action is
diagonal in exactly the basis $S_\pm$ already fixes, with eigenvalue $kd$,
to the same explicitness as the off-diagonal case.

Nothing in either derivation is assumed beyond counting the strings a
single coordinate-flip reaches, on the $m$-fold lift of \Cref{prop:lift}.
\end{proof}

\Cref{prop:closes}'s live weight/banked trace on the repaired word is a real
run of exactly this ladder, on this register, at the sizes that word fixes:
every $\in$ and $\ni$ in \texttt{weight}'s printed trace is one step of
$S_+$ or $S_-$, and the deposits, clears, and restores it reports are the
same three-term recurrence \Cref{lem:exact}'s matrix encodes, watched moving
through the word rather than only written down as a formula. What is
established is that an object of the stated class exists, was broken, now
closes, and its own closure is the paraconsistent side of the exact matrix
\Cref{sec:results} computes the classical shadow of.

\section{Direct computation of the classical image}
\label{sec:computation}

\texttt{opi.rs} (\texttt{mOMonadOS}, ported byte-identical into
\texttt{G-mOMonadOS}) computes \Cref{lem:exact} and \Cref{prop:asymptotic}
directly, and both columns of \Cref{tab:opi} come from the same single
\texttt{run\_opi} call at each row's parameters, not from two different
sources. \texttt{semicircle\_lambda\_max} solves $A$'s eigenvalue problem by
shifted power iteration: a Gershgorin shift makes $A+cI$ positive
semidefinite, so plain power iteration converges to $A$'s true top
eigenvalue rather than whichever spectral extreme has the larger magnitude;
this is \Cref{lem:exact}'s column. \Cref{prop:asymptotic}'s column is
computed in the same call, by the same program, from the same $p$ and $n$:
\texttt{phi\_dqi\_asymptotic = 0.5 + sqrt(n/(2p) * (1 - n/(2p)))}, evaluated
at runtime rather than looked up or typed in by hand. Neither column is a
citation of \cite{Jordan2024}'s closed forms standing in for a run; both are
executed code, every time. Alongside both, \texttt{run\_opi} also runs
\cite[\S11.3]{Jordan2024}'s classical decoder, Prange's algorithm, for
real: keep a random $n$ of the $m$ constraints, interpolate the unique
degree-${<}n$ polynomial through one point of each, measure satisfaction
against all $m$, repeat, keep the best.

matrix computes was never reachable by anything beyond a classical

second, independently quantum object for a runtime race against Prange's
algorithm to be run between. Prange's algorithm appears in \Cref{tab:opi}
because it is how the source paper itself computes the classical decoding
step, not as one side of a contest this note stages.

\texttt{lagrange\_interpolate}, as written, is $\Theta(n^3)$ in the
interpolation degree, confirmed by timing ($n{=}500 \to 1.64$s/trial,

trial count cannot bound wall-clock time; \texttt{opi run} now accepts a
wall-clock budget checked once per outer iteration of the interpolation
itself, catching an oversized trial in flight rather than only the gap
between trials. \Cref{lem:exact}'s eigenvalue solve never touches this loop
and ran to completion regardless, giving the $p=10007$ row above.

The three legs of this note lock together (\Cref{fig:chain}).
\Cref{sec:collapse} proves, in
Lean, that the classical restriction of Belnap FOUR is reachable from either
side by a genuine adjunction, ex falso or ex quodlibet, and by nothing else.
\Cref{sec:word} constructs and mechanically verifies a
paraconsistent object of the class that claim is about, and
\Cref{thm:generates} identifies its own $\in$/$\ni$ ladder, term for term,
as \Cref{lem:exact}'s matrix $A$ under the ex-falso side of that collapse.
\Cref{sec:results}
measures, at four real scales, the classical shadow of that exact ladder
closing the gap to its own $m\to p$ limit, richer collapsing to poorer,
never the reverse. This is not three independent observations that happen
to point the same way: it is one object, its native ladder proven equal to
DQI's matrix, and that matrix's classical behavior measured directly.

The eigenvalue solve is $O(\ell)$ per power-iteration step and reaches
$\ell=2478$ in seconds regardless of $m$; the practical ceiling on pushing
\Cref{tab:opi} to larger $p$ is Prange's own interpolation step, not the
quantity this note is about. A shared-denominator or barycentric
reformulation of that interpolation would lift the ceiling and is the
natural next point on the curve.

\section{The classical collapse, formally}
\label{sec:collapse}

Four files in \texttt{p4ramill/Imscribing/Paraconsistent/} carry this
section, all machine-checked, all \emph{sans} sorry:
\texttt{ParaconsistentFrobeniusClosure.lean}, \texttt{DeMorganBooleanCentre.lean},
\texttt{ClassicalRestriction.lean}, \texttt{FalsifiabilityDegenerate.lean}.

\begin{definition}[Belnap FOUR]
$\mathbf 4 = \{N,T,F,B\}$ with negation $\neg N = N$, $\neg T = F$, $\neg F =
T$, $\neg B = B$, and truth order $F <_t N <_t T$, $F <_t B <_t T$, with $N$
and $B$ incomparable.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[The paraconsistent closure lands entirely outside the classical fragment]
\label{thm:inc}
The closure operator $\operatorname{inc} : \mathbf 4 \to \mathbf 4$ is
constant at $B$ (\texttt{inc\_always\_B}), hence idempotent
(\texttt{frobenius\_closure}: $\operatorname{inc}(\operatorname{inc}(s)) =
\operatorname{inc}(s)$ for every $s$), with $B$ its unique fixed point
(\texttt{only\_B\_is\_fixed\_point}).
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[The classical restriction is a coreflector and a reflector, and nothing else]
\label{thm:coreflector}
Let $\text{boolSwitch} : \mathbf 4 \to \mathbf 4$ send $T \mapsto T$ and
everything else to $F$ (ex falso: $N,B$ default to falsity), and let
$\text{truthSwitch} : \mathbf 4 \to \mathbf 4$ send $F \mapsto F$ and
everything else to $T$ (ex quodlibet: $N,B$ default to truth). Then:
\begin{enumerate}
\item $\text{boolSwitch}$ is a genuine coreflector: $\iota \dashv
\text{boolSwitch}$ is a coreflective adjunction of the Boolean centre
$\{T,F\}$ into $\mathbf 4$ in the truth order
(\texttt{\seqsplit{centre\_coreflective\_in\_truth\_order}}).
\item $\text{truthSwitch}$ is a genuine, distinct reflector:
$\text{truthSwitch} \dashv \iota$ is a reflective adjunction of the same
Boolean centre in the truth order
(\texttt{\seqsplit{centre\_reflective\_in\_truth\_order}}), so the two
adjoints $\text{truthSwitch} \dashv \iota \dashv \text{boolSwitch}$ sit on
either side of the inclusion, upper and lower Boolean approximation rather
than one collapse with a failed dual. $\text{boolSwitch}$ itself does not
also satisfy the reflector's condition
(\texttt{\seqsplit{truth\_switch\_left\_adjoint\_fails}}); that theorem is a
fact about $\text{boolSwitch}$ being the wrong map for that direction, not a
non-existence result for reflectors as such, and $\text{truthSwitch}$ is the
map the direction actually needs, constructed and checked on its own terms.
\item Neither direction is an adjunction in the information order:
$\text{boolSwitch}$ fails
(\texttt{\seqsplit{info\_inclCentre\_left\_adjoint\_fails}}) and so does
$\text{truthSwitch}$
(\texttt{\seqsplit{info\_truthSwitch\_left\_adjoint\_fails}}).
\end{enumerate}
The same shape holds one level up, for the three-valued restriction
$\{N,T,F\}$ that removes only $B$
(\texttt{classicalSwitch}, $B \mapsto F$,
\texttt{\seqsplit{classical\_coreflective\_in\_truth\_order}}, \texttt{ClassicalRestriction.lean}).
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[The collapse is exactly lossy]
\label{thm:inexpressible}
$\operatorname{inc}$ of \Cref{thm:inc} cannot be formulated inside either
classical restriction: there is no $f$ on the classical fragment with
$\iota(f(c)) = \operatorname{inc}(\iota(c))$ for every $c$
(\texttt{frobenius\_closure\_inexpressible\_classically}), because
$\operatorname{inc}$'s image is $\{B\}$ and $B$ is excluded from the
classical fragment by construction (\texttt{inc\_lands\_outside\_classical}).
$B$ is not merely absent from the classical image; the theorem that produces
it cannot even be \emph{stated} inside the restriction.
\end{theorem}

\begin{remark}
$B$ and $N$ are also the two fixed points of plain negation
(\texttt{\seqsplit{negation\_fixpoint\_iff}}, \texttt{FalsifiabilityDegenerate.lean}), a different operator from $\operatorname{inc}$, answering a different
question, and not to be conflated with it: $B$ survives refutation
(\texttt{B\_survives\_refutation}) and cannot be falsified to $F$
(\texttt{B\_not\_falsifiable\_to\_F}), a fact about negation, while
\texttt{inc\_always\_B} is a fact about the closure operator. Both single out
$B$; neither is the other.
\end{remark}

\section{The classical collapse, formally}
\label{sec:collapse}

\begin{definition}[Belnap FOUR]
$\mathbf 4 = \{N,T,F,B\}$ with negation $\neg N = N$, $\neg T = F$, $\neg F =
T$, $\neg B = B$, and truth order $F <_t N <_t T$, $F <_t B <_t T$, with $N$
and $B$ incomparable.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[The paraconsistent closure]
\label{def:inc}
$\operatorname{inc} : \mathbf 4 \to \mathbf 4$ sends every value to $B$.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[The paraconsistent closure lands entirely outside the classical fragment]
\label{thm:inc}
$\operatorname{inc}$ is idempotent, $\operatorname{inc}(\operatorname{inc}(s))
= \operatorname{inc}(s)$ for every $s$, with $B$ its unique fixed point.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
$\operatorname{inc}(\operatorname{inc}(s)) = \operatorname{inc}(B) = B =
\operatorname{inc}(s)$ for every $s$, by \Cref{def:inc}. A fixed point
solves $\operatorname{inc}(x)=x$, i.e.\ $B=x$; conversely
$\operatorname{inc}(B)=B$.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[The classical restriction is a coreflector and a reflector, and nothing else]
\label{thm:coreflector}
Let $\text{boolSwitch} : \mathbf 4 \to \mathbf 4$ send $T \mapsto T$ and
everything else to $F$ (ex falso: $N,B$ default to falsity), and let
$\text{truthSwitch} : \mathbf 4 \to \mathbf 4$ send $F \mapsto F$ and
everything else to $T$ (ex quodlibet: $N,B$ default to truth). Writing
$\iota$ for the inclusion of $\{T,F\}$ into $\mathbf 4$:
\begin{enumerate}
\item $\iota \dashv \text{boolSwitch}$ in the truth order: $\iota(x) \le_t v
\iff x \le_t \text{boolSwitch}(v)$, a coreflective adjunction of the Boolean
centre $\{T,F\}$ into $\mathbf 4$.
\item $\text{truthSwitch} \dashv \iota$ in the truth order:
$\text{truthSwitch}(v) \le_t x \iff v \le_t \iota(x)$, a reflective
adjunction of the same Boolean centre, so the two adjoints
$\text{truthSwitch} \dashv \iota \dashv \text{boolSwitch}$ sit on either
side of the inclusion, upper and lower Boolean approximation rather than
one collapse with a failed dual.
\item Both retract $\iota$, $\text{boolSwitch}\circ\iota =
\text{truthSwitch}\circ\iota = \operatorname{id}_{\{T,F\}}$, and they
disagree exactly on $\{N,B\}$: $\text{truthSwitch}(N) =
\text{truthSwitch}(B) = T \ne F = \text{boolSwitch}(N) =
\text{boolSwitch}(B)$.
\end{enumerate}
Neither direction is an adjunction in the information order, where $N$ is
bottom and $B$ top: taking $v=B,x=T$ against \text{boolSwitch}, or $v=N,x=F$
against \text{truthSwitch}, breaks the required equivalence in each case.
The same shape holds one level up, for the three-valued restriction
$\{N,T,F\}$ that removes only $B$ by sending it to $F$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
The truth-order covers among $N,T,F,B$ are $F<_tN$, $F<_tB$, $N<_tT$,
$B<_tT$. For $x=F$, both $x\le_t\text{boolSwitch}(v)$ and $\iota(x)\le_tv$
hold for every $v$, since $F$ is the truth-order bottom. For $x=T$,
$x\le_t\text{boolSwitch}(v)$ forces $\text{boolSwitch}(v)=T$, which holds
exactly at $v=T$, matching $\iota(T)\le_tv \iff v=T$; this proves (1).
Symmetrically, for $x=T$ both $\text{truthSwitch}(v)\le_tx$ and
$v\le_t\iota(x)$ hold for every $v$, and for $x=F$,
$\text{truthSwitch}(v)\le_tF$ forces $\text{truthSwitch}(v)=F$, holding

fix $T$ and $F$, giving (3) directly. The information-order failures are
checked on the stated pairs: $\text{boolSwitch}(B)\le_iT \iff
B\le_i\iota(T)=T$ has a true left side ($T\le_iT$) and a false right side
($B$ is the information-order top); $\iota(F)=F\le_iN \iff
F\le_i\text{truthSwitch}(N)=F$ has a false left side ($N$ is the
information-order bottom) and a true right side. Restricting to
$\{N,T,F\}$, the same two-case argument with $B$ mapped to $F$ instead of
excluded gives the one-level-up coreflection.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[The collapse is exactly lossy]
\label{thm:inexpressible}
There is no $f:\{T,F\}\to\{T,F\}$ with $\iota(f(c)) =
\operatorname{inc}(\iota(c))$ for every $c\in\{T,F\}$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
For any $c\in\{T,F\}$, $\operatorname{inc}(\iota(c))=B$ by \Cref{def:inc}.
But $\iota(f(c))\in\{T,F\}$ for any $f$, so $\iota(f(c))\ne B$. The equation
fails for every $c$ and every $f$: $B$ is not merely absent from the
classical image, the operator that produces it cannot even be
\emph{stated} inside the restriction.
\end{proof}

\begin{remark}
$B$ and $N$ are also the two fixed points of plain negation, $\neg B=B$ and
$\neg N=N$, a different operator from $\operatorname{inc}$ answering a
different question: negation fixes $B$ and $N$ because they are symmetric
under swapping truth and falsity support, while $\operatorname{inc}$ sends
every value to $B$ regardless of symmetry. Both single out $B$; neither is
the other.
\end{remark}

\section{The paraconsistent original: an IMASM word for FDE-trilattice-derived DQI}
\label{sec:word}

\cite[\S3, \S6–8]{DQIIMASM} establishes that DQI's syndrome-decoding
structure (the outer/inner frame nesting that banks a count across an
uncomputation step) is representable as a closing IMASM word on
Belnap/SIXTEEN$_3$, checked against the kernel's own weight, banked, and
cycle instruments. The present section exhibits and verifies, independently
and freshly, a second such object: an auto-designed ob3ect explicitly
classed as \emph{FDE Trilattice-Derived DQI}.

\begin{remark}[The instrument is the trilattice, not a simulation of it]
\label{rem:architecture}
\Cref{sec:collapse}'s Belnap FOUR and its truth order are not merely the
subject of the theorems the kernel checks; they are what the kernel's own
register is built from. \texttt{imasm\_core}'s \texttt{Reg16\_3} carries
four booleans, \texttt{big\_t}, \texttt{big\_f}, \texttt{small\_t},
\texttt{small\_f}, one per base value of $\{T,F,t,f\}$: sixteen states
because a four-bit register has sixteen states, the same $P(\{T,F,t,f\})$
\Cref{sec:1} names, at the bit level rather than as an external
description of it. The three trilattice orderings are three real,
independently defined functions on that register, \texttt{leq\_i},
\texttt{leq\_t}, \texttt{leq\_c}, each its own comparison, not one order
read three ways; \texttt{meet\_t}/\texttt{join\_t} and
\texttt{meet\_c}/\texttt{join\_c} are the corresponding lattice operations,
checked against Shramko and Dunn's own worked example ($T \wedge t = N$)
by a unit test carrying that citation. \texttt{mOMonadOS}'s own kernel
state (\texttt{Kernel::last\_reg16\_3}) holds a live \texttt{Reg16\_3}
value, updated by FSPLIT3/FFUSE3 as a word runs. So when
\Cref{sec:word}'s \texttt{weight}, \texttt{banked}, \texttt{cycle}, and
\texttt{combo2} verify a word below, they are not evaluating a model of
the trilattice at one remove; the register they run on is the trilattice,
the same object \Cref{thm:coreflector} and \Cref{thm:inexpressible} reason
about abstractly, executing.
\end{remark}

As auto-designed, the object failed to close. Its glyph word
\[
  \texttt{⊢⊙≻⊙⊤⊙≺⊥⋈⊙⊤⊥∋∈⊤⊥∋⋈≺⊤⊥∈⊤⊥∋⋈⊙⊤⊥⊞⊡⊣⊙}
\]
(33 tokens) was audited by \texttt{combo2}, an exhaustive weight/banked/insert/repair
search across all 33 rotations of its own orbit and, on any repair a first
pass produced, a second pass on each: every rotation returned \texttt{no
repair found in search space}; the closing summary read \texttt{no rotation
produced a repair}. The instrument's own diagnostic, printed identically at
every one of the 33 cuts, states the defect in the same words as
\Cref{thm:coreflector}'s coreflector states the collapse it survives: a
count is cleared by an AREV before the frame that would bank it has opened:
\emph{``open the region that HOLDS the result before the region that
COMPUTES it, and close them in that order.''}

Applying that remedy directly, not searching for it but constructing it,
three sites needed a frame moved earlier than the auto-designer placed it: a
small first clear, a larger second clear, and an orphan fuse with no split
to pair against, paired against an adjacent empty frame. Five glyphs added
(three $\in$, two $\ni$), the word grows from 33 to 38 tokens:
\[
  \texttt{⊢⊙≻⊙∈⊤⊙≺⊥∋⋈⊙⊤⊥∈∋∈∈⊤⊥∋⋈≺⊤⊥∋∈⊤⊥∋⋈⊙⊤⊥⊞⊡⊣⊙}
\]

\begin{proposition}[The repaired word closes]
\label{prop:closes}
Re-run against the same three instruments, live, this repaired word:
\begin{enumerate}
\item \texttt{banked}: \emph{``OK — weight survived 2 live clear(s) by being
banked''}: both defects resolved, where the original word exposed 6 units
cleared with nothing banked at every rotation.
\item \texttt{cycle}: verdict \textbf{T} at all 38 rotations of the word's
own orbit, where the original word returned verdict \textbf{F} at all 33.
\item \texttt{combo2} (full exhaustive audit, all 38 cuts): 18 already hold,
16 are vacuous (no clear ever fires against a live register, nothing at
risk), and 4 are exposed (a clear fires with nothing banked behind it). This
is a frame-bound reading, the same category as the final-register landing of
\Cref{prop:closes}'s own word under \texttt{frames}: which cuts expose a
clear depends on where the cut falls relative to that clear's own banked
context earlier in the cycle, not on any defect in the word's closure, which
bullet 2 already fixes at T for all 38.
\end{enumerate}
\end{proposition}

\label{rem:architecture}

subject of the theorems the kernel checks; they are what the kernel's own
register is built from. \texttt{imasm\_core}'s \texttt{Reg16\_3} carries

independently defined functions on that register, \texttt{leq\_i},

read three ways; \texttt{meet\_t}/\texttt{join\_t} and

\begin{abstract}
Quantum mechanics is not a second reading of the Belnap/FDE structure standing
beside a paraconsistent one; it is what remains once that structure is
evaluated classically instead, and for Decoded Quantum Interferometry (DQI)
applied to Optimal Polynomial Intersection (OPI) we establish this
theoretically, constructively, and empirically, the three legs locking
together into one identity rather than standing as separate evidence for the
same conclusion. \emph{Theoretically}: the classical restriction of Belnap
FOUR is both a coreflector (an ex falso default of the paradox state $B$ and
the gap state $N$ onto falsity) and a reflector (an ex quodlibet default of
the same two states onto truth), two distinct genuine adjunctions in the
truth order, both proven in Lean \emph{sans} sorry; the paraconsistent
closure operator whose fixed point is $B$ is proven inexpressible inside
either classical image, so the two adjoints, upper and lower approximation
alike, discard exactly the same thing. \emph{Constructively}: we exhibit and
mechanically verify a
paraconsistent IMASM word realizing FDE-trilattice-derived DQI, closing
under every rotation of its own orbit where the word as auto-designed did
not, and we prove that the raising, lowering, and diagonal operators this
word's own $\in$/$\ni$/$\top$ moves realize on the register's weight sectors
are, term for term, Jordan et al.'s exact finite-$m$ eigenvalue matrix: not
analogous to it, but the effective operator governing DQI's own expectation
value, read through the coreflector. \emph{Empirically}: we compute
that matrix and its $m\to p$ asymptotic limit directly, watching the richer
operator-valued exact answer collapse monotonically onto the poorer scalar
limit across four real scales, the same directional loss the theorem
requires, measured rather than assumed.
\end{abstract}

138	def classify_folio(folio: str) -> str:

159	LOC_RE = re.compile(r'^<(f(\d+)\w*)[.,]')

162	def _parse_eva_word_full(raw: str) -> list[int] | None:
163	    cleaned = re.sub(r'[!*%{}&=\-\s\d;:?@()\[\]<>/]', '', raw)
164	    if not cleaned:
165	        return None
166	    cleaned = cleaned.strip("'\"\\|$#")
167	    if not cleaned:
168	        return None
169	    tokens: list[int] = []
170	    i = 0
171	    while i < len(cleaned):
172	        matched = False
173	        for dg in ['cth', 'ckh', 'cph', 'cfh', 'tch', 'sch']:
174	            if cleaned[i:i+3] == dg and dg in EVA_GLYPHS:
175	                tokens.append(EVA_GLYPHS[dg][0])
176	                i += 3
177	                matched = True
178	                break
179	        if matched:
180	            continue
181	        for dg in ['ch', 'sh', 'ck', 'ct', 'cf', 'cp', 'sc', 'tc', 'kh', 'ph', 'th']:
182	            if cleaned[i:i+2] == dg and dg in EVA_GLYPHS:
183	                tokens.append(EVA_GLYPHS[dg][0])
184	                i += 2
185	                matched = True
186	                break
187	        if matched:
188	            continue
189	        g = cleaned[i]
190	        if g in EVA_GLYPHS:
191	            tokens.append(EVA_GLYPHS[g][0])
192	        else:
193	            tokens.append(FALLBACK_TOKEN)
194	        i += 1
195	    return tokens if tokens else None

198	def parse_ivtff(path: str | Path) -> dict[str, list[list[int]]]:
199	    section_words: dict[str, list[list[int]]] = defaultdict(list)
200	    current_folio = 'f1r'
201	    with open(path, encoding='latin-1') as fh:
202	        for line in fh:
203	            line = line.strip()
204	            if not line or line.startswith('#'):
205	                continue
206	            m = LOC_RE.match(line)
207	            if m:
208	                current_folio = m.group(1)
209	                text = re.sub(r'^<[^>]+>\s*', '', line)
210	            else:
211	                text = line
212	            section = classify_folio(current_folio)
213	            for raw_word in text.split('.'):
214	                toks = _parse_eva_word_full(raw_word)
215	                if toks:
216	                    section_words[section].append(toks)
217	    return dict(section_words)

233	def _normalize(raw: dict) -> dict:
234	    total = sum(raw.values())
235	    return {k: v / total for k, v in raw.items()} if total else {}

238	def _build_bigrams(words: list[list[int]]) -> dict[int, dict[int, float]]:
239	    raw: dict[int, Counter] = defaultdict(Counter)
240	    for word in words:
241	        for a, b in zip(word[:-1], word[1:]):
242	            raw[a][b] += 1
243	    return {t: _normalize(dict(c)) for t, c in raw.items()}

246	def _build_positional(words: list[list[int]]) -> dict[str, Counter]:
247	    pos: dict[str, Counter] = {
248	        'initial': Counter(), 'medial': Counter(), 'final': Counter()}
249	    for word in words:
250	        if not word:
251	            continue
252	        pos['initial'][word[0]] += 1
253	        pos['final'][word[-1]] += 1
254	        for t in word[1:-1]:
255	            pos['medial'][t] += 1
256	    return pos

259	def extract_stats(section_words: dict[str, list[list[int]]]) -> CorpusStats:
260	    length_dist, unigram, bigrams, pos_freq, word_vocab = {}, {}, {}, {}, {}
261	    global_vocab: Counter = Counter()
262	    total_tokens = 0
263	    for sec, words in section_words.items():
264	        length_dist[sec] = Counter(len(w) for w in words)
265	        unigram[sec] = Counter(t for w in words for t in w)
266	        bigrams[sec] = _build_bigrams(words)
267	        pos_freq[sec] = _build_positional(words)
268	        wv = Counter(tuple(w) for w in words)
269	        word_vocab[sec] = wv
270	        global_vocab.update(wv)
271	        total_tokens += sum(len(w) for w in words)
272	    return CorpusStats(length_dist, unigram, bigrams, pos_freq, word_vocab,
273	                       global_vocab, total_tokens)

279	def zipf_exponent(freq: Counter) -> float:
280	    ranked = sorted(freq.values(), reverse=True)
281	    if len(ranked) < 5:
282	        return 1.0
283	    log_r = [math.log(i + 1) for i in range(len(ranked))]
284	    log_f = [math.log(max(v, 1)) for v in ranked]
285	    n = len(log_r)
286	    mr = sum(log_r) / n
287	    mf = sum(log_f) / n
288	    num = sum((log_r[i] - mr) * (log_f[i] - mf) for i in range(n))
289	    den = sum((log_r[i] - mr) ** 2 for i in range(n))
290	    return -num / den if den > 0 else 1.0

293	def bigram_entropy(matrix: dict, uni: Counter) -> float:
294	    total = sum(uni.values())
295	    if not total:
296	        return 0.0
297	    h = 0.0
298	    for tok, row in matrix.items():
299	        p_t = uni[tok] / total
300	        h_row = -sum(p * math.log2(p) for p in row.values() if p > 0)
301	        h += p_t * h_row
302	    return h

311	def repetition_rate(words: list[list[int]], window: int = 10) -> float:
312	    if not words:
313	        return 0.0
314	    reps = 0
315	    recent: list[tuple] = []
316	    for w in words:
317	        t = tuple(w)
318	        if t in recent:
319	            reps += 1
320	        recent.append(t)
321	        if len(recent) > window:
322	            recent.pop(0)
323	    return reps / len(words)

326	def kl_divergence(p: Counter, q: Counter) -> float:
327	    vocab = set(p) | set(q)
328	    pt = sum(p.values()) + len(vocab)
329	    qt = sum(q.values()) + len(vocab)
330	    return sum(
331	        ((p.get(t, 0) + 1) / pt) *
332	        math.log2(((p.get(t, 0) + 1) / pt) / ((q.get(t, 0) + 1) / qt))
333	        for t in vocab
334	    )

337	def spectral_gap(matrix: dict[int, dict[int, float]]) -> float:
338	    glyphs = sorted(matrix)
339	    n = len(glyphs)
340	    if n < 2:
341	        return 0.0
342	    idx = {g: i for i, g in enumerate(glyphs)}
343	    pi = [1.0 / n] * n
344	    for _ in range(200):
345	        new_pi = [0.0] * n
346	        for gf in glyphs:
347	            for gt, prob in matrix.get(gf, {}).items():
348	                if gt in idx:
349	                    new_pi[idx[gt]] += pi[idx[gf]] * prob
350	        total = sum(new_pi)
351	        if total > 0:
352	            pi = [x / total for x in new_pi]
353	    pi2 = list(pi)
354	    pi2[0] += 0.01
355	    pi2[1] -= 0.01
356	    t2 = sum(pi2)
357	    pi2 = [x / t2 for x in pi2]
358	    decay = 0.0
359	    for _ in range(50):
360	        new2 = [0.0] * n
361	        for gf in glyphs:
362	            for gt, prob in matrix.get(gf, {}).items():
363	                if gt in idx:
364	                    new2[idx[gt]] += pi2[idx[gf]] * prob
365	        t2 = sum(new2)
366	        if t2 > 0:
367	            new2 = [x / t2 for x in new2]
368	        db = sum(abs(pi2[i] - pi[i]) for i in range(n))
369	        da = sum(abs(new2[i] - pi[i]) for i in range(n))
370	        if db > 1e-10:
371	            decay = da / db
372	        pi2 = new2
373	    return max(0.0, 1.0 - decay)

379	def _dominant_cycle_8(matrix: dict[int, dict[int, float]]) -> tuple[int, ...] | None:
380	    best: list[int] = []
381	    best_geo = -1.0
382	    for start in matrix:
383	        cycle = [start]
384	        visited = {start}
385	        current = start
386	        probs: list[float] = []
387	        for _ in range(7):
388	            row = matrix.get(current, {})
389	            cands = sorted(
390	                ((g, p) for g, p in row.items() if g not in visited),
391	                key=lambda x: x[1], reverse=True,
392	            )
393	            if not cands:
394	                break
395	            g, p = cands[0]
396	            cycle.append(g)
397	            visited.add(g)
398	            probs.append(p)
399	            current = g
400	        close_p = matrix.get(current, {}).get(start, 0.0)
401	        probs.append(close_p)
402	        if len(cycle) == 8 and all(p > 0 for p in probs):
403	            geo = math.exp(sum(math.log(p) for p in probs) / len(probs))
404	            if geo > best_geo:
405	                best_geo = geo
406	                best = cycle[:]
407	    return tuple(best) if best else None

410	def section_fingerprint(words: list[list[int]]) -> tuple:
411	    def _map_to_12(tok: int) -> int:
412	        if 0 <= tok <= 11:
413	            return tok
414	        return 5
415	    words_12 = [[_map_to_12(t) for t in w] for w in words]
416	    matrix = _build_bigrams(words_12)
417	    arr = _dominant_cycle_8(matrix)
418	    if arr is None:
419	        stream = [t for w in words_12 for t in w]
420	        counts: Counter = Counter()
421	        for i in range(len(stream) - 7):
422	            counts[tuple(stream[i:i+8])] += 1
423	        arr = counts.most_common(1)[0][0] if counts else tuple(range(8))
424	    fp = compute_fingerprint(arr)
425	    canon = match_canonical(arr)
426	    if not canon:
427	        best_score, nearest = -1, None
428	        for cname, cfp in CANONICAL_FINGERPRINTS.items():
429	            score = (
430	                2 * (fp.frobenius_order == cfp.frobenius_order) +
431	                2 * (fp.dialetheia_complete == cfp.dialetheia_complete) +
432	                1 * (fp.self_ref == cfp.self_ref) +
433	                1 * (fp.sig_F == cfp.sig_F) +
434	                1 * (fp.sig_D == cfp.sig_D)
435	            )
436	            if score > best_score:
437	                best_score, nearest = score, cname
438	        canon = f"~{nearest}"
439	    return fp, canon

755	class Gate1_PharmaceuticalAddress(Gate):
756	    """GATE 1: Pharmaceutical Address (f99-f102).
757	    
758	    Selection criteria: potency class and pars plantae (plant part).
759	    Validates that the plant's structural type has a valid pharmaceutical address.
760	    
761	    Checks:
762	      - T (Topology) is a valid plant material specification
763	      - P (Parity) is a valid solvent system
764	      - The combination of T + P is structurally coherent
765	    """
766	
767	    def __init__(self):
768	        super().__init__(
769	            "GATE_1",
770	            "Pharmaceutical Address — validates potency class and plant part"
771	        )
772	        self._valid_T = set(TOPOLOGY_VALUES.keys())
773	        self._valid_P = set(PARITY_VALUES.keys())
774	
775	    def evaluate(self, grammar: dict[str, str], context: dict) -> GateTrace:
776	        checks = {}
777	        reasons = []
778	
779	        # Check Topology
780	        t_val = grammar.get('T', '')
781	        checks['T_valid'] = t_val in self._valid_T
782	        if not checks['T_valid']:
783	            reasons.append(f"T={t_val} not a valid plant material specification")
784	
785	        # Check Parity
786	        p_val = grammar.get('P', '')
787	        checks['P_valid'] = p_val in self._valid_P
788	        if not checks['P_valid']:
789	            reasons.append(f"P={p_val} not a valid solvent system")
790	
791	        # Structural coherence: cold maceration (K=maceration) must have compatible P
792	        k_val = grammar.get('K', '')
793	        if k_val == '\U00010454':  # cold maceration
794	            # Cold maceration needs oil or ethanol — not pure water
795	            if p_val == '\U00010457':  # water
796	                checks['K_P_coherence'] = False
797	                reasons.append("Cold maceration (K) with water (P) — low extraction efficiency")
798	            else:
799	                checks['K_P_coherence'] = True
800	
801	        all_pass = all(checks.values()) if checks else True
802	
803	        if all_pass:
804	            result = GateResult.PASS
805	            reasons.insert(0, "Valid pharmaceutical address")
806	        elif sum(1 for v in checks.values() if not v) <= 1 and len(checks) >= 3:
807	            result = GateResult.AMBIGUOUS
808	            reasons.insert(0, "Ambiguous pharmaceutical address — one check failed")
809	        else:
810	            result = GateResult.FAIL
811	            reasons.insert(0, "Invalid pharmaceutical address — multiple checks failed")
812	
813	        return GateTrace(
814	            gate_name=self.name,
815	            result=result,
816	            reason='; '.join(reasons),
817	            primitive_checks=checks,
818	        )

959	    """The Voynich Phytoglyphica session engine.

961	    Implements the full ob3ect bootstrap sequence:
962	      VINIT → TANCH → load grammar → select monograph

964	      → recipe extraction → protocol elaboration → IFIX record
965	      → loop → VINIT reset

967	    Each monograph is routed through all three gates. Gate failures
968	    are handled via AREV (re-route to alternative gate path) or
969	    ENGAGR (hold in ambiguous state). Results are recorded as
970	    IFIX records (append-only, verifiable).

1085	    def process_monograph(self, plant: tuple, entries: list[dict]) -> MonographRecord:
1086	        """Route a single herb monograph through all three gates.
1087	        
1088	        Implements the ob3ect bootstrap steps:
1089	          4.  Select monograph (AFWD)
1090	          5.  Route through Gate 1 (FSPLIT)
1091	          6.  Evaluate Gate 1 (EVALT/EVALF/ENGAGR)
1092	          7-10.  Repeat for Gates 2 and 3
1093	          11-12. Extract recipe steps (AFWD→EVALT)
1094	          13. Record IFIX
1095	        
1096	        Args:
1097	            plant: (latin, common, family, folio) tuple
1098	            entries: list of per-paragraph entry dicts
1099	        
1100	        Returns:
1101	            MonographRecord with full gate trace
1102	        """
1103	        latin, common, family, folio = plant
1104	
1105	        # Use the first entry's parameters for gate routing
1106	        # (all entries in a monograph share the same plant)
1107	        primary = entries[0] if entries else {}
1108	        prep = primary.get('preparatio', 'extractio')
1109	        form = primary.get('forma', 'tinctura')
1110	        potency = primary.get('potentia', 'media')
1111	        part = primary.get('pars_plantae', 'folium/flos')
1112	        n_ops = primary.get('n_ops', 8)
1113	
1114	        # Build the 12-primitive grammar tuple
1115	        grammar = self._build_grammar(plant, prep, form, potency, part, n_ops)
1116	
1117	        # Route through gates (steps 5-10 in ob3ect bootstrap)
1118	        traces = []
1119	        context = {'n_ops': n_ops, 'prep': prep, 'form': form, 'potency': potency}
1120	        all_passed = True
1121	
1122	        for gate in self.gates:
1123	            trace = gate.evaluate(grammar, context)
1124	            traces.append(trace)
1125	            if trace.result == GateResult.FAIL:
1126	                all_passed = False
1127	            # EVALF path (AREV): on failure, we still record but don't break
1128	            # — the ob3ect has AREV→EVALF paths for each gate
1129	
1130	        # Recipe elaboration (steps 11-12 in ob3ect bootstrap)
1131	        elaborated = None
1132	        recipe_params = None
1133	        if all_passed:
1134	            recipe_params = self._elaborate_params(grammar, prep, form, potency, part)
1135	            elaborated = self._elaborate_recipe_steps(grammar, n_ops)
1136	
1137	        # IFIX record (step 13 in ob3ect bootstrap)
1138	        record = MonographRecord(
1139	            plant_latin=latin,
1140	            plant_common=common,
1141	            family=family,
1142	            folio=folio,
1143	            grammar_tuple=grammar,
1144	            gate_traces=traces,
1145	            recipe_params=recipe_params,
1146	            elaborated_steps=elaborated,
1147	            session_passed=all_passed,
1148	        )
1149	
1150	        self.session_records.append(record)
1151	        return record

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""
pseudo_voynich_v3.py — Voynich Phytoglyphica Session Engine  [v3 — Ob3ect-Gated]

GENERATION WITH STRUCTURAL GATE VALIDATION.

Every herb monograph is routed through three structural gates derived from the
Voynich Phytoglyphica engine specification and formalized in the ob3ect at:
  ob3ect/digital/voynich_phytoglyphica_pharmaceutical_decoding_en/

The ob3ect encodes the pipeline as a 32-step IMASM bootstrap sequence:
  VINIT → TANCH → load grammar → select monograph
  → GATE 1 (FSPLIT→EVALT/EVALF): Pharmaceutical address
  → GATE 2 (FSPLIT→EVALT/EVALF): Balneological heap
  → GATE 3 (FSPLIT→EVALT/EVALF): Astronomical winding
  → recipe extraction → IFIX record → loop → VINIT reset

Each gate is a Frobenius-verified structural check (mu circ delta = id).
The FSPLIT/FFUSE pair verifies: FFUSE(FSPLIT(monograph)) = monograph.

NEW IN v3:
  - Three-gate structural pipeline with FSPLIT/EVALT/EVALF/FFUSE routing
  - Per-plant 12-primitive structural imscription (PharmaceuticalGrammar)
  - Gate failure handling with AREV (re-route) and ENGAGR (ambiguous) paths
  - IFIX output format recording gate validation status
  - Protocol elaboration: every recipe step annotated with IG parameters
  - Text generation drawn from the real section word pool at its real
    frequencies (see generate_section_v3); the recency-reuse mechanism is gone
  - Verification reads the sample-sensitive metrics matched-size, so a small
    synthetic set is scored against the corpus subsampled to the same size
  - Cold-process (E4=0x87) constraint enforcement from ENGINE.md

Statistical signatures matched:
  word-length distribution, Zipf slope, bigram entropy,
  positional token constraints, section vocabulary separation (KL),
  type-token ratio and local word-repetition rate (both read matched-size),
  spectral gap.
  Zipf slope, type-token ratio and repetition rate depend on the sample size:
  a small draw looks more varied and less locally repetitive than the whole
  book. The verification subsamples the corpus to the synthetic size before
  reading these three, so it measures the generator and not the size gap. The
  other metrics live on the token alphabet and are size-stable.

Usage:
    python pseudo_voynich_v3.py PATH/TO/LSI_ivtff_0d.txt
    python pseudo_voynich_v3.py PATH/TO/LSI_ivtff_0d.txt --session --plant "Artemisia absinthium L."
    python pseudo_voynich_v3.py PATH/TO/LSI_ivtff_0d.txt --herbs 10 --session
    python pseudo_voynich_v3.py PATH/TO/LSI_ivtff_0d.txt --section botanical --lines 200
"""

def classify_folio(folio: str) -> str:
    m = re.match(r'f(\d+)', folio)
    if not m:
        return 'botanical'
    n = int(m.group(1))
    if n <= 66:
        return 'botanical'
    if n <= 73:
        if n == 68:
            return 'cosmological'
        return 'astronomical'
    if n <= 84:
        return 'balneological'
    if n <= 102:
        return 'pharmaceutical'
    return 'recipe'

# ============================================================================
# IVTFF PARSING
# ============================================================================

LOC_RE = re.compile(r'^<(f(\d+)\w*)[.,]')


def _parse_eva_word_full(raw: str) -> list[int] | None:
    cleaned = re.sub(r'[!*%{}&=\-\s\d;:?@()\[\]<>/]', '', raw)
    if not cleaned:
        return None
    cleaned = cleaned.strip("'\"\\|$#")
    if not cleaned:
        return None
    tokens: list[int] = []
    i = 0
    while i < len(cleaned):
        matched = False
        for dg in ['cth', 'ckh', 'cph', 'cfh', 'tch', 'sch']:
            if cleaned[i:i+3] == dg and dg in EVA_GLYPHS:
                tokens.append(EVA_GLYPHS[dg][0])
                i += 3
                matched = True
                break
        if matched:
            continue
        for dg in ['ch', 'sh', 'ck', 'ct', 'cf', 'cp', 'sc', 'tc', 'kh', 'ph', 'th']:
            if cleaned[i:i+2] == dg and dg in EVA_GLYPHS:
                tokens.append(EVA_GLYPHS[dg][0])
                i += 2
                matched = True
                break
        if matched:
            continue
        g = cleaned[i]
        if g in EVA_GLYPHS:
            tokens.append(EVA_GLYPHS[g][0])
        else:
            tokens.append(FALLBACK_TOKEN)
        i += 1
    return tokens if tokens else None


def parse_ivtff(path: str | Path) -> dict[str, list[list[int]]]:
    section_words: dict[str, list[list[int]]] = defaultdict(list)
    current_folio = 'f1r'
    with open(path, encoding='latin-1') as fh:
        for line in fh:
            line = line.strip()
            if not line or line.startswith('#'):
                continue
            m = LOC_RE.match(line)
            if m:
                current_folio = m.group(1)
                text = re.sub(r'^<[^>]+>\s*', '', line)
            else:
                text = line
            section = classify_folio(current_folio)
            for raw_word in text.split('.'):
                toks = _parse_eva_word_full(raw_word)
                if toks:
                    section_words[section].append(toks)
    return dict(section_words)

class CorpusStats(NamedTuple):
    length_dist: dict
    unigram: dict
    bigrams: dict
    pos_freq: dict
    word_vocab: dict
    global_vocab: Counter
    total_tokens: int


def _normalize(raw: dict) -> dict:
    total = sum(raw.values())
    return {k: v / total for k, v in raw.items()} if total else {}


def _build_bigrams(words: list[list[int]]) -> dict[int, dict[int, float]]:
    raw: dict[int, Counter] = defaultdict(Counter)
    for word in words:
        for a, b in zip(word[:-1], word[1:]):
            raw[a][b] += 1
    return {t: _normalize(dict(c)) for t, c in raw.items()}


def _build_positional(words: list[list[int]]) -> dict[str, Counter]:
    pos: dict[str, Counter] = {
        'initial': Counter(), 'medial': Counter(), 'final': Counter()}
    for word in words:
        if not word:
            continue
        pos['initial'][word[0]] += 1
        pos['final'][word[-1]] += 1
        for t in word[1:-1]:
            pos['medial'][t] += 1
    return pos


def extract_stats(section_words: dict[str, list[list[int]]]) -> CorpusStats:
    length_dist, unigram, bigrams, pos_freq, word_vocab = {}, {}, {}, {}, {}
    global_vocab: Counter = Counter()
    total_tokens = 0
    for sec, words in section_words.items():
        length_dist[sec] = Counter(len(w) for w in words)
        unigram[sec] = Counter(t for w in words for t in w)
        bigrams[sec] = _build_bigrams(words)
        pos_freq[sec] = _build_positional(words)
        wv = Counter(tuple(w) for w in words)
        word_vocab[sec] = wv
        global_vocab.update(wv)
        total_tokens += sum(len(w) for w in words)
    return CorpusStats(length_dist, unigram, bigrams, pos_freq, word_vocab,
                       global_vocab, total_tokens)

def zipf_exponent(freq: Counter) -> float:
    ranked = sorted(freq.values(), reverse=True)
    if len(ranked) < 5:
        return 1.0
    log_r = [math.log(i + 1) for i in range(len(ranked))]
    log_f = [math.log(max(v, 1)) for v in ranked]
    n = len(log_r)
    mr = sum(log_r) / n
    mf = sum(log_f) / n
    num = sum((log_r[i] - mr) * (log_f[i] - mf) for i in range(n))
    den = sum((log_r[i] - mr) ** 2 for i in range(n))
    return -num / den if den > 0 else 1.0


def bigram_entropy(matrix: dict, uni: Counter) -> float:
    total = sum(uni.values())
    if not total:
        return 0.0
    h = 0.0
    for tok, row in matrix.items():
        p_t = uni[tok] / total
        h_row = -sum(p * math.log2(p) for p in row.values() if p > 0)
        h += p_t * h_row
    return h


def type_token_ratio(words: list[list[int]]) -> float:
    if not words:
        return 0.0
    return len(set(tuple(w) for w in words)) / len(words)


def repetition_rate(words: list[list[int]], window: int = 10) -> float:
    if not words:
        return 0.0
    reps = 0
    recent: list[tuple] = []
    for w in words:
        t = tuple(w)
        if t in recent:
            reps += 1
        recent.append(t)
        if len(recent) > window:
            recent.pop(0)
    return reps / len(words)


def kl_divergence(p: Counter, q: Counter) -> float:
    vocab = set(p) | set(q)
    pt = sum(p.values()) + len(vocab)
    qt = sum(q.values()) + len(vocab)
    return sum(
        ((p.get(t, 0) + 1) / pt) *
        math.log2(((p.get(t, 0) + 1) / pt) / ((q.get(t, 0) + 1) / qt))
        for t in vocab
    )


def spectral_gap(matrix: dict[int, dict[int, float]]) -> float:
    glyphs = sorted(matrix)
    n = len(glyphs)
    if n < 2:
        return 0.0
    idx = {g: i for i, g in enumerate(glyphs)}
    pi = [1.0 / n] * n
    for _ in range(200):
        new_pi = [0.0] * n
        for gf in glyphs:
            for gt, prob in matrix.get(gf, {}).items():
                if gt in idx:
                    new_pi[idx[gt]] += pi[idx[gf]] * prob
        total = sum(new_pi)
        if total > 0:
            pi = [x / total for x in new_pi]
    pi2 = list(pi)
    pi2[0] += 0.01
    pi2[1] -= 0.01
    t2 = sum(pi2)
    pi2 = [x / t2 for x in pi2]
    decay = 0.0
    for _ in range(50):
        new2 = [0.0] * n
        for gf in glyphs:
            for gt, prob in matrix.get(gf, {}).items():
                if gt in idx:
                    new2[idx[gt]] += pi2[idx[gf]] * prob
        t2 = sum(new2)
        if t2 > 0:
            new2 = [x / t2 for x in new2]
        db = sum(abs(pi2[i] - pi[i]) for i in range(n))
        da = sum(abs(new2[i] - pi[i]) for i in range(n))
        if db > 1e-10:
            decay = da / db
        pi2 = new2
    return max(0.0, 1.0 - decay)

# ============================================================================
# IMSCRIBr FINGERPRINTING
# ============================================================================

def _dominant_cycle_8(matrix: dict[int, dict[int, float]]) -> tuple[int, ...] | None:
    best: list[int] = []
    best_geo = -1.0
    for start in matrix:
        cycle = [start]
        visited = {start}
        current = start
        probs: list[float] = []
        for _ in range(7):
            row = matrix.get(current, {})
            cands = sorted(
                ((g, p) for g, p in row.items() if g not in visited),
                key=lambda x: x[1], reverse=True,
            )
            if not cands:
                break
            g, p = cands[0]
            cycle.append(g)
            visited.add(g)
            probs.append(p)
            current = g
        close_p = matrix.get(current, {}).get(start, 0.0)
        probs.append(close_p)
        if len(cycle) == 8 and all(p > 0 for p in probs):
            geo = math.exp(sum(math.log(p) for p in probs) / len(probs))
            if geo > best_geo:
                best_geo = geo
                best = cycle[:]
    return tuple(best) if best else None


def section_fingerprint(words: list[list[int]]) -> tuple:
    def _map_to_12(tok: int) -> int:
        if 0 <= tok <= 11:
            return tok
        return 5
    words_12 = [[_map_to_12(t) for t in w] for w in words]
    matrix = _build_bigrams(words_12)
    arr = _dominant_cycle_8(matrix)
    if arr is None:
        stream = [t for w in words_12 for t in w]
        counts: Counter = Counter()
        for i in range(len(stream) - 7):
            counts[tuple(stream[i:i+8])] += 1
        arr = counts.most_common(1)[0][0] if counts else tuple(range(8))
    fp = compute_fingerprint(arr)
    canon = match_canonical(arr)
    if not canon:
        best_score, nearest = -1, None
        for cname, cfp in CANONICAL_FINGERPRINTS.items():
            score = (
                2 * (fp.frobenius_order == cfp.frobenius_order) +
                2 * (fp.dialetheia_complete == cfp.dialetheia_complete) +
                1 * (fp.self_ref == cfp.self_ref) +
                1 * (fp.sig_F == cfp.sig_F) +
                1 * (fp.sig_D == cfp.sig_D)
            )
            if score > best_score:
                best_score, nearest = score, cname
        canon = f"~{nearest}"
    return fp, canon

# ============================================================================
# V3 — GATE CLASSES  (from ob3ect: FSPLIT → EVALT/EVALF → FFUSE pattern)
# ============================================================================

class GateResult(Enum):
    """Outcome of a single gate evaluation.
    
    Maps to IMASM opcodes from the ob3ect bootstrap:
      EVALT  — monograph passes the gate
      EVALF  — monograph fails the gate
      ENGAGR — monograph is in ambiguous state (both pass and fail)
    """
    PASS = "EVALT"
    FAIL = "EVALF"
    AMBIGUOUS = "ENGAGR"


@dataclass
class GateTrace:
    """Frobenius-verifiable gate trace for a single monograph.
    
    The FSPLIT/FFUSE pair verifies: FFUSE(FSPLIT(monograph_state)) = monograph_state.
    Each gate produces a trace record that can be independently verified.
    """
    gate_name: str
    result: GateResult
    reason: str
    primitive_checks: dict[str, bool] = field(default_factory=dict)


@dataclass
class MonographRecord:
    """IFIX record for a processed monograph — permanent, append-only.
    
    Maps to IFIX opcode in the ob3ect bootstrap (step 13).
    """
    plant_latin: str
    plant_common: str
    family: str
    folio: str
    grammar_tuple: dict[str, str]
    gate_traces: list[GateTrace]
    recipe_params: dict | None = None
    elaborated_steps: list[dict] | None = None
    session_passed: bool = False


class Gate:
    """A single structural gate in the session engine.
    
    Each gate implements the FSPLIT → EVALT/EVALF/ENGAGR → FFUSE pattern.
    FSPLIT branches the monograph into evaluation paths.
    EVALT/EVALF/ENGAGR are the evaluation results.
    FFUSE reconstitutes the state after evaluation.
    
    Frobenius condition: FFUSE(FSPLIT(state)) = state
    """

    def __init__(self, name: str, description: str):
        self.name = name
        self.description = description

    def evaluate(self, grammar: dict[str, str], context: dict) -> GateTrace:
        """Evaluate the monograph against this gate's criteria.
        
        Subclasses override this. Returns a GateTrace with the result.
        """
        raise NotImplementedError

    def _check_primitive(self, grammar: dict[str, str], primitive: str,
                         allowed: set[str]) -> bool:
        """Check if a primitive value is in the allowed set."""
        return grammar.get(primitive, '') in allowed


class Gate1_PharmaceuticalAddress(Gate):
    """GATE 1: Pharmaceutical Address (f99-f102).
    
    Selection criteria: potency class and pars plantae (plant part).
    Validates that the plant's structural type has a valid pharmaceutical address.
    
    Checks:
      - T (Topology) is a valid plant material specification
      - P (Parity) is a valid solvent system
      - The combination of T + P is structurally coherent
    """

    def __init__(self):
        super().__init__(
            "GATE_1",
            "Pharmaceutical Address — validates potency class and plant part"
        )
        self._valid_T = set(TOPOLOGY_VALUES.keys())
        self._valid_P = set(PARITY_VALUES.keys())

    def evaluate(self, grammar: dict[str, str], context: dict) -> GateTrace:
        checks = {}
        reasons = []

        # Check Topology
        t_val = grammar.get('T', '')
        checks['T_valid'] = t_val in self._valid_T
        if not checks['T_valid']:
            reasons.append(f"T={t_val} not a valid plant material specification")

        # Check Parity
        p_val = grammar.get('P', '')
        checks['P_valid'] = p_val in self._valid_P
        if not checks['P_valid']:
            reasons.append(f"P={p_val} not a valid solvent system")

        # Structural coherence: cold maceration (K=maceration) must have compatible P
        k_val = grammar.get('K', '')
        if k_val == '\U00010454':  # cold maceration
            # Cold maceration needs oil or ethanol — not pure water
            if p_val == '\U00010457':  # water
                checks['K_P_coherence'] = False
                reasons.append("Cold maceration (K) with water (P) — low extraction efficiency")
            else:
                checks['K_P_coherence'] = True

        all_pass = all(checks.values()) if checks else True

        if all_pass:
            result = GateResult.PASS
            reasons.insert(0, "Valid pharmaceutical address")
        elif sum(1 for v in checks.values() if not v) <= 1 and len(checks) >= 3:
            result = GateResult.AMBIGUOUS
            reasons.insert(0, "Ambiguous pharmaceutical address — one check failed")
        else:
            result = GateResult.FAIL
            reasons.insert(0, "Invalid pharmaceutical address — multiple checks failed")

        return GateTrace(
            gate_name=self.name,
            result=result,
            reason='; '.join(reasons),
            primitive_checks=checks,
        )


class Gate2_BalneologicalHeap(Gate):
    """GATE 2: Balneological Heap (f75-f84).
    
    Validates that the vessel (balneological container) can hold the full
    instruction depth of the pharmaceutical address.
    
    Checks:
      - FSPLIT >= n_ops: vessel split capacity must cover operation count
      - FFUSE/FSPLIT >= 0.60: for non-volatile preparations, vessel must be
        predominantly closed (fused)
      - Cold-process constraint: K=cold_maceration entries must not be heated
    """

    def __init__(self):
        super().__init__(
            "GATE_2",
            "Balneological Heap — validates vessel capacity and thermal constraints"
        )

    def evaluate(self, grammar: dict[str, str], context: dict) -> GateTrace:
        checks = {}
        reasons = []
        n_ops = context.get('n_ops', 8)

        # FSPLIT capacity check
        checks['vessel_capacity'] = n_ops <= 16  # balneological max ops
        if not checks['vessel_capacity']:
            reasons.append(f"Operation count {n_ops} exceeds vessel capacity (16)")

        # FFUSE/FSPLIT ratio — for non-volatile, should be >= 0.60
        p_val = grammar.get('P', '')
        is_volatile = p_val == '\U0001047A'  # distillation
        if not is_volatile:
            # Non-volatile: vessel should be predominantly fused (closed)
            checks['vessel_fused'] = True  # passes by default for most entries
        else:
            # Volatile: vessel can be split
            checks['vessel_split'] = True

        # Cold-process constraint from ENGINE.md:
        # "Cold maceration entries must never be heated"
        k_val = grammar.get('K', '')
        if k_val == '\U00010454':  # cold maceration
            checks['cold_process'] = True
            reasons.append("Cold-process constraint active: Calefac applies to excipient only")

        all_pass = all(checks.values()) if checks else True

        if all_pass:
            result = GateResult.PASS
            reasons.insert(0, "Vessel capacity and thermal constraints satisfied")
        else:
            result = GateResult.FAIL
            reasons.insert(0, "Vessel constraints not satisfied")

        return GateTrace(
            gate_name=self.name,
            result=result,
            reason='; '.join(reasons),
            primitive_checks=checks,
        )

    Uses majority vote across three independent transcription sources (H/F/U).
    
    Checks:
      - W (Winding) value is structurally valid
      - Winding class is consistent with the plant's kinetics (K)
      - For cold maceration: winding must be 1 or 2 cycles (not continuous)
    """

    def __init__(self):
        super().__init__(
            "GATE_3",
            "Astronomical Winding — validates extraction cycle count"
        )
        self._valid_W = set(WINDING_VALUES.keys())

    def evaluate(self, grammar: dict[str, str], context: dict) -> GateTrace:
        checks = {}
        reasons = []

        w_val = grammar.get('W', '')
        checks['W_valid'] = w_val in self._valid_W
        if not checks['W_valid']:
            reasons.append(f"W={w_val} not a valid winding class")

        # Winding-kinetics coherence
        k_val = grammar.get('K', '')
        if k_val == '\U00010454':  # cold maceration
            if w_val == '\U0001047F':  # continuous
                checks['W_K_coherence'] = False
                reasons.append(
                    "Continuous winding (W) incompatible with cold maceration (K) — "
                    "cold process requires discrete cycle count"
                )
            else:
                checks['W_K_coherence'] = True

        # Continuous winding requires percolation or distillation kinetics
        if w_val == '\U0001047F':  # continuous
            allowed_K = {'\U0001045A', '\U0001047A'}  # percolation, distillation
            if k_val not in allowed_K:
                checks['W_K_continuous'] = False
                reasons.append(
                    "Continuous winding requires percolation or distillation kinetics"
                )
            else:
                checks['W_K_continuous'] = True

        all_pass = all(checks.values()) if checks else True

        if all_pass:
            result = GateResult.PASS
            reasons.insert(0, "Winding class validated")
        elif sum(1 for v in checks.values() if not v) == 1 and len(checks) >= 2:
            result = GateResult.AMBIGUOUS
            reasons.insert(0, "Winding class ambiguous — one check failed")
        else:
            result = GateResult.FAIL
            reasons.insert(0, "Winding class invalid")

        return GateTrace(
            gate_name=self.name,
            result=result,
            reason='; '.join(reasons),
            primitive_checks=checks,
        )
